author: johnny4young
body:
UX-audit P1 batch — macOS **clarity & safety**. Low-risk, all verified in code.

## What changed
- **Plainer snippet wording.** "Promote to Library" → **"Save as snippet"**, "Remove from Library" → **"Move to history"** (now consistent with the ⌘S entry in the panel cheat-sheet). The demote action also drops its misleading destructive-red trash icon — it doesn't delete anything.
- **"New board…" from a clip no longer creates a board named "Board".** The per-clip *Add to board → New board…* path now prompts for a name and files the clip into the board it creates, via a new `createBoard(named:assigning:)` overload.
- **No-results is actionable.** When a type or board filter is narrowing the list, the panel's empty state offers a **"Clear filters"** button — replacing a hint that wrongly told you to "press esc to clear the search" (esc hides the panel).
- **Board deletion asks first.** Deleting a board (panel rail + Library sidebar) now shows a confirmation dialog; the message reassures that clips stay in history and only the board is removed.

## Why
These are the highest-ROI, lowest-risk P1 items from the usability audit: remove jargon, fix a real "named-Board" bug, give the no-results state a real way out, and put a guard on a destructive action.

## Verification
- `make build` (macOS, Debug) — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no new warnings.
- `make lint --strict` — clean.
- `swift test` localization gate green; 6 new en+es strings added to `Localizable.xcstrings` (board terminology kept as "tablero" for consistency).

## Deliberately left out
- The `dev-actions-run` counter in the Privacy Center — it sits in the "Pasteboard access" transparency section and may be intentional, so hiding it behind `#if DEBUG` is the owner's call, not a safe code-read change.

Audit P0 (Pro-path: paywall sells un-shipped iCloud sync + license dead-end) still waits on the `GANCHO_LICENSE_SIGNING_KEY`.

author: grayson039
body:
## Summary

Full security and functionality audit of the SceneOne site across all 4 HTML files, Supabase edge functions, and SQL migrations. 21 issues found and fixed across 3 critical, 6 high, 4 medium, and 1 low categories.

## Changes

### Critical
- **admin.html** — Sanitize `imdb_url` before inserting into `href`; reject any non-`http(s)` scheme to block `javascript:` XSS (C1)
- **landing.html** — Remove duplicate `requestScriptAccess` stub at line 5136 that silently overrode the real auth-checking implementation, causing access requests to never be sent or checked (C2)
- **supabase/migrations/010_fix_profile_rls.sql** — Drop the overly broad cross-user profile `SELECT` policy whose condition (`id = auth.uid() OR auth.uid() IS NOT NULL`) simplified to allowing any authenticated user to read all columns (`plan`, `stripe_customer_id`, `plan_renews_at`) on any profile row (C3)

### High
- **landing.html** — Fix `goTo('signin')` → `goTo('welcome')` + `switchAuthTab('login')` — `screen-signin` does not exist, leaving users stuck on sign-up error (H1)
- **landing.html** — Escape `error.message` with `esc()` before inserting into `innerHTML` in the login error path (H2)
- **landing.html** — `reanalyze()` now shows an honest "Coming soon" message instead of a fake 1.8s animation that implied a real re-analysis occurred (H3)
- **landing.html** — `updateOverallScore()` now reads live scores from `.scat-score` DOM elements instead of a hardcoded `[82, 71, 91, 68, 80]` array unrelated to the user's actual report (H4)
- **landing.html** — Escape `data.message` via `esc()` in `_showLimitReached` before injecting into `innerHTML` (H6)

### Medium
- **landing.html** — Celebration overlay (`#ob-celebrate`) now populates overall score, best category name+value, and lowest category name+value from live `_reportData` instead of hardcoded 79/91/68 placeholders (M6)
- **landing.html** — Standardize legal contact email to `sceneone.net` across privacy policy and content policy sections (M7)
- **supabase/functions/grade-script/index.ts** — Return 401 for unauthenticated non-sample analyses; previously anonymous users could bypass plan limits by sending `is_sample: false` (M3)
- **admin.html** — Remove admin email address from the login form `placeholder` attribute (M5)

### Low
- **landing.html** — Escape `name`, `company`, and `email` through `esc()` in `approveRequest` `innerHTML` to close a latent XSS sink when wired to real data (L5)

## Issues noted but not changed (require larger architectural work)

- **H5** — Admin gate is client-side email comparison only. Proper fix requires a server-side `is_admin` column + RLS or edge function enforcement.
- **M1/M2** — `approveRequest`, `declineRequest`, and `submitReaderRequest` are UI-only stubs with no Supabase persistence. These are incomplete features, not regressions.
- **L1** — Footer legal links in `index.html` point to `#`. Needs real content pages before fixing.
- **L2** — Keep-warm ping uses GET on a POST-only endpoint. Harmless in practice.

author: xananasx7
body:
## Summary

Pins all GitHub Actions to full immutable commit SHAs instead of mutable version tags.

## Vulnerability

Mutable tags (`@v1`, `@v3`, `@v4`, etc.) can be silently updated — a compromised action repository could deliver malicious code into CI with access to secrets and write permissions. This is the same attack class as the [tj-actions/changed-files supply chain incident (March 2025)](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/popular-github-action-tjactionschanged-files-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack/).

## Change

All `uses: action@vX` references replaced with `uses: action@<full-sha> # vX`. No behaviour change — pins point to the exact same code as the current tags.

## References
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions
- https://securitylab.github.com/research/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/

## Actions pinned (88 pins across 5 workflows)
`actions/cache@v4`, `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/download-artifact@v4`, `actions/setup-go@v5`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, `docker/build-push-action@v6`, `docker/login-action@v3`, `docker/metadata-action@v4`, `docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`, `golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9`, `google-github-actions/auth@v2`

author: brandon-reinhart
body:
## What

Exposes `VisualStateManager::GoToState` so Rust can drive control visual state
transitions (the `CommonStates` / `CheckStates` / `FocusStates` groups a
`ControlTemplate` declares) from code, instead of only through XAML triggers.
This is the `VisualStateManager::GoToState` item from TODO §6.

## Surface added

C ABI (`cpp/noesis_shim.h`, implemented in new `cpp/noesis_visual_state.cpp`):

```c
bool dm_noesis_visual_state_go_to_state(
    void* element, const char* state, bool use_transitions);
```

Safe Rust (`src/view.rs`):

```rust
pub fn go_to_state(&self, state: &str, use_transitions: bool) -> bool
```

## SDK entry point

The SDK declares `static bool VisualStateManager::GoToState(FrameworkElement*
control, Symbol stateName, bool useTransitions)`. We DynamicCast the handle to
`FrameworkElement*` and call it. Although the SDK doc comment talks about a
"control", the parameter type is `FrameworkElement*`, and GoToState only finds
state groups on a templated control's `ControlTemplate` — so a non-templated
element or an unknown state name both fall out as `false` naturally, no extra
type gating needed. We expose `GoToState` (control template states, the common
case) rather than `GoToElementState` (app-defined groups on an arbitrary root),
which can be added separately if a need shows up.

The implementation never calls `VerifyAccess()` and never throws across the ABI,
matching the `text_*` / `dependency_object_*` accessors.

## Tests

`tests/visual_state.rs` follows the `tests/dependency_property.rs` conventions
(in-memory `XamlProvider`, init/shutdown, runtime SDK gate via license env).
The scene declares an inline `ControlTemplate` with a `CommonStates`
`VisualStateGroup` (`Normal` / `MouseOver` / `Pressed` / `Disabled`) so the
valid-state assertions hold regardless of whether a default theme dictionary is
present. It asserts: valid states return `true` (with and without transitions);
an unknown state returns `false`; a `TextBlock` and the root `Grid` (non-control)
return `false`.

## TODO.md

Elided the GoToState item from §6, rewrote §2 to list only remaining bullets,
added a terse GoToState mention to the "Already exposed" summary, and updated the
closing prioritization note.

author: codetalcott
body:
## Summary

Clears the **lone remaining parse hard-fail** (`tr window-resize`), taking the priority corpus to **3696/3696 (100%)** — zero failing patterns across all 24 languages.

(Supersedes #509, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch `fix/multilingual-sov-primary-role-r1` was deleted on merge of #508. This branch is now rebased directly onto `main`.)

## Root cause (grounded, not assumed)

The i18n tr dict emitted `boyut_değiştir` for the `resize` event. The tr semantic tokenizer splits on `_` → `boyut` + `değiştir`, and `değiştir` normalizes to **`toggle`** (homonym collision) — destroying the resize event so the handler parsed **NULL**.

Grounding via `ml.parse` on the actual gate translation **corrected the documented framing**: the handoff claimed the fronted untranslated `debounced at 200ms` modifier was "the separate, harder half" also needed. It isn't — the parser tolerates the fronted modifier; the underscore-split toggle homonym was the **sole** blocker.

## Fix (low-risk, single-token route)

Mirrors the documented ru/uk `install` single-token precedent and the working `kaydır`/`kaydırma` scroll pattern:
- **i18n tr dict**: `resize: 'boyut_değiştir'` → `'boyutlandırma'`
- **semantic event map**: `boyutlandırma`/`boyutlandır` → `resize` (replaces the dead underscore key)

`window-resize` tr now parses faithfully: `action=on, event=resize, body=call` — structurally identical to the en reference.

## Result

- Parse rate **3695/3696 → 3696/3696 (100%)**; tr `parseFailure` 1 → 0; **zero failing patterns** in all 24 priority languages.
- R0 recall 1.000, precision 0.971, avgRoleFidelity 0.872 (from #508), execution 1.000, degenerate 0, lossy 0 — all unchanged.
- `--regression` gate green; baseline regenerated; 6218 semantic + 880 i18n tests pass.
- Guards (verified failing without the fix): `grammar.test.ts` + `multilingual-roadmap-fixes.test.ts` → "tr resize single-token event keyword".

`patterns.db` not committed (CI repopulates), per repo convention.

author: masra91
body:
## Summary
Restores **multi-file third-party plugin loading**, broken in production since **v0.40.0** by #1499 (HIGH severity, hitting a live client).

`#1499` removed the dev-only guard in `dynamic-import.ts` and routed **all** `file://` plugin imports through IPC + a **blob URL**. A `blob:` URL has **no path component**, so any relative or bare import inside a plugin's entry module (e.g. `import './util.js'`) resolved against `blob:file:///<uuid>` → nothing → `Failed to load module: Cannot find module`. Single-file plugins kept working; any plugin with >1 module broke.

## Root cause
`src/renderer/plugins/dynamic-import.ts` blob-wrapped every `file:` URL regardless of origin. Production (renderer on `file://`) is same-origin with the plugin files, so it can — and pre-#1499 did — import them directly with their real path, which is what lets relative/bare imports resolve.

> Note: the pre-#1499 production path was `import(url)` with the `?v=` cache-buster **still attached** — that was #1499's *Bug 2* (Chromium's ESM loader rejects query params on `file://`). So the old guard could not simply be restored verbatim; the fix strips `?v=` **and** imports directly.

## Fix (Part A — production direct `file://` import)
- `dynamic-import.ts`: keep the **dev** (`http:` origin) blob path — it dodges Chromium's cross-origin block on `file://` imports — but in **production** (`file:` origin) strip the `?v=` query and `import()` the `file://` URL **directly**, preserving the real path so relative/bare imports resolve.
- The #1499 `./`-manifest normalization in `plugin-loader.ts` is **kept** (not reverted).
- Added a tiny `_internals.rawImport` seam so the direct-import path is unit-testable (asserts the exact specifier — proving `?v=` stripping).
- Extracted the production CSP to `buildProductionCsp()` and locked `script-src 'self'` (required for same-origin `file://` plugin import) + `blob:` with tests.

### CSP verification
Production CSP is `script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' blob:`; the renderer loads from `file://` and the `protocol.handle('file', …)` handler (#1431) serves the modules, so the same-origin direct import is permitted. CSP does **not** block it. Locked by `buildProductionCsp` tests.

## Part B (custom same-origin protocol) — fast-follow, **not in this PR**
The durable fix (serve modules via a custom privileged scheme so relative imports + cache-busting work in dev *and* prod) requires registering a privileged scheme, a main-process handler, CSP changes, and a plugin-loader URL change — non-trivial and only meaningfully verifiable via Electron E2E. Per the brief's guidance, **Part A ships now to un-break the client; Part B will be a separate PR.** Trade-off: with `?v=` stripped, in-session production hot-reload may return the ESM-cached module (dev is unaffected — blob is always fresh). Pre-#1499 production couldn't load multi-file plugins at all, so this is strictly better; Part B restores prod cache-busting.

## New / updated regression tests
`src/renderer/plugins/dynamic-import.test.ts`:
- **multi-file plugin with relative import — production** imports the `file://` URL directly, no IPC, no blob (the exact case #1499's tests missed)
- **bare/external dependency import** in entry module — direct import
- **`?v=` stripping** in production (asserts the exact cleaned specifier)
- **single-file plugin** — production
- **dev blob path** still imports the generated blob URL (via the seam) and revokes it
- rewrote the prod-mode tests that previously asserted the #1499 (blob) behavior

`src/main/csp-nonce.test.ts`:
- `buildProductionCsp` keeps `script-src 'self'` (plugin import not blocked) + `blob:`, and embeds the nonce

`plugin-loader.test.ts` `./` + nested `./lib/index.js` normalization tests remain green (file untouched).

## Validation
- `npm test` — **12,430 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures** (490 files)
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `eslint .` — 0 errors (2 pre-existing `any` warnings in the test file, not introduced here)

## Review
No self-merge — requesting **QA** + **design-lead** approval per the mission brief.

## Known limitations (tracked → Part B)
- **Production hot-reload cache:** with `?v=` stripped, re-importing the same `file://` module within a session returns the ESM-cached copy, so in-session hot-reload of a community plugin won't pick up on-disk changes in **production**. Dev is unaffected (blob URLs are always unique). Production multi-file plugins were fully broken before this PR, so this is strictly better; the durable fix (unique same-origin URLs via a custom protocol) lands in **Part B** (separate fast-follow PR).

author: jomcgi
body:
## What

Reworks fc-agentd guest egress (ADR 023 stage 6a) from the planned `HTTP_PROXY` forward-proxy into a **transparent data plane**. The guest is configured with real URLs and needs no per-destination routing config; goose (whose reqwest [ignores `HTTP_PROXY`](https://github.com/block/goose/issues/6835)) works unchanged.

## How

- **fc-agent-init** becomes a dumb funnel: a wildcard DNS responder answers every name with `127.0.0.1`, and per-port loopback listeners (`80/443/8080`) tunnel each connection over vsock to the host sidecar. Drops `HTTP_PROXY` and the old forward-proxy/redirect listeners.
- **egress-proxy** is rewritten as a transparent proxy: it reads the funnel's port preamble, recovers the destination host by **peeking the TLS SNI or HTTP Host header** (without consuming the stream), applies policy, and pipes to the real upstream (the pod resolves cluster + public DNS).
- **`EGRESS_POLICY`**: `allow` (default, open egress in/out of cluster) or `allowlist` (fail closed). The per-secret `egressTo` (6b) remains the exfiltration control, not a global firewall.
- **chart**: replaces the egress channel/allowlist/default-upstream values with `policy` + `harnessEnv` (real URLs), injected as `FC_AGENTD_INJECT_*`.
- Unit tests for the hand-rolled SNI, Host, and DNS parsers.

## Design notes

- The whole transparent model exists because goose ignores `HTTP_PROXY` (confirmed: the fix shipped in goose v1.24.0 but is incomplete; we run v1.27.1 and it still connects directly) and the guest is vsock-only. Routing by SNI/Host in the sidecar means **no per-destination config** and real URLs everywhere.
- Connection capture is **per-port loopback listeners** today (covers the ports the harness uses). Generic any-port capture via `iptables` REDIRECT + `SO_ORIGINAL_DST` is a localized follow-up that needs the guest kernel built with netfilter; ~80% of this code is shared with that upgrade.
- ADR 023 architecture section updated to describe the transparent data plane and the `allow`-by-default posture.

## Validation

- `go test` green locally for the new parsers (SNI ClientHello, HTTP Host, DNS A/NODATA), including peek-non-consumption guarantees.
- `helm template` renders the egress env wiring correctly.
- In-cluster `goose -> Qwen` validation to follow once the chart deploys (chart-version-bot will bump on merge).

author: andy-emerson
body:
Acting on the external security review, the two items with real, in-scope value:

1. **scrypt instead of PBKDF2** — `_hash_password`/`_check_password` now use stdlib `hashlib.scrypt` (N=2¹⁴, r=8, p=1), **no new dependency**. The meaningful upgrade is CPU-hard → **memory-hard**: ~16 MB per guess denies an attacker who steals the hash the cheap GPU parallelism PBKDF2 allows. ~30 ms/check, Pi-friendly. Zero users, so no on-disk migration. design.md updated; hashing test section extended (133/133).

2. **SECURITY.md** — supported versions, private disclosure via GitHub's 'Report a vulnerability', and in/out-of-scope (out-of-scope points at design.md's non-goals).

We deliberately did **not** act on: the 'small trusted base vs. framework' note (that's the documented design thesis), the #4/#3 CodeQL dismissals (intentional/FP), the #6 'redact config' fix (a misread — the display never prints the hash/salt, only the non-secret trusted_proxy IP), and Dependabot/Ruff (limited fit; can revisit).

**Action needed:** enable *Settings → Security → Private vulnerability reporting* so the SECURITY.md link is live.

body:
## Summary

Two fixes from the same report:

### 1. ATC Boundaries (and other Settings toggles) didn't persist
Turning **ATC Boundaries** off worked for the current session but came back every time the site was reopened.

**Cause:** the Settings-sheet checkbox handler in `MobileSettingsUI.js` (the one that wires the ATC & Airports / Terrain / NAT toggles) updated `mapFilters` and re-rendered the map via `updateMapFilters()`, but **never called `saveFiltersToLocalStorage()`** — unlike the tactical-board handler, which does. So nothing was written to storage and every reload fell back to the default (`showAtcBoundaries: true`).

**Fix:** persist the change in that handler. This also fixes the same silent non-persistence for the sibling toggles (Classic Airport Tags, Show Unstaffed, Hide No-ATC Dots, Hide ATC Markers, Terrain Elevation Map, TAWS, NAT Tracks/Labels, etc.).

### 2. Redesigned the global toast notifications
The app-wide notifications behind `window.showGlobalNotification` used the **Toastify** library — flat green/red/grey rectangles pinned top-right with a close ✕ — which didn't match the rest of the UI.

**Fix:** replaced it with a polished, self-contained glass toast:
- top-center card, backdrop blur, rounded, soft shadow — matches the existing dashboard toast aesthetic
- a colored type icon (success / error / warn / info)
- slide-in / slide-out animation (respects `prefers-reduced-motion`), auto-dismiss, click-to-dismiss
- **public API unchanged** (`window.showGlobalNotification(message, type)`), so every existing caller — including the slow-connection monitor — is upgraded automatically
- message rendered via `textContent` (matches Toastify's old escaping behaviour)
- keeps a Toastify fallback if anything throws

The two stray "account has been deleted" Toastify calls (`profileUI.js`, `MobileDashboardUI.js`) now route through the new global toast as well.

## Notes / scope
- The already-polished `mdui-toast` (dashboard) and `pui-toast` (profile) systems were left as-is.
- The local `showToast` helpers inside the ATC/flight **replay** views are separate; happy to unify those into the new global toast too if you'd like one consistent system everywhere.

## Testing
- `node --check` passes on all changed files.
- Logic verified by tracing: the toggle handler now persists; the new toast keeps the same call signature and types used across the codebase.

author: alex-mextner
body:
## Why

After #80 (uv-based install hints) and #82 (bare `rig init` previews, never presumptuously applies), an interactive `rig init` on a machine without the optional `[tui]` extra still just PRINTED a "go install textual yourself" hint and degraded to a preview.

CTO directive (Telegram): *"Да какая подсказка, все само должно устанавливаться!"* — when interactive setup is genuinely wanted, rig should self-bootstrap its own optional UI dependency and just launch the wizard.

Closes #83.

## What

- `_tui_install_command()` — the runnable twin of `_tui_install_hint`: an argv matched to how rig itself is installed (uv-tool → `uv tool install --reinstall 'rig-cli[tui]'`; pipx → `pipx inject`; source/unknown → `uv pip install --python <sys.executable>`, or plain pip into the venv / `pip --user` on a base interpreter). Returns `None` when no installer is on PATH.
- `_auto_install_tui()` — runs it with a bounded, env-overridable timeout (`RIG_TUI_INSTALL_TIMEOUT`, default 180s), re-checks importability, returns `True` only when textual+rich are importable in-process afterward. Every failure mode (no installer, offline, permission, timeout, non-zero exit, installed-but-unimportable) returns `False` — never raises, never hangs.
- `cmd_setup` interactive branch: missing extra → auto-install then launch; a genuine failure degrades to the existing hint + #82 non-destructive preview (writes/applies NOTHING).
- Guards: no auto-install when there's no TTY, under `--yes` (headless), the new `--no-tui` flag, or `RIG_NO_TUI=1`. `_tui_importable()` is exception-safe so a broken partial install can't crash the front door.

## Scope / boundary

Only rig's OWN optional UI dependency self-installs. #82's gating of the catalog apply (no presumptuous `rig.yaml` write/apply without `--yes`) is untouched. `doctor` already self-installs deps; `config-web` keeps its structured hint (its deps are local editable agent-tools libs needing a resolved source path — not a clean/safe silent auto-install).

## Tests

Auto-install invoked then TUI launched; failure → graceful fallback to preview; no-TTY / `--no-tui` / `RIG_NO_TUI` → no install (headless preserved); textual present → launch directly; per-method command selection; every `_auto_install_tui` failure branch; env parsing for `RIG_NO_TUI` + the install timeout. Full suite: 1361 passed, 16 skipped. Version bumped 0.3.0 → 0.4.0.

No UI surface (a CLI behavior change) — no screenshot.

## Summary
Completes **SD-LEO-INFRA-S5-KILL-GATE-DEMAND-FEASIBILITY-001**'s missing half. `evaluateKillGate` now returns `decision='conditional_pass'` (route-to-review) for demand-unvalidated ventures, but the orchestrator was **executing that as a genuine KILL** — the `gateBlocked` boolean conflated HOLD with KILL, so the blocked branch archived the vision (stages 3/5) and returned BLOCKED for both.

## Fix
`eva-orchestrator.js` distinguishes route-to-review from a genuine kill via **`stageOutput.decision`** (the verdict is NOT carried by `validateStageGate` at S3/S5 — the 5→6 gate is FINANCIAL_VIABILITY with only `{passed}`; confirmed by a code-grounded Plan-agent investigation).

- **HOLD** (`conditional_pass` + no hard non-stage_gate/reality-gate block): do NOT archive the vision, mint a pending `chairman_decision` (`createOrReusePendingDecision` → `resolveDecisionHealth` guarantees non-null health), keep the vision intact, return the new **`STATUS.HELD`**.
- **genuine KILL**: archive + BLOCKED (unchanged).
- **mis-route guard**: a reality-gate / gate-error structural failure is never downgraded to HOLD.
- **dry-run** HOLD returns HELD with zero side effects.

`STATUS.HELD` added and tolerated by the run-loop and the stage-execution-worker (no-retry terminal set + a dedicated HELD branch that holds-blocked **without** governance auto-advance + `stage_status → blocked`).

author: adriantworek
body:
## What

- Add `.github/dependabot.yml` covering two ecosystems:
  - **`gomod`** — weekly, minor/patch updates grouped into a single PR, majors kept separate, `build(deps):` commit prefix
  - **`github-actions`** — weekly, all bumps grouped, `ci(deps):` commit prefix
- Pin all workflow actions to immutable commit SHAs (with `# vX.Y.Z` comments), keeping the same major versions:
  - `release-please-action` → `v4.4.1`
  - `actions/checkout` → `v4.3.1`
  - `actions/setup-go` → `v5.6.0`
  - `golangci-lint-action` → `v9.2.1`

## Why

- SHA-pinned actions are immutable, closing a supply-chain gap (mutable tags can be re-pointed). Relevant for an auth library.
- The `# vX.Y.Z` comments let Dependabot bump both the SHA and the comment automatically, so pinning stays maintenance-free.
- Commit prefixes are `build`/`ci`, which are non-releasing under the release-please config — dependency bumps won't each cut a release.

## Manual follow-up (not in this PR)

Enable **Dependabot alerts + security updates** in **Settings → Code security** for CVE-driven PRs.

author: oyi77
body:
💡 **What:** Added a mathematical length-based pre-check to the `similarity` function in `scripts/lint-skills.py` before executing the expensive `difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio()`.

🎯 **Why:** The script checks for near-duplicate skill names across 1300+ skills in a nested loop (O(N^2) comparisons). `SequenceMatcher` is slow. Because the max possible similarity ratio is `2.0 * min(len(a), len(b)) / (len(a) + len(b))`, we can immediately reject pairs that mathematically cannot meet the `0.99` threshold based purely on their string lengths, skipping the expensive calculation entirely.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces the execution time of `python3 scripts/lint-skills.py` from ~47.2 seconds down to ~3.4 seconds (a ~14x speedup) while returning exactly the same results. 

🔬 **Measurement:** Run `time python3 scripts/lint-skills.py` to observe the massive reduction in execution time and verify that the lint output is perfectly identical to before.

body:
## Summary

- **Free users** see anomalies on a **30-second delay** with Strike disabled — they can see the opportunity existed but can't act on it in time
- **Premium users** ($99/mo) get **real-time data** + 1-click Strike execution
- Stripe Checkout subscription flow with webhook-based activation/cancellation

## How the moat works

```
Anomaly detected at T=0
    ↓
Premium user sees it at T=0 → clicks Strike → captures edge
Free user sees it at T=30s → edge is gone → market already repriced
    ↓
Free user realizes they need premium to make money → upgrades
```

## Changes

**Backend:**
- `flash_scan` queries `live_anomalies` with 30s time offset for free users
- User status returns `tier` field (`free` / `premium`)  
- New `upgrade` action creates Stripe Checkout session ($99/mo subscription)
- Stripe webhook handles `checkout.session.completed` → sets `premium: true`
- Stripe webhook handles `customer.subscription.deleted` → sets `premium: false`

**Frontend:**
- `DELAYED` / `LIVE` badge on every anomaly card
- `30s DELAY` / `PREMIUM` tier badge in stream header
- Strike button replaced with upgrade CTA for free users
- Auto-execute disabled for free tier (cards fade with upgrade prompt on expiry)
- `upgradePrompt()` redirects to Stripe Checkout

## Test plan

- [ ] Free user sees anomalies with DELAYED badge and locked Strike button
- [ ] Free user clicks Strike → redirected to Stripe Checkout for $99/mo
- [ ] After payment, webhook fires → user document gets `premium: true`
- [ ] Premium user sees LIVE badge and functional Strike button
- [ ] Subscription cancellation via Stripe → `premium: false` in Firestore
- [ ] Tier badge in header updates correctly on page load

author: carloshrdezc
body:
Convert the 7 remaining Controller->Display NOTIFY/READ characteristics from comma-delimited text (and ArduinoJson for SystemInfo) to nanopb encode/decode, using the messages already defined in `lib/NimBLEComm/proto/comms.proto` (package `gaggimate`). Slice 3 of the Option-A migration (slices 1/2 merged).

## Converted (encode in NimBLEServerController, decode in NimBLEClientController notifyCallback)
- `ERROR_CHAR` (Error.code) — was std::to_string / atoi
- `BREW_BTN` (BrewButton.pressed) — was std::to_string / atoi
- `STEAM_BTN` (SteamButton.pressed) — was std::to_string / atoi
- `AUTOTUNE_RESULT` (AutotuneResult) — was lossy 3-dp float_to_string text
- `VOLUMETRIC_MEASUREMENT` — was lossy 3-dp float_to_string text
- `TOF_MEASUREMENT` (TofMeasurement) — was std::to_string / atoi

## Notes
**AutotuneResult**: the controller's public `sendAutotuneResult(Kp,Ki,Kd)` signature is UNCHANGED. The old text path appended a literal `,0.0` Kf token; nanopb now leaves the proto `kf` field at its default (0 = disabled). Decode still feeds the 4-arg autotune_result callback (Kf=0), so no callback typedef changes.

**SystemInfo** (INFO_UUID, READ): drop ArduinoJson for this characteristic. The controller now encodes `gaggimate_SystemInfo`+`Capabilities` in `make_system_info()` (`lib/GaggiMateController/src/utilities.h`) and the display decodes it in `Controller::setupInfos()`. Added `lib/NimBLEComm/proto/comms.options` to bound the SystemInfo string fields (hardware/version max_size:48) so nanopb generates plain char arrays (no callbacks) and `gaggimate_SystemInfo_size` is a constant. `initServer(String)`/`setInfo(String)`/`readInfo()` signatures are unchanged — the String/std::string now carries raw protobuf bytes (length-delimited setValue).

**Simulator**: `sim/comms` is UNTOUCHED. Its `NimBLEClientController::readInfo()` still serves the legacy JSON string and the display-sim build does not link the nanopb codegen, so `Controller::setupInfos()` keeps the JSON path under `#ifdef GAGGIMATE_SIM` and uses nanopb otherwise. `[env:display-sim]` still builds.

The other text characteristics and the 2 already on nanopb (slice 2) are unchanged — mixed wire-format state mid-migration is expected.

## Tests
`test/test_nanopb_comms/` gains host round-trip cases for all 7 messages, incl. bit-exact + old-text-was-lossy regression guards for AutotuneResult and VolumetricMeasurement, a full SystemInfo+Capabilities round trip, and an exhaustive 16-way capability-bool permutation. `pio test -e native` 102/102.

Fixes PRO-243

## Summary

Adds a merchant-controlled Store Canvas trigger builder.

### Trigger creation
- Adds a **+ Trigger** button in the upper-right corner of the Merchant Store Canvas.
- Clicking the button creates a transparent IN/OUT Box trigger square on the canvas.
- The trigger square can be dragged anywhere on the canvas.
- The trigger square can be resized from the lower-right handle.
- Trigger position, size, and selected campaign are persisted in local storage for the merchant browser session.

### Campaign assignment
- The trigger square loads the merchant's active campaigns from `/api/merchant-canvas/reward-options.php`.
- The merchant can choose which active campaign is assigned to the trigger.
- When a customer avatar crosses the trigger square, the selected campaign ID is passed to `api/merchant-canvas/campaign-trigger.php`.
- The backend validates that the selected campaign is active/available for the merchant before issuing the reward.
- If the selected campaign has an attached reward template, it prefers that template; otherwise it falls back to the first available template.

### Campaign firing
- Trigger still logs a Store Canvas campaign event.
- Trigger still sends a real Store Canvas message to the customer.
- If the selected campaign and reward template are valid, it attempts to issue that campaign reward.
- Trigger throttling now includes the selected campaign ID, so different assigned campaigns are tracked separately.

## Test plan

1. Open `/merchant-canvas.php` as a merchant.
2. Click **+ Trigger** in the upper-right of the canvas.
3. Confirm a transparent trigger square appears.
4. Drag the square to a new part of the canvas.
5. Resize it from the lower-right corner.
6. Select an active campaign from the dropdown.
7. Let a customer avatar cross the square.
8. Confirm the selected campaign fires a real message/event.
9. If the campaign/reward template is valid, confirm the reward is issued.

## Notes

This is a clean follow-up branch from the merged merchant motion work. It only changes the trigger endpoint and the Store Canvas motion CSS/JS.

# Vercel Web Analytics Integration for Hono Deno Benchmarks

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for the Hono Deno benchmark project located in `benchmarks/deno`. The implementation follows the latest official Vercel Analytics documentation fetched from https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart.

## What Was Implemented

### 1. Created Configuration Files
- **benchmarks/deno/deno.json**: Deno configuration file with import maps for `@vercel/analytics` via esm.sh CDN
  - Maps `@vercel/analytics` to `https://esm.sh/@vercel/analytics@1.1.1`
  - Configured compiler options for DOM libraries support

### 2. Created Analytics-Enabled Demo
- **benchmarks/deno/hono-with-analytics.ts**: New Hono server implementation featuring:
  - A homepage serving HTML with integrated Vercel Analytics
  - Module script importing and injecting analytics tracking
  - All original API endpoints from the benchmark
  - Uses Hono's `html` helper for template rendering
  - Demonstrates proper analytics integration in development mode

### 3. Added Documentation
- **benchmarks/deno/README.md**: Comprehensive documentation including:
  - Setup and configuration instructions
  - Usage examples for both HTML and module-based integration
  - Deployment guidelines for Vercel
  - Notes about analytics requiring browser-based traffic
  - Instructions for production deployment

### 4. Generated Lock File
- **benchmarks/deno/deno.lock**: Auto-generated dependency lock file ensuring consistent package versions

## Implementation Approach

Since this is a Deno project (not Node.js/npm), I adapted the installation approach:
1. Used Deno's import maps in `deno.json` instead of npm package installation
2. Leveraged esm.sh CDN for package delivery (standard Deno practice)
3. Created a new demo file rather than modifying existing benchmarks to preserve their purpose
4. Used the `inject()` function method as recommended for TypeScript/Deno projects

## Why These Choices?

1. **Preserved Original Benchmarks**: The existing benchmark files (`hono.ts`, `oak.ts`, etc.) are API-only servers for performance testing. Adding analytics to them wouldn't make sense as they don't serve HTML/browser content.

2. **Created Separate Demo**: `hono-with-analytics.ts` demonstrates the proper integration without affecting benchmark results.

3. **Used ESM CDN**: Deno projects typically use URL imports and esm.sh CDN rather than npm packages, making this the idiomatic approach.

4. **HTML Integration**: Analytics requires browser execution, so the demo includes an HTML page with the analytics script injected as a module.

## Testing Performed

- ✅ Verified Deno configuration is valid
- ✅ Checked analytics package is accessible via esm.sh
- ✅ Ran Deno lint on the new file (passed)
- ✅ Started server and verified HTML page renders with analytics script
- ✅ Confirmed all API endpoints are functional

## How to Use

### Development
```bash
cd benchmarks/deno
deno run --allow-net --sloppy-imports hono-with-analytics.ts
```
Visit http://localhost:8000 to see the analytics-enabled demo page.

### Production Deployment
1. Enable Web Analytics in Vercel project dashboard
2. Change mode from 'development' to 'production' in the analytics inject call
3. Deploy to Vercel
4. Analytics will start collecting real user data

## Files Changed

Created:
- `benchmarks/deno/deno.json` - Deno configuration with analytics import map
- `benchmarks/deno/hono-with-analytics.ts` - Demo server with analytics integration
- `benchmarks/deno/README.md` - Documentation for analytics setup
- `benchmarks/deno/deno.lock` - Dependency lock file

No existing files were modified, preserving the integrity of the benchmark suite.

author: tjones-gss
body:
## What

Adds the `npx @mission-control/app` install path — zero to a running cockpit in one command, no global installs.

The root package is repurposed as the publishable `@mission-control/app` (dropped `private`, added `bin` + `engines` + a lean `files` whitelist). The bin (`bin/start.mjs`):

1. **Node version gate** — hard-fails fast if Node < 22.13 (the server's `node:sqlite` read-cache requires it).
2. **Install if needed** — runs `npm run setup` only when a workspace is missing `node_modules` (setup is idempotent).
3. **Launch** — runs `npm run up` (server + client via the existing health-gated launcher).
4. **Open browser** — opens `http://localhost:5173` once `/api/health` responds (cross-platform: `open` / `cmd start` / `xdg-open`, with a printed-URL fallback for WSL).

It reuses the existing `waitForReady` poller from `scripts/wait-ready.js` and follows the `.mjs` convention already used by `installers/setup.mjs`, so the typeless root package needs no `"type": "module"` change.

## Why these design choices

- **Repurpose root, not a new sub-package.** `npx` ships and runs a single published tarball, so the package that `npx` downloads must *contain* the whole monorepo (server + client + installers). Only the root can do that — a `packages/*` sub-package can't reach up to `apps/`.
- **Renamed `mission-control` → `@mission-control/app`** and updated the server's vestigial self-referential `file:../../..` dep key to match. Nothing imports that package; `@mission-control/contracts` resolves independently via the root workspace, verified by the passing contract tests.
- **Lean publish.** A `files` whitelist with negations excludes `node_modules`, tests, e2e, fixtures, coverage, `client/dist`, and server runtime data (incl. the local `cockpit.db` cache). `npm pack --dry-run`: **221 files, 445 KB tarball** (down from 21k files / 94 MB before exclusions).

## How to test locally (no publish required)

From the repo root on this branch:

```bash
# 1. Direct run of the bin (what `npx` will execute):
node bin/start.mjs
#    → gates Node, installs if needed, starts server+client, opens the browser at :5173

# 2. Or simulate the real npx resolution end-to-end with a packed tarball:
npm pack                                   # produces mission-control-app-0.5.0.tgz
npx ./mission-control-app-0.5.0.tgz        # resolves the bin and runs it

# 3. Inspect what would publish (should be lean — no node_modules/tests/db):
npm pack --dry-run

# 4. Unit tests for the pure helpers:
cd apps/cockpit/server && npx vitest run tests/scripts/start-bin.test.js
```

## Verification done

- ✅ End-to-end smoke (PowerShell, real PATH): `node bin/start.mjs` → server `/api/health` 200, client `:5173` 200, **browser auto-opened** (Chrome requests to the API confirmed in logs).
- ✅ Full server suite green: **1389 tests / 101 files**, incl. the new `start-bin` tests and the contracts-dependent audit-log tests (rename didn't break resolution).
- ✅ `npm run lint` (Prettier) clean.
- ✅ `npm pack --dry-run` audited: 0 leaked test/fixture/node_modules/db files.

## Notes / out of scope

- CI and coverage thresholds untouched. The bin and `scripts/wait-ready.js` are root files outside the server coverage scope, so thresholds are unaffected.
- README still documents `npm run setup` / `npm run up`; adding an `npx` quickstart line there is a reasonable follow-up but left out to keep this surgical.

body:
## Phase 1d, Stage B.2 — full native project-detail read (behind a flag)

Wires the project detail page to a **100% native, reactive** read behind `NATIVE_PROJECT_DETAIL_ENABLED` (**default OFF**). Merging changes nothing for users. With the flag on (after the members backfill), the whole `getProject` composite comes from live Convex subscriptions reconstructed client-side — **no server action, reactive over the WebSocket**.

**This makes the backfill the literal last blocker:** with the flag on but no backfill, `requireOrgPermission` denies (no member row); with the backfill, the native page works.

### Changes
- **`src/lib/project-detail-reconstruct.ts`** (NEW, client-safe): `reconstructProjectDetail` combines `projectDetail.bundle` + `projectEquipment.browserBundle` into the exact `getProject` shape — project scalars (`mapProject`), managers + mirrored users, media + files, location + parent + address/coord inheritance, equipment tree, client. Pure mappers **copied** from `projects-read`/`locations-read`/`media-read` (which keep server-only co-residents); types via `import type` (erased). **Zero server imports.**
- **`use-native-project-equipment.ts`**: `useNativeProjectDetail` — two auth-gated subscriptions + reconstruct; returns the `{ data, isLoading }` shape `useProjectDetail` expects; skips unless the flag is on.

author: jhosm
body:
## In plain English

Running a big parallel-lane backlog session — the lifecycle-command-driver epic, where one orchestration carved 10 issues into 7 collision-free lanes — taught us a handful of concrete lessons about the `parallel-backlog-orchestrator` skill itself. In two spots the skill literally told you to do the wrong thing; in a couple more it left out a discipline the run proved we needed. This PR edits the skill doc so the next run starts from those learnings instead of re-discovering them.

## Summary

Edits to `plugins/babelstone-engine/skills/parallel-backlog-orchestrator/SKILL.md`:

**Near-bugs (the skill instructed something that misfires):**
1. **Branch-footprint diff: two-dot → three-dot.** The skill prescribed `git diff --name-only origin/main..<branch>` (two-dot), which inflates a branch that is *behind* main — it reports every file main changed since the fork as if the branch touched it. In this run that made stale comment-pass branches falsely appear to edit the ADR ledger. Now prescribes the three-dot `origin/main...<branch>` (the merge-base diff = what the branch authored), in all three places the command appears, with the two-dot inflation called out as a warning.
2. **`adr-conformance` in the Workflow path.** The Step-4 lane brief told every lane to run `babelstone-engine:adr-conformance` before pushing — but a Workflow `agent()` can't spawn a subagent. Now states the orchestrator runs it centrally post-run in the ultracode/Workflow path (lanes run it only in the default Agent-tool path, if able); never skipped, only relocated.

**Disciplines the run exposed:**
3. **Verify your *own* asserted collisions, not just asserted blockers.** Added a paragraph: an inferred collision (from a title/ADR) is a claim — pull the real *file-level* footprint before excluding an issue. (This run wrongly excluded `hkwp.1` by inference; it was clean new-file work that unblocked two downstream issues.)
4. **Pack file-colliding ready issues into one sequential lane *this* run.** Step 2 now makes sequential packing (combined PR, multiple `- Closes` lines) the default for two ready issues that share files, and reserves "defer to a future run" for unmerged-PR dependencies only. Step 6's refill text reconciled to match.

**Refinements that raise safe throughput:**
5. **Shared ledgers split by type.** The Guardrails rule now distinguishes the *wholesale-regenerated* `adr-index` (strict single writer) from the *row-addressable* `commitment-catalogue.md` (disjoint, non-adjacent rows may be written by separate lanes after a quick `grep -n` check). The lane brief and Guardrails both updated.
6. **`agent_dispatchable` filter.** Step 1 now drops human/account-bound issues (e.g. "create a cloud account"), with the inverse carve-out that account-independent artifact authoring (manifests, CI gates, migrations) stays dispatchable even when the live apply is account-gated.
7. **Reserved-set incremental planning.** A new note documents the second-pass case (add lanes to an already-committed plan): check each new candidate against the *union of committed-lane footprints*, not just against the other new candidates.

## Testing

Documentation-only change to a skill `SKILL.md`. Verified: the diff renders coherently; the prescribed footprint command is three-dot in all three locations while the two remaining two-dot references are the intentional inflation warnings; the primary checkout was untouched throughout (authored in a dedicated worktree). No code paths affected.

## ADRs touched/honoured

None — this is a skill-documentation change to `plugins/`; it implements, amends, or honours no ADR.

## bd issues closed on merge

- Closes babelstone-je32

author: genezhang
body:
## Summary

Fixes the ClickHouse-side failure on LDBC interactive **complex-12**, a multi-type variable-length path `(tag:Tag)-[:HAS_TYPE|IS_SUBCLASS_OF*0..]->(baseTagClass:TagClass)`.

Such a VLP is rendered as a `UNION ALL` of fixed-hop SELECT branches inside a CTE. The 1-hop branch additionally projected the Browser-dedup columns `r_from_id`/`r_to_id` (used to build a canonical relationship element_id), but the 0-hop and multi-hop branches did not — so the branches had **different column counts** and ClickHouse rejected the UNION:

```
Code: 53. DB::Exception: UNION different number of columns in queries. (TYPE_MISMATCH)
```

## Fix

In `generate_select_items` (`multi_type_vlp_joins.rs`), emit `r_from_id`/`r_to_id` only when the VLP is a **pure fixed single hop** (`min_hops == 1 && max_hops == 1`) — the only case where every branch is a uniform 1-hop, and the single-edge dedup is meaningful. A variable-length relationship binds to a *list* of relationships, so the single-edge element_id dedup does not apply there anyway.

A second uniformity hole (found in review) is also closed: `hop_rel_fk_info` is empty for **composite-FK** relationships, so a multi-type single hop mixing composite and non-composite FK rels would again diverge. Composite-FK branches now emit `NULL` placeholder `r_from_id`/`r_to_id`, keeping all branches uniform. (`NULL` unions cleanly with `toString(col)`/`string(col)` → `Nullable(String)` in CH, widened to string in Spark — verified.)

## Testing

- Verified **complex-12 now executes against live ClickHouse** (previously Code:53).
- Explicit `*1..1` still emits **real** dedup columns for non-composite FK rels (Browser feature preserved); `*1..2`/`*0..` are column-uniform.
- `vlp_multi_type` golden (`*1..2`) regenerated — it previously locked the broken non-uniform output; the comment now documents the column-count invariant.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, full `cargo test` all clean.
- Two adversarial review rounds: round 1 found the composite-FK uniformity hole (fixed); round 2 → 0 defects.

## Scope note

This is dialect-agnostic (shared renderer) and CH-side. Triage of the other LDBC non-MATCH queries: complex-1/3/11 are mini-dataset fixture column mismatches (not engine bugs); complex-14 uses Neo4j GDS/APOC procedures (unsupported feature). complex-12 was the only genuine translation bug among them.

author: btli
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1477. On macOS, agy binds its OAuth credential to the **real `$HOME`** via the login Keychain item *"Antigravity Safe Storage"* — which resolves against the real home path, **not** the contents of an isolated `$HOME/.gemini`. The per-session isolated HOME the bridge uses on Linux therefore makes **every agy turn hang at the interactive OAuth login prompt** on macOS — even with `.gemini`/`.antigravity` symlinked into the bridge tree and `oauth_creds.json` seeded.

## Fix

`seed_isolated_agy_home` returns `{"HOME": <real home>}` on `darwin` — no per-session HOME isolation, because the Keychain binding makes it impossible. Linux keeps the seedable file-token (`antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token`) isolation unchanged.

## Trade-off (macOS only)

Per-session agy state shares the user's real `~/.gemini`, and the relay MCP config lands in the bridge tree agy won't read (separate concern, #1194). Given agy's Keychain binding this is the only way it authenticates on macOS, and macOS hosts are single-user dev machines, so a shared `~/.gemini` is acceptable.

## Validation

**Live-validated 2026-06-27.** With this change, agy **1.0.13** authenticated headlessly on macOS (Google AI Pro account, model Gemini 3.5 Flash) and ran a full 3-gate approval turn end-to-end through a homelab omnigent server — the same run that validated #1472. Without it, agy stalls at the OAuth prompt under the isolated HOME and the turn never starts.

## Scope

One self-contained change to `seed_isolated_agy_home` (darwin early-return). ruff clean; introduces no new mypy errors over `main`. Independent of #1473 (the #1472 fix) — branched from `main`.

body:
## Summary

Stabilize magic link authentication across its public HTTP contracts, challenge lifecycle, transactional email delivery, local email capture, and OpenAPI documentation.

## Problem

Magic link request and consumption existed, but the request endpoint returned a message-only `200` response, lifecycle failures were collapsed into broad errors, and runtime delivery relied on an in-memory email gateway without production Resend or local SMTP support.

## Root cause

The original magic link foundation intentionally deferred the final cross-stack HTTP contract and transactional email integration. As a result, the API lacked stable semantic responses, explicit challenge states, environment-aware provider configuration, and production-ready delivery adapters.

## Changes

- Changed magic link requests to return `202 Accepted` with a stable `{ status: "accepted" }` body while preserving account-enumeration protection.
- Added semantic request and consumption errors for validation, throttling, delivery availability, invalid, expired, reused, superseded, and forbidden states.
- Implemented latest-link-wins challenge replacement with a serializable Prisma transaction and conflict retries.
- Added trusted frontend URL construction and typed email configuration for development, SMTP, and Resend providers.
- Added Resend and SMTP adapters behind the existing `EMAIL_GATEWAY` port, plus Mailpit for local capture.
- Updated Swagger decorators, auth/session docs, configuration docs, README guidance, and focused tests.

## Files added or updated

- `src/config/email/*`
- `src/config/env/*`
- `src/modules/auth/application/**/*magic-link*`
- `src/modules/auth/infrastructure/gateways/email/*`
- `src/modules/auth/infrastructure/persistence/**/*magic-link*`
- `src/modules/auth/presentation/http/**/*magic-link*`
- `src/infra/http/filters/*`
- `test/support/email/*`
- `docker-compose.yaml`
- `README.md`
- `docs/ai/**/*`
- `package.json`
- `package-lock.json`

## Impact

### Fixed

- Frontend consumers receive stable semantic status codes and public error codes for magic link flows.
- Staging and production can deliver through Resend, while local development and E2E environments can capture mail through SMTP/Mailpit.
- Only the latest active magic link for an email remains consumable.
- Provider details, raw tokens, cookies, and internal failures stay out of public responses and logs.
- Successful consumption preserves the shared auth/session response and cookie-only refresh-token contract.

### Not changed

- No frontend UI or browser E2E flow was implemented.
- No marketing email system, bounce or complaint webhook, or durable outbox was added.
- No distributed or email-keyed throttling was introduced.
- Resend remains replaceable through the existing email gateway abstraction.

- [x] lint (CI: Quality)
- [x] typecheck (CI: Quality)
- [x] tests (CI: Test)
- [x] build (CI: Build)
- [x] dependency audit (CI: Dependency audit)
- [x] manual validation completed

## 概要
ユーザー着眼「システム順位1位を常に買い、その馬の人気(オッズ順位)別にROIがどう動くか」を測る診断スクリプトを追加。前テスト（`analyze_dangerous_favorites`＝1番人気をシステム順位で層別）の**逆向き**で、軸を入れ替える。常にシステムTop-1を単勝で買い、その馬が2〜6番人気のとき（＝我々が市場より高く評価した逆張りピック）に妙味が出るか、人気が下がる（市場との乖離が広がる）ほどROIが開くかを順位別に確認する。

author: edugabriel12
body:
## Problema

Apostas **liquidadas antes de a carteira ser adicionada** apareciam nos resultados dos dois sistemas (dashboard e Sports). Só as entradas geradas **depois** da adição (as que ficam no BD) deveriam aparecer.

**Causa raiz:** ao adicionar uma carteira, o watcher lia **todas** as posições atuais da Data API — inclusive as que a carteira já tinha e que já haviam liquidado antes. No primeiro poll (`seen_conf` vazio):
- `persist_bets` gravava todas em `wallet_bets` → poluíam os **Resultados do wallet-dashboard**;
- `detect_entries` as disparava como "entradas novas" → empurradas ao **Sports**, onde liquidavam.

## Correção (causa raiz) — `watcher.py` + `wallets_store.py`

O **primeiro poll** de uma carteira apenas tira um *snapshot* de tudo que ela já possui (aberto **ou** já liquidado) como **baseline** e **não emite nada**. Esses mercados antecedem o monitoramento e são ignorados para sempre — só posições abertas **depois** da adição são rastreadas, persistidas ou enviadas.

- `wallets.baseline_at` (coluna nova, com migração) + tabela `baseline_markets`;
- `baseline_established` / `set_baseline` / `baseline_markets`;
- `detect_entries` e `persist_bets` pulam mercados do baseline; `detect_settlements` continua seguro (já filtra por `seen_conf`, que mercados do baseline nunca alcançam).

## Limpeza do que já vazou (scripts seguros: dry-run + backup `.bak` + `--apply`)

**1. Sports** — `polymarket-dashboard/backend/clear_db.py` (limpa o `entries.db` por completo):
```
cd polymarket-dashboard/backend
python clear_db.py                          # dry-run
python clear_db.py --apply                  # wipe completo (entries + Telegram) + backup
python clear_db.py --apply --keep-telegram  # mantém a config do Telegram
```

**2. Wallet-dashboard** — `polymarket-wallet-dashboard/backend/reset_tracking.py` (zera o tracking ao vivo, **mantém** as carteiras: nome/endereço/análise/thresholds/filtros):
```
cd polymarket-wallet-dashboard/backend
python reset_tracking.py                       # dry-run, todas
python reset_tracking.py --apply               # reseta todas + backup
python reset_tracking.py --apply --wallet-id 3 # só a carteira #3
```
Após rodar, reinicie os backends: cada carteira re-estabelece o baseline "a partir de agora" no próximo poll, então só as apostas abertas enquanto monitorada passam a aparecer.

## Testes / validação

- Suíte do wallet-dashboard **147/147 verde**; novo `TestBaseline` (pré-existentes ignorados; nova posição rastreada; cold-start; `reset_tracking` re-baselineia) + cobertura de store.
- Migração de `wallets.db` legado validada (adiciona `filters`/`baseline_at`, cria `baseline_markets`).
- CLIs `clear_db.py` e `reset_tracking.py` validados manualmente (dry-run, `--apply`, `--wallet-id`, backup, DB inexistente).

> Os BDs reais ficam na máquina do usuário; por isso a limpeza é entregue como script para rodar localmente.

# Description

Replaces empty `catch {}` blocks with proper error logging using `Logger.error`, `Logger.warn`, or `scope.trace` across 15 files. These catch blocks were silently swallowing errors, making failures invisible during debugging and production monitoring.

## What changed

Each empty `catch {}` now captures the exception and logs it with contextual information (source class/function, what operation failed):

```diff
-} catch {}
+} catch (ex) {
+    Logger.warn(ex, 'IntegrationService', `Failed to get integration '${integrationId}'`);
+}
```

### Severity classification

- **`Logger.error`** — failures that indicate bugs or broken state:

  - Composer file staging before commit (`composerWebview.ts`)
  - Deep link revision URI resolution (`deepLinkService.ts`)

- **`Logger.warn`** — expected-fallible operations (network, auth, optional features):

  - Subscription pre-check during upgrade (`subscriptionService.ts`)
  - Integration provider lookup (`integrationService.ts`)

author: jasonsiders
body:
**Closes #171**. Salesforce introduced an org-wide default delay setting for queueable jobs, which allows admins to slow execution across all queueables that don't explicitly specify a delay. Because `AsyncActionLauncher` was calling `System.enqueueJob(job, options)` without setting a delay value, any org with this setting enabled would unintentionally buffer async actions — undermining the framework's expectation of near-immediate execution.

The fix sets `options.minimumQueueableDelayInMinutes` on the `AsyncOptions` object before enqueueing, ensuring the framework always controls its own timing. The default is `0` (no delay), but users can now configure delays at two levels: a global default via `AsyncActionGlobalSetting__mdt.DelayInMinutes__c`, or a per-processor override via `AsyncActionProcessor__mdt.DelayInMinutes__c`. The processor-level setting takes priority over the global one, and both fall back to `0` when unset.

## What broke and why

Two separate issues in the previous deploy PR:

1. **Wrong Node env var** — \`ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true\` opts *back into* Node 20 (the deprecated path). The correct flag to force Node 24 is \`FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true\`.

2. **buildx container driver broke the Docker build** — \`docker/build-push-action@v5\` uses the \`docker-container\` BuildKit driver, which runs the build inside its own container. This caused \`npm ci --omit=dev\` to fail with exit code 127 (command not found) in the runtime stage. Plain \`docker build\` uses the default driver and has always worked.

## Changes

- Reverts Docker build step to \`docker build\` + \`docker push\` (the original, proven approach)
- Removes \`docker/setup-buildx-action\` and \`docker/build-push-action\` actions
- Replaces \`ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true\` with \`FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true\`

## Docker layer caching

Deferred to a follow-up. Will re-attempt with a CLI-only approach (\`docker buildx build --cache-from/--cache-to\`) that avoids the action compatibility issues entirely.

author: kennethsinder
body:
## The gap (after #3629)

#3628 closed the sentinel path of declared-done-with-red-build, and **#3629 added a loop-CAP done-conversion** that fires when an in-loop reverify ALREADY confirmed green at `iteration >= current_max`. **But the BUDGET / TOKEN / WALL-CLOCK exhaustion exit is still open.** In `crates/harn-stdlib/src/stdlib/agent/loop.harn`:

- `boundary_exhaustion.exhausted` break (~3150, wall-clock/cost)
- `agent_budget_post_call_blocked` breaks (~3704 / ~3764, token/cost)
- `exhaustion.exhausted` break (~3756)
- the natural `while iteration < current_max` fall-through

…all set `final_status = "budget_exhausted"` and break with **no terminal verify** when the model edited but no in-loop reverify fired (e.g. it wrote source and never ran a failing test, so `has_live_failure` was never set, so #3629's `post_edit_reverify_confirmed` is never true). A model that writes source then runs out of runway terminates RED. That is the dominant **zig-feat** failure mode (it exits `budget_exhausted`).

## Coverage verdict on #3629

#3629's only terminal addition is `if should_continue && post_edit_reverify_confirmed && iteration >= current_max { final_status = "done" }`. `post_edit_reverify_confirmed` is set **only** when an in-loop `reverify_mandated` verify ran and passed. It does **not** guard any of the budget/token/cost/wall-clock terminal breaks. So #3629 covers loop-cap-after-confirmed-green; this PR covers the budget-exit-after-unverified-edit residual. **Complementary, not duplicate** — this PR reuses #3629's `__agent_loop_verify_closure_exists` and `__agent_loop_post_edit_reverify_mandated` helpers.

## What this lands — the reserved-budget terminal verify

- **Default-OFF tracked flag** `stall_diagnostics.reserved_terminal_verify` + tunable `reserved_terminal_verify_iterations` (default 2), through the existing `agent_stall_repair_config` plumbing.
- `terminal_write_unverified`: set true on any successful source edit, cleared on any passing verification (reuses the `reverify_owed` clear points + the passing-diagnostic fold). Broader twin of the in-loop mandate, which only arms after a *prior* failure.
- **One centralized post-loop seam** (the main `while` is wrapped in an outer loop) runs the declared verifier once when the run would terminate `budget_exhausted`/`stuck` with an unverified write (**verify-first**). Green → `done`; red → surfaces the actual verifier failure (`reserved_terminal_verify_failed`) and, while reserve remains, spends one on a **bounded repair turn** before re-verifying. Reserve lives outside `current_max` (normal iterations can't consume it) and is hard-capped (can't loop forever). **The run never ends silently on an unverified red edit.**
- **OFF = byte-identical to today** — all 239 agents conformance tests pass, including #3629's `repair_post_edit_reverify_mandate`.
- New `reserved_terminal_verify` agent event (typed `ReservedTerminalVerify` variant, payload-preserving like `LoopStuckSignal`) on the transcript + ACP ext stream; added to `HARN_AGENT_EVENT_KINDS` + the acp-session-update schema; protocol artifacts regenerated.

## Proof

`conformance/tests/agents/reserved_terminal_verify_guard.harn` exercises the **exact residual #3629 cannot reach** (`max_iterations=2`, edit-only, no in-loop failing test → `post_edit_reverify_confirmed` is provably never set):
1. **ON, repair lands:** edit → iteration budget exhausts → reserved verify fires (red) → reserve grants a repair turn → re-verify passes → terminates `done`.
2. **ON, repair never lands:** reserve spent, the terminal verify still **runs** and surfaces the red, bounded.
3. **OFF control:** no reserved-verify events, plain `budget_exhausted` — byte-identical.

Local CI surface green: `harn fmt --check`, `cargo fmt --check`, `dump-protocol-artifacts --check`, `check_protocol_bindings.py`, 239 agents + 34 protocol conformance, `harn-vm`/`harn-serve` tests. (One pre-existing `harn-vm` test `process_exec_injects_workspace_local_tmpdir` fails identically on clean origin/main — macOS `/private/var` symlink quirk, unrelated.)

This is a conformance **spec edit**: adds a new behavioral test + a new agent-event kind; no existing `.expected` baseline changed.

## Owed gate

**Owes the paired N≥5 meter-holdout gate** (does it move zig-feat off 0/5 with a paired 95% CI lower bound > 0) before the flag may default ON. **No convergence flip is claimed here.**

author: okdaichi
body:
## Summary

First step toward optimizing the TS (`moq-web`) serialization layer: a runnable **benchmark baseline** plus a **label-gated CI check** that compares benchmarks on perf PRs — mirroring the Go `performance-check` flow.

### 1. Benchmark suite

`src/internal/message/message_benchmark.ts` (`Deno.bench`) covering the message codec hot path:

- **varint** — `writeVarint` / `readVarint` / `parseVarint` across all four widths (1/2/4/8-byte)
- **length-prefixed strings** — `writeString` (short/long), `writeStringArray`
- **per-message round trips** — `GroupMessage.encode`/`decode` (most frequent control message) and `SubscribeMessage.encode`/`decode` (string-heavy)

Uses minimal in-memory `Reader`/`Writer` to isolate codec CPU from WebTransport stream + async-scheduling overhead.

Also adds a **`deno task bench`** + `bench` config block so the suite is runnable as a unit, and repairs the stale `stream_memory_benchmark.ts` (its `ReceiveStream`/`SendStream` constructors still passed a removed `streamId`) so the whole suite type-checks.

### 2. CI: `ts-performance-check` workflow

New `.github/workflows/moq-web-benchmark.yml`, gated on the new **`ts-performance-check`** label (or manual dispatch):

- Runs the `deno bench` suite for **both the PR head and the base SHA in the same job** (avoids runner drift — same rationale as the Go `benchmark-label.yml`).
- Only runs when `moq-web/**` changed.
- Posts/updates a markdown **sec/op comparison** as a PR comment and uploads the raw JSON as an artifact.
- Backed by `.github/scripts/deno-bench-report.ts`, which diffs two `deno bench --json` runs and flags directional changes past a ±10% band.

> `deno bench` has no benchstat equivalent and its sec/op is shared-runner wall-time, so the comparison is a **directional signal only** (single sample, ±10% band) — re-run locally to confirm a delta.

## Baseline highlights (Deno 2.8.1, i7-10700K)

| benchmark | time/iter |
| --- | --- |
| `parseVarint` 1-byte (sync, buffer path) | ~6 ns |
| `readVarint` 1-byte (async, stream path) | ~1.6 µs |
| `writeVarint` 1-byte | ~1.1 µs (allocates a `Uint8Array` per call) |
| `GroupMessage.encode` / `.decode` | ~2.0 µs / ~1.5 µs |
| `SubscribeMessage.encode` / `.decode` | ~7.9 µs / ~4.0 µs |

Clear optimization targets surface immediately: the async `read*` path is ~150× the sync `parse*` path, and `writeVarint` allocates per call (so `encode`, a chain of small writes, is consistently slower than `decode`). Those are follow-up PRs, measured against this baseline via the new label.

## Test plan

- `deno task bench` runs all three benchmark files end-to-end (exit 0)
- `deno check` / `lint` / `fmt --check` pass on all changed files (incl. the report script)
- `deno-bench-report.ts` verified locally against two real `--json` runs
- Workflow YAML validated; `ts-performance-check` label created

author: kraulerson
body:
## Summary

Cycle 6 counter-sanitizer slot 2 — five sites across three small scripts share the same antipattern PR #53 fixed in `check-phase-gate.sh`:

```bash
var=$(cmd_that_may_exit_nonzero || echo "0")
```

The inner command (`grep -c`, `jq -r '.k | length'`) can print a leading `"0\n"` or `"null"` before failing, so the `||` appends a second fallback and the variable holds a two-line string (`"0\n0"`) or the literal `"null"`. Downstream arithmetic tests (`[ "$var" -gt 0 ]` / `-eq 0`) then error with **"integer expression expected"**, and under `set -euo pipefail` the failed arithmetic short-circuits the gate the script was supposed to take.

Five sites, same fix:

```bash
case "$var" in ''|*[!0-9]*) var=0 ;; esac
```

## Defects fixed

| Site | File:Line | Defect class | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scripts/validate.sh:258` | `grep -c "[RESET]"` zero-match → `"0\n0"` → leaked stderr + skipped `[OK]` branch | **Smoking gun** (reproduced in T2 — fails on main, passes after fix) |
| 2 | `scripts/session-test-gate-check.sh:198` | `jq -r '.features_completed \| length'` on missing key → `"null"` → broke Phase-2 no-features detector | U-K class |
| 3a-c | `scripts/session-end-qdrant-reminder.sh:36-38` | Three `jq -r ... \| length` counters feeding tool-usage summary + Phase-2 advisory checks | Advisory-only, trivially safe |

## Test plan

- [x] New regression suite `tests/test-validate-counter-sanitizer.sh` (5 scenarios): T1+T2 lock validate.sh:258 (T2 was the failing-test-first check); T3+T4 lock session-test-gate-check.sh:198; T5 locks session-end-qdrant-reminder.sh:36-38.
- [x] Adjacent regression: `tests/test-session-test-gate-check-merge.sh` — 7/7 green
- [x] Adjacent regression: `tests/test-check-phase-gate-counter-sanitizer.sh` — 7/7 green (sister suite from PR #53)
- [x] Sanitizer pattern matches `scripts/process-checklist.sh:45` and PR #53 verbatim — no novel pattern introduced.

## Out of scope

`scripts/process-checklist.sh` is deferred per cycle 6 verifier — all four sites there already use `jq -r '... // 0'`, which is safe. `scripts/test-gate.sh` and `init.sh` are owned by sibling agents in this cycle.

body:
# Implement Offline-First Progressive Web App (PWA) Support

## Description

This PR introduces **Offline-First Progressive Web App (PWA)** capabilities, enabling the application to function reliably even during network interruptions.

The implementation includes a Web App Manifest, Service Worker, IndexedDB-powered offline storage, enhanced caching strategies, and real-time offline status indicators. Together, these additions improve application resilience, loading performance, and user experience while maintaining compatibility with the existing architecture.

Closes #1055 

## Type of Change

* [x] New feature
* [ ] Bug fix
* [ ] Refactoring
* [ ] Documentation update

## Checklist

* [x] Code follows project conventions
* [x] Existing functionality preserved
* [x] Web App Manifest added
* [x] Service Worker implemented
* [x] IndexedDB offline storage integrated
* [x] Offline status indicator added
* [x] Ready for testing

---

# What Was Implemented

## Progressive Web App Configuration

Added a new:

* `manifest.json`

The manifest includes:

* Application metadata
* Theme colors
* Display configuration
* Icons for installation
* PWA launch settings

The manifest has been linked into `index.html`, allowing supported browsers to install the application as a Progressive Web App.

---

## IndexedDB Offline Storage

Created:

* `modules/offlineStore.js`

The module provides a reusable IndexedDB abstraction for storing application data locally.

Offline storage supports:

* Problems
* User progress
* Bookmarks
* Visualizer state

This enables critical application data to remain available even when network connectivity is unavailable.

---

## Service Worker

Created:

* `sw.js`

The Service Worker introduces intelligent offline caching strategies.

### Static Assets

Uses a **Cache-First (Stale-While-Revalidate)** strategy for:

* HTML
* CSS
* JavaScript
* Static application assets

This improves loading performance while ensuring cached resources remain updated in the background.

---

### Dynamic Requests

Implements a **Network-First** strategy for API requests.

If the network is unavailable, previously cached responses are served automatically to maintain application functionality.

---

## Cache Engine Integration

Updated:

* `modules/cacheEngine.js`

The cache engine now integrates directly with `offlineStore.js`.

API responses are automatically persisted to IndexedDB, allowing cached data to remain accessible across browser sessions and during offline usage.

---

## Offline Status Indicator

Enhanced the user interface with an offline connectivity banner.

Updates include:

* Offline banner integrated into `index.html`
* Dynamic online/offline detection using browser events
* Automatic visibility updates based on network status

The indicator immediately informs users whenever connectivity changes.

---

## Service Worker Registration

Integrated automatic Service Worker registration into `script.js`.

The application now:

* Registers the Service Worker after page load
* Handles successful registrations
* Logs registration failures gracefully

This enables offline functionality without requiring manual setup from users.

---

# Benefits

* Progressive Web App support
* Offline-first user experience
* Installable application
* IndexedDB-powered local persistence
* Intelligent caching strategies
* Improved application loading performance
* Automatic offline detection
* Seamless integration with the existing cache layer
* Enhanced resilience during network interruptions

---

# Acceptance Criteria

* Web App Manifest added
* Service Worker implemented
* Offline storage supported through IndexedDB
* Static assets cached
* Dynamic API requests cached
* Cache engine integrated with offline storage
* Offline status indicator displayed
* Service Worker registered automatically
* Existing functionality preserved

---

# Technical Notes

* The Service Worker applies a Cache-First (Stale-While-Revalidate) strategy for static assets and a Network-First strategy for dynamic API requests, balancing performance with data freshness.
* IndexedDB is used as the persistent offline storage layer for problems, progress, bookmarks, and visualizer state through a reusable `offlineStore.js` abstraction.
* The existing cache engine has been extended to synchronize cached API responses with IndexedDB, providing seamless offline access across browser sessions.
* Browser online/offline events are monitored to update the connectivity banner in real time, while Service Worker registration is performed automatically during application initialization.

### Motivation
- The legacy compressed pipe-format seals (`QRED1|...`) are being retired in favor of readable fragment URLs and modular reversible recipes such as `b45`.
- Simplify the codepath by removing generation/consumption of the removed compressed pipe format and its runtime dependencies.

### Description

body:
## Summary

Four user-reported items in one PR.

### 1. EMR crash (markup parser)

Root cause from the user's two crash dumps: AWS-returned EMR text contains \`[ContainerError(ContainerGroupId=cecf82cd-c71a-…)]\` brackets. Textual's \`Static\` widget parses Rich markup by default and crashed the compositor reflow with \`MarkupError: Expected markup value (found '-c71a-…')\`, bringing down the whole app.

Fix: \`markup=False\` on every Static rendering AWS-returned content (\`JobRunDetailPane\`, \`JobRunLogsPane\`, NAME/datetime cells in \`JobRunsPane\`). \`ApplicationPicker\` uses \`rich.markup.escape\` on application names so the intentional colored-glyph markup co-exists with arbitrary user text.

### 2. EMR poller cadence

Apps + runs 30s → **60s**; detail 5s → **30s**. Combined with the cadence-decay (×6 idle), an idle EMR page now re-fetches at most every ~6 min.

### 3. NavMenu pane-parity refactor

Rewrote NavMenu to host new \`NavRow\` widgets directly — no \`OptionList\`. Each NavRow uses the file pane's \`entry-row\`/\`-selected\` CSS classes so the visuals match by construction (height, padding, highlight, theme colors, ribbon). One flat cursor walks services + Settings (no Tab-jump between separate lists). Per-theme CSS gets \`NavRow{}\` + \`NavRow.-selected{}\` rules across 10 themes. Rail widened 12→14 so 'Settings' fits without clipping.

New spec at \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-28-cross-platform-readiness-design.md\` laying out five workstreams to make aws-tui first-class on macOS + Linux + Windows:
- Audit platform-sensitive surfaces (paths, config dirs, keychain, terminal caps, etc.)
- Expand CI matrix (lint+pkg on all 3 OS; integration/snapshot stay on linux)
- Per-platform install paths verified
- Release-time \`release-smoke\` job that pip-installs on all three before PyPI publish

Design only — no code yet, implementation plan to follow.
