author: losecher
body:
## What

Gateway startup previously called only **13** \`ensure*Store()\` functions; the other **19** were lazy-wired (called inside their own module's CRUD functions on first feature use). That left a "first feature use patches the schema" window and meant migration-vs-ensure drift on those 19 was only self-healed lazily.

This adds a canonical \`ensureAllStores()\` that calls all **32** \`ensure*Store\` in dependency-safe order, called once at startup right after \`migrateDir\`. The full runtime schema is materialized and any drift is self-healed at startup — no lazy-patch window.

## Changes

- **\`packages/gateway/src/bootstrap.ts\` (new)** — \`ensureAllStores()\` calls all 32 ensure*Store (28 agent + 3 memory + 1 idempotency) in dependency-safe order. \`dead_letter_events\` runs last (its inline FK references \`task_runs\`/\`run_specs\`). The 3 agent ensures not in the barrel (\`execution-store\`, \`tool-call-states\`, \`providers/telemetry\`) are imported via their subpath exports.
- **\`packages/gateway/src/server.ts\`** — replaced the 11 scattered startup ensure calls with a single \`await ensureAllStores()\` (before heartbeat/recovery/seeding); removed the now-unused ensure imports.
- **\`tools/check-migration-drift.ts\`** — imports \`ensureAllStores()\` from \`bootstrap.ts\` instead of re-listing the 32 functions. **Single source of truth** for the ensure set: the gate bootstraps its ensure-only DB with the exact same set the gateway uses.
- **\`package.json\`** — gate scripts switched from \`@los/agent\` to \`@los/gateway\` exec (gateway owns bootstrap and is the top of the dep stack).

## Why this is the right shape

- The drift gate (PR #89) enforces no **new** migration drift. This PR ensures existing drift is **self-healed at startup** for all 32 tables (not just 13), so the runtime is correct regardless of migration drift until PR 3 cleans it.
- Single source for the 32-list (\`bootstrap.ts\`) — the gate reuses it, so the two can't diverge.

## Verification

- Gateway restart: health 200, log \`[bootstrap] All runtime stores ensured\`, no errors.
- Drift gate unchanged: \`367 grandfathered, 0 new\` — \`ensureAllStores()\` produces the same schema as the previous explicit 32-list.
- \`pnpm check\` exit 0; gateway \`tsc\` clean.

## Follow-up

PR 3 (clean the 367 grandfathered drift entries, shrink baseline to empty) — now lower urgency, since all drift is self-healed at startup. Gate still prevents new drift.

author: mikemcdougall
body:
Round-3 release-audit fixes for confirmed S2 correctness/reliability findings in `honua-sdk`. These are new findings (no GH issue numbers); each is referenced below by file:line + recommendation.

## Findings addressed

### 1. UpdateCursor.update_row could emit duplicate OBJECTID keys (`packages/honua-sdk/honua_sdk/cursors.py:276`)
`Row.object_id` resolves the OID from any of `('objectid','objectId','OBJECTID')`, but `update_row` did `merged.setdefault('OBJECTID', object_id)`. When the source feature carried the OID under a non-canonical key (e.g. lowercase `objectid`), this added a **second** upper-case `OBJECTID`, so the `applyEdits` payload contained two object-id-like keys for the same row — which a strict FeatureServer may reject or use to update the wrong field. Now the existing OID key is reused; canonical `OBJECTID` is only added when none of the recognized variants is present. Fixed in both the sync and async cursors.

### 2. Async attachment upload blocked the event loop (`packages/honua-sdk/honua_sdk/protocols/geoservices.py:1168,1204`)
`AsyncGeoServicesFeatureServerClient.add_attachment`/`update_attachment` called the synchronous `_attachment_multipart_file` (blocking `open().read()` / `file.read()`) directly on the event loop, stalling all concurrent async work for the duration of the disk read. The read is now offloaded with `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`, mirroring `_resolve_dynamic_auth_headers_async` in `_http.py`.

### 3. Link-following pagination lacked a non-advancing-page guard (`packages/honua-sdk/honua_sdk/protocols/stac.py:109` and twins in `ogc_extras.py`, `odata.py`)
STAC/OGC-records/OData next-link loops default `max_pages=None`, so a server returning a constant/self-referential `next` link pointing at a full page could loop forever. Added the same guard the FeatureServer `query_pages` path has: track the previous next link and stop when the server repeats it. For STAC POST `/search`, the comparison uses a full link signature (method/href/body) so a body-based continuation token is not mistaken for a stuck cursor.

### 4. WFS-T transaction sent XML with no Content-Type (`packages/honua-sdk/honua_sdk/protocols/wfs.py:37,60`)
`transaction()` POSTed the WFS-T XML document with no declared content type; a conformant WFS endpoint or strict proxy/WAF can `415`/`400` it or mis-route it as form data. Now sends `Content-Type: application/xml` (overridable via a new `content_type` argument), consistent with every other body-bearing method in the SDK.

### 5. GeoServices envelope error codes mis-typed as HTTP statuses (`packages/honua-sdk/honua_sdk/_http.py:400`)
`raise_for_geoservices_error` fed the Esri envelope `error.code` straight into HTTP-status subclass logic, so token errors `498`/`499` surfaced as a plain `HonuaHttpError` (not catchable via `except HonuaAuthError`) and exotic codes (e.g. a negative HRESULT) became bogus out-of-range `status_code`s. Now a GeoServices-aware mapping routes auth/token codes (`401/403/498/499`) to `HonuaAuthError`, preserves the original Esri code on a new `HonuaHttpError.error_code` attribute, and normalizes the surfaced `status_code` for non-HTTP codes.

## Verification
- `ruff check` — clean
- `mypy packages/honua-sdk/honua_sdk packages/honua-admin/honua_admin` — clean
- `pytest tests/ --cov --cov-fail-under=94` — 1323 passed, 1 skipped, **94.50%** coverage
- Public-API snapshot refreshed (additive optional `error_code` kwarg only; backward compatible)

New/updated regression tests cover each fix.

| `@babel/core` | 7.29.0 | **7.29.7** | GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8 (任意ファイル読み取り / low) |

いずれも `devDependencies` 由来の間接依存で、**ビルド時のみ使用**（配布物には混入しない）。

## 🔧 変更内容

`package.json` に以下を追加:

```json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "tar@<7.5.16": "^7.5.16",
    "js-yaml@<4.2.0": "^4.2.0",
    "@babel/core@<7.29.6": "^7.29.6"
  }
}
```

### なぜ範囲指定 (`@<x.y.z`) なのか

`tar` や `js-yaml` はメジャーバージョンを跨ぐ更新（6→7, 3→4）が必要なため、Dependabotは「親パッケージが古い版を要求している」と判断して自動更新を諦めていました。

範囲を限定した override により、**脆弱なバージョンのみを置換**し、既に修正済みのバージョン（例: `tar@7.5.16`）はそのまま残すため、副作用を最小化しています。

## ✅ 検証結果

メジャーバージョン更新（特に `tar` 6→7 が electron-builder のパッケージングに影響しないか）を重点的にローカル検証しました:

- ✅ `pnpm install`（frozen-lockfile互換）
- ✅ `pnpm run build:ts`（TypeScriptビルド）
- ✅ `pnpm run test:ci` → **49 tests passed**（カバレッジ生成も成功 = babel/js-yaml正常動作）
- ✅ `pnpm run lint`（0 errors、既存warningのみ）
- ✅ `pnpm run dist` → **electron-builder で macOS zip + DMG パッケージング成功**（`@electron/rebuild`・dmgbuild など tar@7 使用箇所も正常）

- [x] 3件のオープン脆弱性アラートが解消されるバージョンに更新
- [x] lockfileを更新（CIの `--frozen-lockfile` 対応）

author: sentry[bot]
body:
# Description
This PR addresses the `TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier` (GAZEBO-1810) which occurs when the browser attempts to parse an HTML document as a JavaScript module.

The root cause was identified as the Nginx configuration serving the SPA's `index.html` fallback for missing asset files (e.g., stale hashed polyfills.js after a deployment). When a `<script type="module">` tag requested such a missing asset, it received HTML, leading to a parsing error.

# Code Example

# Notable Changes

**Changes implemented:**

1.  **Nginx Configuration (`docker/nginx.conf` and `docker/nginx-no-ipv6.conf`):**
    *   Added a specific `location /assets/` block that uses `try_files $uri =404;`. This ensures that requests for non-existent hashed assets under `/assets/` now correctly return an HTTP 404 status, preventing the Nginx fallback to `index.html` for these paths.

2.  **Client-side Error Handling (`index.html`):**
    *   Extended the existing `window.addEventListener('vite:preloadError')` logic. A new capturing `error` event listener is added to detect when a `<script type="module">` fails to load (e.g., due to a network error or receiving unexpected content like HTML). Upon detection, `window.location.reload()` is triggered, providing a graceful recovery by forcing the browser to fetch fresh assets.

These changes improve the robustness of asset loading, especially during deployments where asset hashes might change, and prevent the application from breaking due to module resolution failures.

In 2022 this entity acquired Codecov and as result Sentry is going to need some rights from me in order to utilize my contributions in this PR. So here's the deal: I retain all rights, title and interest in and to my contributions, and by keeping this boilerplate intact I confirm that Sentry can use, modify, copy, and redistribute my contributions, under Sentry's choice of terms.

author: var123321
body:
This PR implements several React performance optimizations in the XHub landing page:

1. **Component Memoization**: All major section components are now wrapped in `React.memo`. This significantly reduces re-renders when the `App` component state (like `versionInfo` or `modalOpen`) changes.
2. **Callback Stability**: Used `useCallback` for event handlers passed to child components. This ensures that the referential identity of these props is stable, allowing `React.memo` to be effective.
3. **Scroll Listener Optimization**: Added `{ passive: true }` to the scroll event listener in the `Header` component. This allows the browser to handle scrolling more efficiently without waiting for the JS execution.
4. **Static Data Extraction**: Moved complex static data transformations (like the scrolling background arrays) outside of the component render cycle to avoid redundant object creation.
5. **Type Safety**: Refactored internal Icon components to properly support standard SVG props, fixing several TypeScript errors.

Expected Impact:
- Smoother scrolling performance.
- Reduced CPU usage during state updates and modal transitions.
- Better overall responsiveness by minimizing main-thread blocking.

The server-side 用神 (analyze route) isn't visible here, but the view already has `result.pillars` → compute the canonical engine value once via `useMemo` (same `computeUsefulElement`), no reimplementation |

- **Strength bar:** support (扶) vs drain (抑) scores + the deciding thresholds (weak/strong/special) + weighted per-structure totals (比劫/印/食伤/財/官杀).

Render the card in isolation (hourly-UI pattern): strong/weak (用神 + 喜/忌 shown), borderline/special ("Not asserted", no crash on null), breakdown completeness (one side-cell per component → no rows dropped; stems shown), 月令 tagging, and pure-renderer proof (sentinel `reasoning`/`supportScore` props render verbatim → no recompute).

用神 was AI-only → now shown in full on the Result page (classification, 用神/喜/忌, and the weighted per-position breakdown) — calibration-ready.

author: kraulerson
body:
## Summary

Sister sweep to #53 (check-phase-gate.sh). Applies the canonical
counter-sanitizer pattern from `scripts/process-checklist.sh:45-46` to
all 8 `var=$(cmd | grep -c X || echo "0")` sites in
`scripts/test-gate.sh::check_phase_gate`.

The pattern, verbatim:

```bash
case "$var" in ''|*[!0-9]*) var=0 ;; esac
```

placed on the line immediately after each capture.

## Background — why this happens

`grep -c X` exits 1 on zero matches, but it has already printed `"0\n"`
to stdout. The `|| echo "0"` fallback then appends a second `"0"` and
the variable holds the two-line string `"0\n0"`. The subsequent
`[ "$var" -gt 0 ]` errors with `integer expression expected` and
(under `set -euo pipefail`) the arithmetic test returns non-zero —
silently bypassing whatever gate the test was guarding.

## Cycle 4 verifier correction (the educational artifact)

The cycle 4 survey claimed all 8 sites were equally exploitable.
**That was wrong.** Empirical verification in this PR distinguishes
three classes:

### EXPLOITABLE (no armor, fed real Phase 2 to 3 gate)

| Line | Variable | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| 373 | `feature_count` | grep direct; multi-line capture leaked to stderr but fell through to safe WARN branch |
| 375 | `feature_count` | same pattern with `head -1`; same fall-through |
| 395 | `cutline_items` | **smoking gun** — fed `if [ "$cutline_items" -gt 0 ] && [ "$recorded_features" -gt 0 ]`. When `PRODUCT_MANIFESTO.md` had a `Must-Have` section with zero `- **` bullets, `cutline_items` captured `"0\n0"`, the `[ -gt 0 ]` errored, the `&&` short-circuited, and the MVP-cutline comparison block was silently skipped — no WARN about "Feature count < MVP Cutline items". Same defect class as #53's `APPROVAL_LOG.md` silent OK. |

### LATENT — defense-in-depth (currently armored)

| Lines | Variables | Why safe today |
|---|---|---|
| 293-296 | `sev1_count`, `sev2_open`, `sev2_deferred`, `sev3_open` (BUGS.md) | `tr -d '[:space:]'` reduces `"0\n0"` to `"00"`; arithmetic treats `"00"` as 0 cleanly; downstream `$((${var:-0} + ...))` tolerates it too. |
| 302-305 | `gh_sev1`, `gh_sev2_open`, `gh_sev2_deferred`, `gh_sev3` (gh CLI + jq length) | Same `tr -d` armor. |

These are safe **by accident**. A future maintainer who drops the
`tr` would silently re-introduce the same bypass class.

### REDUNDANT — jq with `// 0` default

| Line | Variable | Why redundant |
|---|---|---|
| 380 | `recorded_features` | `jq '.features_completed | length'` returns a clean integer when the file exists; the `|| echo "0"` only fires if jq itself errors. |
| 416 | `untested` | `jq '... // 0'` already has a null-default. |

Sanitizer is purely cosmetic for these two, applied for codebase
consistency so all eight sites read identically.

## Test strategy (TDD)

`tests/test-test-gate-counter-sanitizer.sh` (new, 5 cases):

| | Scenario | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | zero-cutline-items in `PRODUCT_MANIFESTO.md` Must-Have | FAIL (integer leak) | PASS (no leak) |
| T2 | populated cutline + recorded < cutline | PASS (cutline_items captured cleanly when non-zero) | PASS (regression guard) |
| T3 | matched cutline + features | PASS | PASS (regression guard) |
| T4 | zero bugs in BUGS.md | PASS (armored sites work) | PASS (sanitizer + armor co-exist) |
| T5 | worst-case zero-match across all sites | FAIL (integer leak) | PASS (no leak) |

T1 + T5 fail on `main` before this fix, proving the smoking gun.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test-test-gate-counter-sanitizer.sh` — 5/5 passing
- [x] `tests/test-test-gate-null-handling.sh` — 5/5 passing (adjacent regression)
- [x] `tests/test-check-phase-gate-counter-sanitizer.sh` — 7/7 passing (PR #53 sister suite)

## Don't list

- Did not add `set -o pipefail` (cycle 4 verifier proved it does not
  fix this defect class; the case-statement IS the fix).
- Did not touch init.sh / validate.sh / session-* — those are sibling
  slots in this cycle.

body:
## Summary

Two salvaged fixes for the OpenCode Zen / Go model picker, both surfaced by a Discord `/model` report where `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` was missing from the dropdown and a typed switch failed against a stale build.

- **#49129 (@Afnath-max):** refreshes the OpenCode Zen curated catalog (adds the models the report was missing, incl. `nemotron-3-ultra-free`), uncaps the picker for OpenCode aggregators so their full 70+ catalog is visible instead of being cut to 25 before display, and merges live-API entries first for aggregators (their live `/v1/models` is the authoritative catalog).
- **#51488 (@ipriyaaanshu):** clears a stale inline `model.base_url` when the gateway persists a `/model` switch to a built-in provider, completing the endpoint-cleanup gap from merged #49380.

## What was salvaged + corrected

The original #49129 made the live-first merge **unconditional** in the shared `provider_model_ids()` profile branch — which regressed curated-first for single providers (kimi/zai, #46309) and encoded that regression by flipping the existing `kimi-coding` and `zai` test assertions to expect live-first. Salvage scopes live-first to an explicit `_LIVE_FIRST_PICKER_PROVIDERS = {opencode-zen, opencode-go}`; every other provider keeps curated-first. The uncapped-picker and live-first sets were both widened to `opencode-go`, which has the same large-catalog problem.

The `#51488` change is correct as-is: built-in providers resolve their endpoint from the provider profile, so popping the stock/stale inline `base_url` for non-`custom` providers is the right behavior; `custom` endpoints keep their `base_url` (guarded by the `!= "custom"` check). `clear_base_url` is opt-in (default `False`), so no other caller changes behavior.

> Discord's 25-option select-menu limit is a hard API constraint; the adapter already shows "*N more available — type `/model <name>` directly*". A pagination/autocomplete UI is a separate follow-up, not in this PR.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/models.py`: refreshed opencode-zen curated catalog; per-provider merge order via `_LIVE_FIRST_PICKER_PROVIDERS`.
- `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`: `_UNCAPPED_PICKER_PROVIDERS` = {opencode-zen, opencode-go}.
- `hermes_cli/config.py`: opt-in `clear_base_url` on `clear_model_endpoint_credentials()`.
- `gateway/slash_commands.py`: clear stale inline `base_url` for non-`custom` providers on gateway model-switch persistence.
- Tests: per-provider merge-order contract; restored `kimi-coding` curated-first assertion; opencode-zen uncap + gateway base_url-persist guards.
- `scripts/release.py`: AUTHOR_MAP entries for both contributors.

author: dcetlin
body:
## Summary

Type `! do this instead` in a session thread to interrupt the session's current work and redirect it. The `!` prefix sends Escape to the session's tmux pane (interrupting mid-turn), waits 50ms for the interrupt to register, then delivers the stripped message through the bridge.

The daemon owns the sequencing between two independent delivery paths — tmux terminal input (Escape keypress) and MCP bridge (message notification). The 50ms delay guarantees the interrupt lands before the new message arrives.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `daemon/router.ts` | +19 lines — detect `!` prefix in thread messages, send Escape via tmux, delay, deliver |
| `daemon/commands/global.ts` | +1 line — add `! <message>` to commands help text |
| `daemon/__tests__/router-commands.test.ts` | +34 lines — regex matching tests for interrupt prefix |

+54 lines total.

## How it works

1. User types `! stop and do this instead` in a session thread
2. Router detects `!` prefix, strips it
3. Reacts ⚡ on the message
4. `tmux send-keys -t <session> Escape` — interrupts current generation
5. 50ms delay — Escape is a synchronous terminal keypress, lands immediately
6. Delivers `stop and do this instead` as a normal message through the bridge
7. Session receives the new message as its next instruction

## Edge cases

- `!` alone (no content after prefix) — ignored, not treated as interrupt
- `!` with only whitespace — ignored (stripped content is empty)
- `!` in the middle of a message — not an interrupt, routed normally
- Session tmux is dead — `execSync` fails silently, message still delivers (graceful degradation)

## Tests

5 new tests for the interrupt prefix regex. 173 total pass.

author: williamchildres
body:
## Summary

Fixes duplicate incoming Recovery-amplification blocks in the live **Show analysis details** view for the Feskar / Rhysarion / Shadowsong formation.

The underlying trace collection and project-context export were already structurally deduplicated. The remaining issue was caused by the React rendering boundary using a non-unique `trace.id` as the component key.

Ebbing Fury and Echoing Melody incoming-amplification traces can share the same generated `trace.id` when they use the same modifier and recipient. React therefore received duplicate keys and could reconcile the live trace cards incorrectly, leaving duplicate Ebbing Fury blocks in the rendered DOM.

This PR:

* applies the canonical final Technical Analysis dedupe before live rendering;
* exports and reuses the canonical structural trace identity;
* uses that structural identity as the React key;
* adds a live application-rendering regression test.

No mechanics, cards, schemas, versions, Commands, or Pass 2 behavior were changed.

## Root cause

The live analysis path is:

```text
FormationBuilderSection
  → analyzeFormationTraces
  → filteredTraces
  → visibleTraces
  → TraceCard
```

The trace collection itself was correct.

The defect occurred in `src/app/App.tsx`, where the live rendering loop used:

```text
trace.id
```

as the React key.

For incoming Recovery amplification, the generated trace ID is based primarily on the modifier and recipient. It does not fully distinguish the source ability or matched output.

As a result, these distinct traces could share the same React key:

* Ebbing Fury → Feskar through Unbroken Devotion
* Echoing Melody → Feskar through Unbroken Devotion

The same collision occurred for Shadowsong.

React duplicate-key reconciliation could then leave an extra Ebbing Fury card in the live DOM even though the source trace collection and exported JSON contained the correct unique set.

The project-context export did not exhibit the issue because it serializes structurally deduplicated trace data and does not use React component keys.

## What changed

### Canonical structural identity

The existing structural identity used for final Technical Analysis deduplication is now exported as:

```text
technicalAnalysisTraceIdentity
```

This identity distinguishes traces using stable structured data rather than display prose or the shorter generated trace ID.

It includes relevant fields such as:

* source dragon;
* source ability;
* receiving dragon and mechanic;
* channel;
* match kind;
* interaction scope;
* modifier capability IDs;
* matched output capability IDs;
* source-scope compatibility;
* target structure;
* state;
* structured effects;
* other trace-defining metadata.

### Defensive live deduplication

The live Technical Analysis card boundary now uses:

```text
dedupeFinalTechnicalAnalysisTraces
```

before rendering trace cards.

This protects the live view from duplicate inputs even when duplicates are introduced after the primary formation-analysis stage.

### Unique React keys

`TraceCard` components now use:

```text
technicalAnalysisTraceIdentity(trace)
```

as their React key.

This prevents Ebbing Fury and Echoing Melody traces for the same recipient from colliding during reconciliation.

## Before and after

### Before

Ctrl+F results in live **Show analysis details**:

```text
Feskar amplifies Rhysarion Recovery: 3
Shadowsong amplifies Rhysarion Recovery: 3
```

Each heading contained:

* one Ebbing Fury trace;
* one duplicate Ebbing Fury trace;
* one Echoing Melody trace.

### After

```text
Feskar amplifies Rhysarion Recovery: 2
Shadowsong amplifies Rhysarion Recovery: 2
```

Each heading now contains exactly:

* one Ebbing Fury trace;
* one Echoing Melody trace.

Final structural counts:

* Incoming Recovery amplification: `4`
* Outgoing Recovery support: `5`
* Total Technical Analysis traces: `61`

## Preserved trace separation

The correction preserves the four distinct incoming amplification interactions:

1. Ebbing Fury → Feskar through Unbroken Devotion
2. Ebbing Fury → Shadowsong through Unbroken Devotion
3. Echoing Melody → Feskar through Unbroken Devotion
4. Echoing Melody → Shadowsong through Unbroken Devotion

It also preserves the five distinct outgoing Recovery-support traces:

1. Ebbing Fury → Feskar
2. Ebbing Fury → Rhysarion
3. Ebbing Fury → Shadowsong
4. Echoing Melody → Feskar
5. Echoing Melody → Shadowsong

Incoming amplification is not merged with outgoing support, and different recipients, source abilities, channels, target groups, or source effects remain distinct.

## Existing behavior preserved

This PR does not change:

* Formation Builder card aggregation;
* exact-recipient aggregation;
* Ebbing Fury Recovery behavior;
* Ebbing Fury friendly impairment behavior;
* Ebbing Fury enemy-side all-enemies reduction;
* Echoing Melody targeting;
* Unbroken Devotion targeting or attribution;
* Scorched Earth’s 10% base chance;
* Scorched Earth’s 20% Panic replacement chance;
* Scorched Earth’s Vulnerable +15%;
* Scorched Earth’s unresolved roll scope;
* Blazing Onslaught;
* Blazing Conductor;
* Inspiring Melody;
* Ensnare;
* Resilient Bond;
* Unyielding Grasp;
* Emerald Inferno;
* Trial by Flame;
* Commands;
* Full Command text;
* Dragon Database raw wording;
* Pass 2 presentation behavior.

## Files changed

* `src/app/App.tsx`
* `src/services/synergyTrace.ts`
* `src/test/appRendering.test.tsx`
* refreshed tracked `project-context/` outputs

`project-context.zip` remained untouched, untracked, and unstaged.

## Regression coverage

Added a live application-rendering regression that verifies the actual **Show analysis details** path.

The test confirms:

```text
Feskar amplifies Rhysarion Recovery: 2
Shadowsong amplifies Rhysarion Recovery: 2
```

It also verifies that each recipient has:

* one Ebbing Fury incoming amplification;
* one Echoing Melody incoming amplification.

Additional existing regression coverage confirms:

* four total incoming Recovery amplification traces;
* five outgoing Recovery-support traces;
* no collapse of materially distinct traces;
* project-context export remains structurally unique.

## Validation

Passed:

```text
Passed

Final Technical Analysis dedupe tests
Passed

Feskar / Rhysarion / Shadowsong regression
21 tests passed

Application rendering tests

Full Vitest suite

Passed

Passed

git diff --check
Passed

```

## Versions

Unchanged:

* Database: `0.6.2`
* Data schema: `12`
* Local roster schema: `3`
* Game build: `26.6.53509`
* Context export: `1`

No schema, migration, persisted-roster data, public export-format, or version change was introduced.

* Baseline: `4247ae501f3b0ba39ba31435b0742c9d96b0e88f`
* Branch: `fix/live-analysis-output-dedupe`
* Commit: `d5050cc419dab468a899ecea6686a763b622a747`

The PR could not be opened automatically because GitHub CLI was unavailable in the Codex environment.

Use:

* Left Flank: Feskar

5. Confirm one result uses Echoing Melody.

body:
Beat C of the galaxy roadmap: an on-camera "tamper it and the signature breaks" demo, fully wired and server-verified.

## Backend
- **GET /demo/signed-manifest** — the primary demo manifest + its COSE signature (signed with the server's persistent checkpoint key) + the public key. `demo.primary_manifest()` builds the canonical manifest so signing and verifying agree.
- **POST /verify {manifest, signatureB64}** — re-verifies a possibly-edited manifest against the signature using the checkpoint public key. Changing any signed field (manifest id, asset hash, created-at, system provenance) flips `signatureValid=false`. Adversarial input collapses to false, never a 500.

## Frontend
- **TamperPanel** — fetches the signed manifest, shows the model + asset-SHA as editable inputs, re-verifies on demand. Untouched → green "SIGNATURE VALID"; edit a signed field → red "TAMPERED". Real cryptographic check server-side, not a UI trick.

## Tests

author: gproust
body:
## Problem

The `Release` workflow failed on **every push** with a `startup_failure` (0 jobs ran). Root cause: it referenced the **`secrets` context inside an `if:` condition**, which GitHub Actions does not allow:

```yaml
- name: Decode keystore
  if: ${{ secrets.KEYSTORE_BASE64 != '' }}   # ❌ invalid — secrets not allowed in if:
```

Because the file couldn't compile, GitHub recorded a failed run for every push regardless of the `tags`-only filter — which is why it appeared to "run every time" *and* always fail.

## Fix

- **Stop the startup failure:** map the secret to a job-level `env` var and gate the decode step on `env.KEYSTORE_BASE64` (which *is* valid in `if:`).
- **Make it manual-only** (as requested): trigger on `workflow_dispatch` only, with an optional `tag` input. Run it from **Actions → Release → Run workflow**; supply a tag (e.g. `v1.0`) to also create that tag and a GitHub Release with the APK attached, or leave it empty to just build and upload artifacts.
- **Docs:** update `README.md` and `docs/RELEASING.md` to describe the manual run instead of tag-push.

The workflow no longer runs on ordinary pushes, so `main` won't accumulate failed release runs anymore.

author: lionsr
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the mode-observable row contract for early-stopped multi-frequency cooling runs.

For strided mode measurements, the cooling loop already recorded the initial cycle, stride-selected cycles, and the requested final cycle. In stop-on-cap or other early-stopped runs, the physically relevant final state is instead the completed stopped cycle. If that cycle was off the stride grid, the run kept finite energy and bond diagnostics but omitted the corresponding `mode_hk` and `mode_nk` row.

The cooling loop now appends the completed stopped cycle to `mode_measurement_cycles` and records its Bogoliubov mode row before truncating the result arrays. Non-stopped runs keep the existing requested-final-cycle behavior.

## Validation

- `julia --project=. --startup-file=no test/test_tn_mode_observables.jl`
- `julia --project=. --startup-file=no test/test_multi_frequency.jl`
- `julia --project=. --startup-file=no test/runtests.jl`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #513.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized change to mode-measurement bookkeeping on early stop, with docs and regression tests; no auth or broad API surface changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **strided Bogoliubov mode measurements** when cooling stops before the requested step count (e.g. `--stop-on-bond-cap` or a custom `stop_condition`). Previously, `mode_measurement_cycles` only covered stride hits and the **requested** final cycle, so an off-stride **actual** last cycle could have finite energy/bond data but **missing** `mode_hk` / `mode_nk` rows.
> 
> The cooling loop now calls **`_record_final_stopped_mode_measurements!`** before **`truncate_measurements_to_step`**: it adds the completed stopped cycle to `mode_measurement_cycles`, fills that row when needed, and rolls back the cycle list if recording fails. Docs and the large-N driver describe the same contract.
> 
> **Tests** cover TN MCWF and ED density-matrix early stops with `mode_measurement_stride=3`, expecting measured cycles `[0, 2]` and finite mode data on rows 1 and 3.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1ce7f9e764964c4d74623c9f55f89856b775ce0b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: davidobando
body:
## Summary

cs2gs rendered a bare `GenericNameSyntax` in expression position (a static-member-access receiver on a **constructed generic type**, e.g. `Mp4Operation<ChapterInfo?>.FromCompleted(this, null)`) as a bare identifier, **dropping the type arguments**. The emitted G# became `Mp4Operation.FromCompleted(...)`, which bound the wrong non-generic overload and failed with `GS0144` at the call site.

This renders such a receiver as a `TypeExpression` so the type arguments are preserved: `Mp4Operation[ChapterInfo?].FromCompleted(...)`. Generic **method groups** (`M<T>(...)`, where the enclosing invocation applies the type args) continue to render as bare identifiers — the fix is gated on the generic name binding to an `INamedTypeSymbol`.

## Detail

- `TranslateExpression`'s `GenericNameSyntax` case previously returned `new IdentifierExpression(generic.Identifier.Text)`, erasing `<…>`.
- Now: when `GetSymbolInfo(generic).Symbol is INamedTypeSymbol`, render `new TypeExpression(typeMapper.Map(genericType, …))` → `Name[args]`; otherwise keep the bare identifier (method-group case).
- Depends on gsc #1323 (now merged) so the emitted `Type[T?].Member` form round-trip-parses for nullable/array/nested-generic type args.

## Oahu impact (#914)

`Oahu.Decrypt` `Mp4File.cs:161` `Mp4Operation<ChapterInfo?>.FromCompleted(this, null)` now translates to `Mp4Operation[ChapterInfo?].FromCompleted(this, nil)` and the `GS0144` clears. Decrypt baseline 94 → 92.

## Tests

`GenericStaticReceiverTranslationTests` (2): static call on a constructed generic type keeps `[T]`; non-generic call is unchanged.

## Verification

- `dotnet build GSharp.sln -c Release -graph`: 0/0.
- Full cs2gs suite: **322 passed**.
- Decrypt re-baseline: Mp4File `FromCompleted` `GS0144` cleared.

Refs #914

author: shangkunli
body:
## Summary
This PR adds an analysis pass for already-scheduled Taskflow programs. Given tasks with `profile_info.duration` and `task_orchestration_info.cgra_positions`, the pass reconstructs the task execution order from data dependencies and per-CGRA context order, then reports the schedule’s pipeline interval, bottleneck task, and critical path.

## Changes:
- Add `TaskScheduleResult` to represent concrete per-task scheduling facts.
- Add `TaskPipelineIntervalAnalyzer` to compute the pipeline interval from task dependencies and CGRA context reuse.
- Add `--analyze-task-pipeline-interval`, which emits `task_pipeline_interval_info` on the parent func.func.
- Add focused tests for: temporal reuse on different CGRAs, dependency chains, diamond-shaped task graphs, and independent tasks on one CGRA

## Terminology
- Pipeline interval: the steady-state time gap between two consecutive completed executions of the scheduled task graph. It measures how often the scheduled pipeline can produce results after warm-up.
- Per-CGRA context reuse: multiple tasks sharing the same physical CGRA at different context slots, which adds ordering constraints beyond data dependencies.

body:
Closes #247.

Follow-up to the order-overlay demo (#223). A demo recording now reproduces what the player did with the **mouse**, not just the orders that resulted. A new optional `pointer` presentation track (alongside the #222 camera track) captures the cursor, selection, drag-box and armed stance per tick during live play, and the demo overlay replays them.

| Drag-box select | Selection halos + stance label |
|---|---|
| ![cursor drag-boxing three regiments, marquee + reticle over the order markers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lacaedemon/sparta/a6a27a341a1159c105346435fa1cff98376c373a/demos/shots/demo-pointer-drag.png) | ![yellow selection halos on three regiments; yellow Skirmish-tinted cursor with label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lacaedemon/sparta/a6a27a341a1159c105346435fa1cff98376c373a/demos/shots/demo-pointer-selection.png) |

## What it draws (under the demo overlay)
- **Cursor reticle**, tinted + **labelled** when a stance (Hold / Flank / Rear / Skirmish / Support) is armed.
- **Selection halos** — yellow rings on the still-living selected regiments.
- The multi-select **drag-box**.
- A **click pulse** ringing out where each order was issued — driven from the orders already in the replay, so no extra capture.

## Design
Mirrors the camera track throughout: tick-stamped, **deduplicated** (a still pointer costs one keyframe; sub-pixel cursor jitter dropped), holds the latest keyframe at/before the current tick, and **additive/back-compatible** — replays without a pointer track show no cursor overlay, and no format `version` bump is needed.

Purely cosmetic and deterministic: recorded only in `RECORD`, drawn only under the demo overlay, **never read by the simulation**. In-app *Watch Replay* keeps the Space-held survey, unchanged.

## Changes
- `Replay.gd` — `record_pointer` / `pointer_for_tick` / `has_pointer_track` / `pulses_for_tick`; load + save the optional track.
- `Battle.gd` — sample `SelectionManager.pointer_state()` each recorded tick; expose `current_tick()` / `unit_by_uid()`.

author: john-rocky
body:
Adds **Places365 scene recognition** (ResNet18, CSAILVision, **MIT**) — **365 scene categories** (beach, kitchen, forest, office, …), a new zoo task distinct from object classification (it answers *what kind of place* a photo is). Pure CNN, **fully on the CompiledModel GPU**, stacked on the RTMPose-family PRs.

## On-device (Pixel 8a, Tensor G3 — verified)

- **61 / 61** nodes on `LITERT_CL` (full GPU residency), **~2 ms** @ 224×224, fp16 **22.8 MB**
- device-vs-PyTorch corr **1.0**, top-1 match (bundled beach → "beach"); ran on device, no crash.

## Two numerically-exact re-authorings (the 2nd is a reusable Mali finding)

1. global `AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)` → `mean(3).mean(2)` (the multi-axis-pool fix).
2. **ResNet stem `MaxPool2d(3,s2,p1)` → zero-pad + valid max-pool.** PyTorch's max-pool pads with `-inf`, which litert-torch lowers to a **`PADV2`** the Mali ML Drift delegate **won't delegate** — it splits the graph into CPU partitions (`36 out of 61, 2 partitions`) and **fails to compile** (desktop op-check passes; not an op-blocklist hit). Since the stem max-pool follows a ReLU (inputs ≥ 0), a **0-pad is exactly equivalent** and emits a delegatable `PAD` → `61/61` full GPU. Reusable for any ResNet/ImageNet/Places stem.

## What's in this PR

- `places365/` module (`PlacesClassifier.kt` + `MainActivity.kt` top-5 scenes + `scripts/` + README + 365-label json + bundled landscape image)
- Root `README.md` entry + a `docs/LITERT_CONVERSION_GUIDE.md` note
- Model on HF: [litert-community/Places365-ResNet18-LiteRT](https://huggingface.co/litert-community/Places365-ResNet18-LiteRT); models gitignored.

Upstream: [CSAILVision/places365](https://github.com/CSAILVision/places365) (MIT).

author: jeffrey-stellar
body:
## Summary

Music stopped playing on iPhone whenever the screen locked, even though the Media Session lock-screen controls were set up correctly.

**Root cause:** the visual equalizer routes the `<audio>` element through a Web Audio `AudioContext` (`createMediaElementSource`), and `initEqualizer()` runs on **every** track. iOS suspends the `AudioContext` whenever the screen locks or the PWA is backgrounded, which silences anything flowing through that context — so playback died on lock.

**Fix:** detect iOS (including iPadOS, which reports a desktop Safari UA but exposes touch) and skip the Web Audio routing there, so the `<audio>` element plays straight to the system output and keeps playing in the background. The empty equalizer canvas is hidden on iOS.

**Trade-off:** the visual equalizer no longer renders on iOS. This is unavoidable — there's no reliable way to keep both the visualizer and background playback (the suspended `AudioContext` can't be resumed without a foreground user gesture), and the equalizer isn't visible on a locked screen anyway. Desktop and Android are unchanged and keep the equalizer.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` passes; `npm test` → 62/62 frontend tests pass.
- [ ] On iPhone (PWA): play a track, lock the screen → audio continues; lock-screen controls (play/pause/next/prev/seek) work.
- [ ] On desktop: equalizer still animates during playback.

author: petwashglobal
body:
From the full auth review. Three **confirmed** issues (verified, not over-fires):

## 1. Login didn't return users where they were (the big one)
`RequireAuth.tsx` redirects gated pages to `/signin?**from**=<page>`, but the login screen only read `?**redirect**=`. So after logging in from **any** gated page (booking chat, marketplace booking, etc.), the user landed on `/home` — losing their destination. `SignUpLuxury` now reads **both** `?redirect=` and `?from=` (same open-redirect-safe `/^\/(?!\/)/` validation).

## 2. Marketplace detail pages lost booking intent
`SitterDetail`, `WalkerDetail`, `MarketplaceBookingFlow` navigated to `/signin` with **no return path**. Now pass `?from=<current path+query>` → user lands back on the booking after login.

## 3. OAuth token logging (security hygiene)
`social-oauth.ts` logged the **full** provider response on token-exchange failure (TikTok + Instagram) — could leak access/refresh tokens into logs. Now logs the **error code only**.

## Verify
- Auth regression tests: **39 pass** (seedIntent, intentParam, postLoginCoordinator, signinEnumeration).
- No bare `navigate('/signin')` left in the 3 detail flows.

## Risk
**Low.** Redirect-param read + return-path on nav + a log redaction. Open-redirect protection unchanged (same validation applies to `from`). Rollback = revert single commit.

## Still open from the review (separate follow-ups, NOT in this PR)
- `AdminKYC`/`AdminSystemLogs` gate on a client-only hardcoded email (server APIs are admin-gated, so not a breach — but should use AdminRouteGuard). **Admin-internal.**

author: lakshay122007
body: ## What does this PR do? Adds Code to Complexity (`pages/tools/complexity-analyzer/`) — a tool where users paste pseudocode or JavaScript and get instant line-by-line Big-O annotations with a full derivation explaining why the complexity is what it is. **How it works:** The analyzer scans code line by line, tracking loop nesting depth and recursion patterns to assign per-line complexity, then takes the dominant term as overall. **Pattern detection:** | Pattern | Detected As | |---|---| | Single `for`/`while` loop | O(n) | | Nested loops (depth 2) | O(n²) | | Triple nested loops | O(n³) | | Loop with halving (mid, `>>=1`) | O(log n) | | Outer loop + inner halving | O(n log n) | | Two recursive calls on same line | O(2ⁿ) | | Single tail recursion (n-1) | O(n) | | Permutation/factorial keywords | O(n!) | | `.sort()` call | O(n log n) | | `.shift()` inside loop | ⚠️ Hidden O(n) warning | | Array access, hash map ops | O(1) | **8 Presets:** Linear Search, Binary Search, Bubble Sort, Merge Sort, BFS, Naive Fibonacci, LCS DP, Matrix Multiply **Panels:** - Per-line annotation badge column (right of editor) - Verdict card: time + space + plain English + danger rating - Derivation steps: each pattern explained with line numbers - Pattern detector: named recognized patterns ## Related issue Fixes #1059 ## Checklist - [x] All 8 presets analyzed correctly - [x] Nesting depth tracks O(n) → O(n²) → O(n³) - [x] Halving detection correct - [x] Double recursion → O(2ⁿ) - [x] Line nums sync with scroll - [x] Verdict updates after every analyze - [x] Ctrl+Enter shortcut works - [x] No console errors - [x] No conflicts with script.js - [x] Mobile responsive ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a new “Code to Complexity Analyzer” page with an interactive editor, preset examples, complexity results, pattern detection, and learning content. * Added a navigation entry so the tool is easier to discover from the site menu. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved the analyzer experience with synced line numbers, inline annotations, clear/reset actions, copy support, and responsive layouts for smaller screens.

author: hanzei
body:
## Summary

A design doc (no code) for the **capstone of the serverless local-mode epic (#511)**: letting a user who started in **local mode** adopt a real Jot server, push all on-device notes/labels/settings up to it, and then continue as a normal server-backed client.

The doc explains why this is largely *orchestration*, not a new sync engine — the epic already paid for the hard parts:
- Local IDs (user/note/item/label) are already **server-format**, so rows migrate without re-keying.
- The server already **honors client-supplied IDs**, so local notes can be created under their existing IDs.
- The offline **replay engine** (`sync_queue` + `performDrain`) already exists and is reused; local mode just no-ops it today (#514).

## Decisions captured

- **New-account-only** target this iteration (empty account ⇒ no client-ID collisions).
- **No user-ID adoption** — `POST /notes` sets ownership from the authenticated user, so only note/label/item IDs need to survive.
- **Keep the local DB as the server cache**, flipping only after a clean drain (zero dead-letters), then a background reconcile — instant UX with no data-loss window. The doc spells out why "wipe + re-fetch" was rejected for v1.

## Proposed flow

Four phases: authenticate (register) → seed the replay queue from local data in dependency order → drain via existing machinery → flip to server mode on a clean drain + background reconcile. Includes risks, open questions, and a suggested sub-issue breakdown mirroring #511's structure.

## Notes

- **Docs only** — no API, schema, or behavior changes.
- Intended as a review artifact before any implementation PRs.

author: srikarappal
body:
Makes the client pip-installable and PyPI-ready, and renames it to a shorter, on-brand name.

## 1. Fix the broken packaging (it couldn't build at all)

`pip install` failed at wheel build:

```
error: package directory 'thinking_sdk_server' does not exist
```

`pyproject.toml` hardcoded a `packages` list that named a `thinking_sdk_server` directory which isn't in this repo, and omitted the `integrations` subpackage (so even a forced build failed at import with `ModuleNotFoundError`). Switched to find-based discovery so every client subpackage is included and the phantom package is gone.

## 2. Rename `thinking_sdk_client` -> `thinkingsdk`

Shorter, matches the thinkingsdk.ai brand, and drops the redundant "client" (an SDK *is* the client). Now:

```python
pip install thinkingsdk

import thinkingsdk as thinking
thinking.start(api_key="...")
```

Renames the package directory and updates pyproject (name, find pattern, package-data, console scripts, coverage), every internal absolute import, the self-frame filter regex, the integration dotted paths, and the docs.

## Housekeeping
- Untracked committed test bytecode (`tests/__pycache__/*.pyc`) and added a `.gitignore` for build artifacts.

## Verified
- `pip install .` -> `import thinkingsdk` and `import thinkingsdk.integrations` both succeed.
- `python -m build` produces a valid sdist + wheel; `twine check` PASSES both.

`thinkingsdk` is unregistered on PyPI, so this is ready for a clean first release.

body:
## 概要

两条改动:
1. **admin 权限改用 Google 身份白名单**, 删 ADMIN_PASSWORD 机制 (公网部署密码不安全)
2. **统计页玩家 tab 东北麻将模式隐藏段位列, # 列名改成"排名"** (东北麻将没段位)

5 个文件, +125 / -134。

## 一、admin 通过 Google 身份判定

### 老流程的问题
- 后端: \`@Value("\${ADMIN_PASSWORD:}")\` + 每个 endpoint \`@RequestHeader("X-Admin-Password")\` + \`checkPassword\`
- 前端: AdminPage 自己有一个密码登录表单, 输入后存在内存 state, 后续请求都带 \`X-Admin-Password\` 头
- 公网部署: 密码每次进 /admin 都要敲一遍, 而且 secret 是普通环境变量, 暴露面比 OAuth identity 大

### 新流程
- 新增 \`AdminAuthService\`: 读 \`app.admin-emails\` 配置项 (env \`ADMIN_EMAILS\`, CSV 形式), 暴露 \`resolveAdmin(authHeader)\` — 解 Bearer token → 找 Player → 验 email 在白名单
- \`AdminController\` 所有 endpoint 改为接 Authorization 头, \`requireAdmin\` 判失败直接 403
- 删 \`POST /api/admin/login\` (无意义), 删 \`@Value("\${ADMIN_PASSWORD:}")\`
- AdminPage 删整套密码登录 UI, 用 \`localStorage.mahjong_token\` 装 Bearer 头直接拉数据
- 顺手删 AdminPage 顶部 "Deleting a player removes them..." 这行说明 (admin 自己用, 没必要)

### 路由保护
不动 — /admin 仍走 ProtectedRoute, 没登录根本进不来。新流程只是把"已登录用户能不能用 admin 功能"的判定从"输对密码"换成"email 在白名单"。**非 admin 用户即便手动输 /admin URL, 后端 403, 页面空表呈现, 没破坏**。

### 部署
- \`deploy.yml\`: \`-e ADMIN_PASSWORD\` 改成 \`-e ADMIN_EMAILS\`
- **合并前**: 在 GitHub repo secrets 加 \`ADMIN_EMAILS\`
- **合并后**: 旧的 \`ADMIN_PASSWORD\` secret 没人读, 可以从 GH secrets 删掉

## 二、StatsPage 玩家 tab 修复

统计 → 玩家 → 切到东北麻将, 段位列显示 UNRANKED / 空状态是误导, 因为东北麻将根本没有段位系统。改两件事:

- 表头 \`#\` → \`排名\` (跟数据语义对齐, 是按当前模式排序的名次, 不是数据库 id)
- 段位列 (header + cell) 用 \`gameMode !== 'DONGBEI'\` 条件渲染, 东北模式下整列消失, 表收缩成 4 列

## 测试要点

**admin**:
- [ ] 部署前在 GitHub repo secrets 配 \`ADMIN_EMAILS=<你的 Google 邮箱>\`
- [ ] 用配置的 admin 邮箱 Google 登录后, 浏览器直接输 \`/admin\`: 页面不再弹密码表单, 直接显示 Players / Sessions / Settings
- [ ] 用**非** admin 邮箱 Google 登录后访问 \`/admin\`: 页面 load 完后表都是空 (后端 403), 但页面不崩
- [ ] admin 编辑 userName / 删 player / 删 session / 改 settings / tier backfill 都能跑
- [ ] 退出登录后访问 \`/admin\`: ProtectedRoute 跳 /login

**stats**:
- [ ] 统计 → 玩家 → 选东北麻将: 表头变成 排名 / 用户名 / 姓名 / 注册日期, 段位列消失
- [ ] 统计 → 玩家 → 选国标: 表头是 排名 / 用户名 / 姓名 / 段位 / 注册日期, 段位列正常显示
- [ ] 统计 → 玩家 → 选立直: 同国标

## 文件改动

- \`server/.../service/AdminAuthService.java\` — 新增, 白名单解析 + Bearer token 解析
- \`server/.../controller/AdminController.java\` — 删密码机制, 切 Bearer token, 删 /login endpoint
- \`server/.../resources/application.yml\` — 加 app.admin-emails 配置项
- \`ui/src/pages/AdminPage.tsx\` — 删密码表单, 用 token 鉴权
- \`ui/src/pages/StatsPage.tsx\` — 玩家 tab 段位列条件渲染, # → 排名
- \`.github/workflows/deploy.yml\` — ADMIN_PASSWORD → ADMIN_EMAILS

author: dacort
body:
## The bug

Every Codex worker was dying immediately with:

```
400 invalid_request_error: The 'gpt-5.3-codex' model is not supported
when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
```

`worker/entrypoint.sh` invoked `codex exec` with **no `--model` flag**, so it inherited the codex CLI's built-in default. That default drifts across migrations (`gpt-5-codex → gpt-5.3-codex → gpt-5.4 → …`, visible in the local `~/.codex/config.toml` migration notice) and lands on models the ChatGPT subscription doesn't expose.

Combined with a separately-expired auth token (refreshed out-of-band), **the Codex agent had been silently dead** — nothing in the system noticed until a review task tried to use it.

## Fix

Pin an explicit, supported model, configurable without an image rebuild:

- `controller/dispatcher`: inject `CODEX_MODEL` on codex jobs (mirrors `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), defaulting to `gpt-5.5`, overridable via the controller's `CODEX_MODEL` env — so the next migration is a one-line GitOps change in talos-homelab, not a code change.
- `worker/entrypoint.sh`: `codex exec --model "${CODEX_MODEL:-gpt-5.5}" …`
- tests: assert `CODEX_MODEL` is set on codex jobs + `codexModel()` env override.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./dispatcher/...`, `go test ./...` all green (controller module); `bash -n worker/entrypoint.sh` clean.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The real gap is that **nothing health-checks the agents**. A periodic per-agent smoke test (ask each agent to echo "ok", file an issue on failure) would have caught *both* this model bug and the expired token days before a human hit them. Worth its own capture.

author: junkovich
body:
## What

Adds a flat `just` task graph as the single canonical definition of the repo's format, lint, test, and build commands: a root `justfile` plus four sibling modules (`js.just`, `rust.just`, `infra.just`, `docs.just`). Aggregates `check`/`lint`/`fmt`/`test`/`build` fan out to per-plane recipes via cross-module dependencies.

## Why

The same tool invocations are duplicated across `ci.yml`, the `.husky/` hooks, and `lint-staged.config.js`, with no single place that defines "lint the repo". A change to one surface can silently diverge from the others. This creates the DRY source that later hook and CI wiring consume.

## Scope

Purely additive. No edits to `ci.yml`, `.husky/`, or `lint-staged.config.js`, so nothing consumes the graph yet and the rollback is deleting the new files. One supporting edit normalizes `--max-warnings 0` into the frontend `stylelint` npm script so the recipe delegates without drifting from CI.

## Design notes

- Recipes reproduce the exact tool invocations from CI / hooks / lint-staged. JS-plane tools delegate via `npm run` / `npx --no-install` (node-local, not on PATH); rust + infra use bare binaries (image-baked). The asymmetry is intentional, per tool distribution model.
- `fmt` recipes WRITE; verification lives in `*-check` / `check`, so no aggregate mutates the tree.
- Each module repeats `set shell := ["bash","-ueo","pipefail","-c"]` (just settings do not propagate into submodules).
- DB-backed and server-backed recipes (`rust::test`, `rust::doctests`, `rust::sqlx-check`, `js::a11y`) are excluded from the local aggregates; they ride CI.

## Tests

`scripts/just-selftest.sh` is the mandated test: minimum-version guard, recipe-presence assertions, per-file canonical-format check, and a fail-fast negative case that stubs a system-PATH tool (`cargo`, `shellcheck`) and asserts the recipe aborts. JS-plane tools resolve via `node_modules/.bin` not PATH, so they are covered transitively rather than PATH-stubbed.

Locally verified green: `just check` (full fan-out), `js::lint`, `js::fmt-check`, `infra::lint`, `rust::{fmt-check,clippy,doc-lint,drift}`, `docs::build`, `docs::links`, and the self-test (including negatives).

author: nesquena-hermes
body:
## Salvage of #4113 by @gkd2323c — image-routing divergence fix

Ports the corrected image-routing fix from #4113 (@gkd2323c) fresh onto `master`, with an additional carve-out the original PR was missing.

### The bug (real, still in master)
`api/streaming.py:_resolve_image_input_mode(cfg)` was a **local re-implementation** of `agent/image_routing.py:decide_image_input_mode` that had **diverged** from the canonical function. The local copy never consulted the active model's vision capability — it only checked a handful of config heuristics — so for a model **known to lack vision** it still returned `"native"`, embedding the upload as an `image_url` part and silently sending pixels to a blind model (a #21160-class failure) instead of routing through the text (`vision_analyze`) pipeline.

### The fix
Delegate to the canonical `agent.image_routing.decide_image_input_mode` (single source of truth) with a `try/except` fallback that preserves historical WebUI behaviour when the `agent` package is unavailable (e.g. the WebUI standalone test environment).

### The carve-out (preserved)
The canonical router conservatively returns `"text"` for **unknown/custom models** (no models.dev capability data). WebUI historically forwards those **natively** and relies on the agent's strip-and-retry guard (`_try_shrink_image_parts_in_messages` / `_strip_images_from_messages`) to downgrade on a provider rejection. We keep that: a canonical `"text"` verdict is only honoured when there's a real signal —

- an explicit user choice (`agent.image_input_mode: text`, or a configured `auxiliary.vision` backend), **or**
- a model **known** to lack vision (`supports_vision == False`).

Otherwise we forward native. This is the piece the original #4113 didn't have — a pure full-delegation would have regressed the WebUI native-forwarding behaviour that the gateway test encodes.

### Tests
- Existing `test_gateway_chat_worker_forwards_image_attachments_as_multimodal_parts` **stays green** — an unknown `"test-model"` still forwards native.
- **New non-vacuous regression** `test_resolve_image_input_mode_known_text_only_routes_text`: a model **known** to be text-only now routes `"text"`. This **fails against master** (the old local copy returns `"native"` for the same config) and passes with the fix.
- Added coverage for the unknown-model carve-out, the known-vision native path, explicit-text-signal precedence, and the agent-unavailable fallback.

### Validation
- `tests/test_webui_gateway_chat_backend.py` (gateway image test + 5 new): **pass**
- Activity-stream regression gate: **all layers pass**
- Full suite: **10806 passed**, 4 failed — all 4 are pre-existing known flakes (cron_profile_context ×2, TLS-fallback, sessiondb_fd_leak idempotent), unrelated to image routing.

Credit to @gkd2323c for the original #4113.

author: karajanchang
body:
## Summary

An opt-in `--auto-reads` flag: when a tool-approval (HITL) fires for a `bash` tool whose command is unambiguously **read-only** (`cat`, `ls`, `grep`, `git status`, …), the cli auto-approves it (no prompt) and tags the card `[read · auto]`. Writes and anything uncertain still prompt. Kills approval fatigue for the common read-heavy case without weakening the gate on writes.

```
✔ bash cat Cargo.toml · 8ms        [read · auto]
✔ bash grep -rn foo src/ · 12ms    [read · auto]
◐ bash rm -rf target/ · …          [y] approve  [a] always  [n] deny
      ↑ only writes still prompt
```

## How it works

- **`--auto-reads`** (default OFF) → `App.auto_reads`. In the `StreamMsg::Hitl` arm: `read_auto = auto_reads && tool_name == "bash" && is_readonly_bash(tool_input["command"])`, OR'd into the existing auto-approve condition. Default-off is byte-identical to today (the `&&` short-circuits).
- **`bash_class::is_readonly_bash`** — a conservative classifier: `true` only for a single simple command (no shell metacharacters) whose head is in a read-only allowlist, with guards for `find` (no `-delete`/`-exec`/`-fprint`…) and `git` (read-only subcommands only). Fail-safe: anything it can't prove read-only → `false` → normal prompt.
- The card is tagged `[read · auto]` so every auto-approval stays visible in the transcript.

## Why opt-in + conservative (the design constraint)

MUR's cli HITL is **post-hoc** — the runtime runs the tool, *then* asks. So `--auto-reads` can never widen what *executes*; it only skips an after-the-fact prompt. Still: default OFF, a conservative classifier, and every auto-approval visible (note + tag) — consistent with the project's "autonomous needs a safety lens" stance.

## Security: adversarial review of the classifier

The classifier got a dedicated **adversarial pass** that tried to break it — and found **8 real holes**: commands that write/exec with *plain arguments* (no shell metacharacter, so the metachar gate couldn't catch them):

| Bypass | Why it's not read-only |
|---|---|
| `env rm -rf x` | `env` execs its argv — **arbitrary command execution** |
| `sort -o FILE`, `uniq IN OUT`, `xxd IN OUT`, `tree -o FILE` | write a file via a plain positional/flag arg |
| `find . -fprint/-fprintf/-fls FILE` | `find` write family not in the guard |
| `git reflog expire` | destructive reflog prune |
| `date -s …`, `hostname NAME` | mutate system state |

All fixed (commit `71022264`): those heads removed from the allowlist, `reflog` dropped, the `find` guard extended, and **all 14 bypass strings locked in as regression tests**. The invariant is now clean — every allowlisted head is read-only for *all* arguments (`find`/`git` the only guarded exceptions).

## Review

Final opus review: **READY TO MERGE** — 0 Critical / 0 Important. Verified the read lane (bash-only, missing/non-string command → no auto-approve, default-off byte-identical), the classifier still hardened, the card tag truthful, and the post-hoc honesty (a misclassified write would already have run regardless of the answer — observability loss, not new execution, and it's tagged). The one actionable Minor — `--auto-reads` silently no-op'd in plain/multiplex modes — is fixed (warning added, matching `--budget-usd`).

- `cargo clippy -p mur-core -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `bash_class` 5/5 (reads → true, 14 bypasses → false); cli suite 122/122; `cargo test --no-run` clean (no E0027 — every `Cli` destructure carries the new field).

## Not yet live-verified

Reviewed + unit-tested. Not yet driven in a terminal against a real ask-policy agent.

## Deferred (Minor)

- `--auto-reads` enforced only in the interactive TUI (plain/multiplex now *warn*; threading the read lane into plain mode's own `[y/a/n]` prompt is a fast follow).
- No direct unit test of the read-lane wiring (the `mur` binary's test module stack-overflows in the local harness; the E0027 `--no-run` guard covers the real compile concern).

## Out of scope (ponytail)

A `/auto-reads` live toggle; classifying non-`bash` tools; a user-configurable allowlist.

## Docs

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-28-agent-cli-auto-reads.md`.

author: ajju2255-netizen
body:
## Trust Phase — P0 #1 and #2

**Confidence is separate from the grade.** The grade says how *good* a lead is; confidence says how much we actually *know*. A thin lead (name + phone + email ≈ 30%) now reads as **"not enough info yet — enrich it,"** not "bad lead." This is the reframe that solves the thin-CSV trust problem.

### What's shown (lead detail → Lead Score card)
- **Confidence meter** — 0–100% + band (high/moderate/low/very low), color-toned.
- **Needs Enrichment** card when confidence < 50% — plain-English reason + a missing-field checklist (`+ Company`, `+ Role`, `+ Location`, …) ordered by accuracy impact, so the user knows exactly what to add for the biggest gain.

### How confidence is computed
Weighted data-completeness over the fields that actually drive scoring accuracy: company (22), role (18), location (12), inquiry (10), email (10), budget (8), over a name+phone (20) floor. Derived on the fly — **no schema change, no migration.**

### Verification
- `next lint` clean · `tsc` clean · full `next build` succeeds.
- 100/100 scoring tests (incl. 5 new for confidence).
- Visually verified: rich lead → "High confidence 100%"; stripped lead → "Very low confidence 20% · Needs Enrichment" with the checklist.

### Note
`industry`/`website` aren't stored columns today, so confidence is grounded in real fields. Adding those as explicit enrichment targets would be a small future migration.

Part of the Trust → Intelligence roadmap. Next P0: Recommendation Adoption (North Star) — needs a migration + a definition alignment.

Round-2 MEDIUM (sandbox→host reach). The loopback-rewrite mapped loopback host tokens to host.docker.internal (+host-gateway) so the sandbox can reach a host-local target. `0.0.0.0` was in the set — but it's never a legit connect target (use localhost/127.0.0.1; the platform rejects it as non-public) and is a classic SSRF-bypass token, so including it only extended the host reach.

body: ## Summary Brings the training harness in line with the README's WhyLeNet design and adds a pytest suite that verifies the network can train on MNIST. ## README alignment - **`digit_to_image_differentiable`**: einsum blend of a 10-way distribution with the MNIST digit bank - **`get_unit`**: differentiable decimal-place extraction (with proper `position_weight` scaling and soft digit lookup) - **Five LeNet-1 partials per neuron**: hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, hundredths — each outputs an expected digit via `sum(probs * DIGITS)` instead of argmax - **Scalar composition**: `N = 100*a + 10*b + c + 0.1*d + 0.01*e`, clamped to `[0, 999.99]` - **Image re-synthesis**: each decimal place is converted back to a 28×28 digit image and stacked into a 5-channel block for downstream layers - **LeNet-1 style MiniLeNet**: smaller conv head (4→8 channels) consistent with the README's parameter budget note ## Tests - `tests/test_train_whylennet.py` checks helper shapes, WhyNeuron 5-channel output, and that loss decreases over two epochs on a 128-sample MNIST subset (downloads MNIST automatically) - Added `requirements.txt` with `torch`, `torchvision`, and `pytest` ## Remaining README TODOs (unchanged) The README still marks `WhyFC()` and the full `WhyLenet()` conv stack as TODO. body:
## Adapt every runnable ACP-registry agent (+20)

Drops a manifest for **every remaining registry agent that can run** under a relaxed bar:
> the agent only needs to **install + launch its ACP server headlessly in a benchflow task env**. Routing the model through BenchFlow's gateway and capturing the raw LLM are **not** required — an agent that runs on its own/vendor backend (or needs a vendor key at eval time) qualifies, as long as its ACP server launches headlessly.

Adds a **`RUNNABLE`** tier to `catalog.py` (distinct from `WIRED`): installs + launches + handshakes headlessly, but the model is **not** gateway-enforced — executable, not a faithful model-controlled eval.

### New tally (of 36)
**wired 13 · runnable 14 · native 6 · catalog 1 · vendor-locked 1 · out-of-scope 1** — so **33 of 36 are runnable-or-better** (13 wired + 14 runnable + 6 native).

### How each was verified (hermetic, no real-model spend)
`acp_smoke.mjs` installs each agent headlessly, launches its ACP server, and drives `initialize → session/new → session/prompt` against the deterministic mock. **`initialize` + `session/new` OK == RUNNABLE**; **also reaching the mock (`upstreamRequests ≥ 1`) == WIRED**.

**+6 promoted to WIRED** (also routed to the mock; npx/binary) — several were *assumed* blocked but the smoke found headless config paths:

| agent | dist | smoke |
|---|---|---:|
| stakpak | binary | 2 req |
| grok-build | binary | 3 req |
| dimcode | npx | 2 req |
| glm-acp-agent | npx | 2 req |
| codebuddy-code | npx | 4 req |
| github-copilot-cli | npx | 2 req |

**+14 RUNNABLE** (install + handshake headless; own/vendor backend or uvx): `fast-agent` + `minion-code` (uvx; *also* routed but outside the npx-or-binary wired policy), `nova` (anthropic-messages/Claude-only), `sigit` (**local GGUF — no key, no cloud**), `cline`, `junie`, `poolside`, `amp-acp`, `auggie`, `factory-droid`, `qoder`, `cortex-code`, `corust-agent`, `autohand`.

**Blocked headless** (smoke-confirmed, no manifest): `kimi` (`kimi acp` mandates interactive OAuth; `session/new` → -32000), `cursor` (`session/new` → -32603; only auth is `cursor_login` browser OAuth). **Out-of-scope:** `agoragentic` (not an LLM agent).

### Honesty notes
- `RUNNABLE` ≠ a faithful eval — the model isn't gateway-enforced; vendor-backed agents (qoder, auggie, factory-droid, cortex, corust, amp) need their vendor creds at eval time to complete a task. The manifest is the adapter; benchflow can create the task env and launch them.
- Catalog deviations recorded honestly: dimcode kept **npx** (its npm distribution), `bin_name` added for binary-wired entries, github-copilot's `launch_env` moved into its launcher (npx-wired forbids `launch_env`).
- `acp-registry` tests: **86 passed**; all 20 manifests load. `test_register_subset_rejects_non_wired` updated `stakpak`→`kimi` (stakpak is now wired; kimi stays the lone catalog entry).

`ai-sdk` (5 harnesses) + `omnigent` (1) are already adapted in their own paths — unchanged here.

author: grapebaba
body:
## Summary

Part 1 for #406 

- **block_state_cache** — `FIFOBlockStateCache` port: a head-pinned FIFO over recent post-states keyed by state root. Keeps two structures — an insertion-ordered map (so `getSeedState` returns a *stable* reload anchor that doesn't churn when the head moves) and a head-pinned FIFO key order (so eviction takes the oldest tail and never the current head). Per-`add` pruning, with the just-added key protected so `max_states == 1` transiently holds one extra. Read-tracking metrics (size / reads / seconds-since-last-read).
- **cp_datastore** — the checkpoint-state byte datastore the persistent checkpoint cache persists to. Two backends behind a vtable: `File` (the file backend fans batch removal out over `io.async`) and an in-memory `Map` fake for tests. `removeMany` stays in the interface so each backend picks its own strategy (concurrent fan-out for I/O, sequential for the non-thread-safe map).
- **key** — checkpoint ⇄ datastore-key (`0x`-hex filename) encoding.
- **metrics** — block state-cache metric definitions.

## O que entra (11 tarefas TDD)

- **domain:** `IsoKind` (isohybrid vs unsupported).
- **application:** erros `IsoError`/`WriteError`; tipos `WriteState`/`WriteProgress`/`WritePhase`/`WriteRequest`/`IsoSelection`/`CancelFlag`/`ProgressSink`; portas `IsoInspector`/`BootableWriter`/`UiCommands`; `UiState` estendido (defaults); caso de uso `CreateBootable` (classifica → grava; bloqueia `Unsupported`).
- **infrastructure:** `IsoFileInspector` (detecção isohybrid por setores, Rust puro); **`RawCopier`** (cópia + verificação sobre IO genérico — o núcleo testável); `Udisks2BlockWriter` (fd via `Block.OpenDevice`/polkit, **sem `unsafe`** — `File::from(OwnedFd)`); `RfdIsoPicker` (diálogo nativo).
- **app:** `AppCommands` + `LiveUiState` estendido (ponte tokio→egui para `write_state`/`selected_iso`, espelhando a Fase 3).
- **ui:** religada ao estado real — barra de progresso real, fases, aviso de ISO não-suportada, comandos pick/start/cancel; **removida toda a simulação** (`tick`/`Phase`/`progress`).

## Decisões (do brainstorming)

Um único PR · udisks2 `OpenDevice` (GUI nunca como root) · verificar sempre · só modo Boot (Formatar fica para depois) · detecção simples (isohybrid sim/não, bloqueia o resto com aviso honesto).

- `cargo test --workspace` (37 testes) ✅ · `clippy -D warnings` ✅ · `fmt` ✅ · `xtask check` (≤199 linhas, zero campos `pub`) ✅ · `cargo deny` (licenses ok; zbus/rfd sem licença bloqueante) ✅

O núcleo testável (`RawCopier`), a detecção, o use case e a UI estão validados automaticamente. **Não** foi possível validar em CI/sessão a gravação real ponta-a-ponta:

author: tas50
body:
## Summary

`ChefSpec::Coverage#report!` computed the coverage percentage as:

```ruby
h[:coverage] = ((h[:touched] / h[:total].to_f) * 100).round(2)
```

When a run collects **no resources** (`total == 0`), that's `0 / 0.0`, which evaluates to `NaN`. The bundled human ERB template guards display with `if @total == 0`, so it's invisible there — but the `NaN` still lands in the `report` hash and is handed to every registered output, including JSON and any programmatic consumer.

## Fix

Extract the calculation into a private `coverage_percentage(touched, total)` helper that returns `0.0` when there are no resources, and use it in `report!`. `0.0` (rather than `100.0`) is the least-surprising value for "nothing was collected."

## Testing

- Added `spec/unit/coverage_spec.rb` (TDD — verified it failed first) covering the zero-resources case (`0.0`, not `NaN`), a normal percentage, and rounding.
- `bundle exec rspec spec/unit/` → `165 examples, 0 failures`.
- `cookstyle --chefstyle -c .rubocop.yml` → no offenses.

## Note

Adds `spec/unit/coverage_spec.rb`, which #44 also adds (there it covers `Coverage::ResourceWrapper`). Whichever merges first, the other just needs the two `describe` blocks combined into the one file.

author: bartok9
body:
## Summary

- `BrowserScraper` (Selenium) routed pages to its PDF handler with `self.url.endswith(".pdf")`, which missed PDFs behind a query string/fragment and uppercase `.PDF`.
- Such links silently fell through to HTML scraping and returned non-PDF garbage.

## Motivation

Signed CDN/S3 PDF links almost always carry a signature query string (`https://host/report.pdf?sig=...&exp=...`), and uppercase `.PDF` is a valid suffix. The bare suffix check failed on both, so the browser scraper never invoked `scrape_pdf_with_pymupdf` for them.

This mirrors the same class of bug already fixed for `Scraper.get_scraper` in #1828 — but the `BrowserScraper` path is independent and was untouched.

## Fix

Extracted a small `_is_pdf_url(url)` helper that inspects only `urlparse(url).path`, lowercased, before checking the `.pdf` suffix. The scrape path now calls it instead of `endswith`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `endswith(".pdf")` returns `False` for `doc.pdf?sig=x` and `R.PDF`.

**Real environment:** Python 3.14, repo `master`, local venv.

**Exact commands run after the patch:**
```
python -m pytest tests/test_browser_pdf_detection.py -q
```

**Captured output AFTER fix:**
```
7 passed, 2 warnings in 0.34s
```

**Pre-fix demonstration (old logic):**
```
query: False   # https://cdn/doc.pdf?sig=x  -> should be a PDF
upper: False   # https://x/R.PDF            -> should be a PDF
```

**Regression test:** `tests/test_browser_pdf_detection.py` — asserts query-string, fragment, and uppercase PDFs are detected and that a `.pdf` appearing only in a query param is NOT. Fails without the fix.

## Scope / risk

Pure detection helper; only the browser scrape branch changed. Non-PDF and plain `.pdf` behavior unchanged.

## What

A column marked `mdOnly` collapses to zero width below the `md` breakpoint (paired with the existing `hidden md:table-cell` on its cells), so responsive behaviour stays intact and the remaining columns refill.

author: gourabsingha1
body:
## Description

Closes #1487

Per RFC 7230, HTTP header names are case-insensitive. Previously, `FunctionsClient.invoke()` checked whether a `Content-Type` header was provided using exact string match: `!headers.containsKey("Content-Type")`.

If a caller passed a custom content-type header with lowercase or mixed casing (such as `headers: {'content-type': 'application/custom+json'}`), the check failed to detect it. Consequently, the default content-type for the body type was assigned to `finalHeaders['Content-Type']`, overwriting the caller's custom header when headers were set on the request.

## Fix

Switched the check to a case-insensitive lookup over `finalHeaders.keys` before setting default body content types.

## Test Plan

Added a unit test in `packages/functions_client/test/functions_dart_test.dart` verifying that passing `headers: {'content-type': 'application/custom+json'}` correctly overrides default headers. All 37 tests in the package pass.

## What
Adds a permanent 301 redirect `/blog/6-month-revenue-report → /blog` to `BLOG_REDIRECTS` (wired through `next.config.ts`).

## Why
The dev.to repost (article `3513508`) carries `canonical_url = https://aversusb.net/blog/6-month-revenue-report`. That page **404s** because CML excluded it from on-site publication (confidential revenue figures). Google currently sees a canonical pointing at a dead 404.

This resolves the leak **without dev.to API access** (DAN-158 holds only an OAuth secret, no DEV Community API key).

author: alexadewit
body:
## Summary

Red-teaming register **#7** (mirror-write credential as a standing privilege) confirmed the worker is a high-value but **well-designed** trust boundary, and surfaced one control its mitigation didn't name: **the mirror queue is co-equal to the write token.**

A `MirrorJob` is unauthenticated data (`Queue.hs` — no signature) and the worker verifies fetched bytes against **the digest the job carries**, with no upstream re-fetch (`Worker.hs`). So it cannot distinguish a gate-produced job from a forged one, which makes **queue-send access equivalent to trusted-write access** — the same blast radius as the mint token. The control is the same flavour as the write-token IAM: **isolate and manage queue access at the infrastructure level** (only the serve role enqueues, only the worker consumes). Message signing is **deliberately not used** — for an internal single-producer/single-consumer queue the standard pattern is to control access, not message authenticity, and signing would add shared-secret/key-rotation burden for marginal gain over correct IAM.

Also credited a verified mitigating factor: the worker is **hash-only** (`verifyIntegrity` runs `hashlazy` over the raw bytes; no decompression or tarball parsing), so a malicious artifact is a poor code-execution vector.

With the queue expectation formalized, **#7 → Mitigated** (residual: operator IAM correctness + the role's bounded blast radius — operator-owned, like the edge).

- `threat-modelling/ecluse.json`: #7 Open → Mitigated; mitigation names the queue as a co-equal IAM-controlled boundary and credits the hash-only worker.
- `USAGE.md` Golden Path step 3: scope the mirror queue (`SendMessage` to the serve role, `ReceiveMessage`/delete to the worker).
- `security.md`: the #7 essay names the queue alongside the write token.

Register validated `jq` + `ajv`: **15 threats / 5 Open / 9 Mitigated / 1 NA**.

## In plain terms

Écluse's background "mirror worker" is the one component that can write into your trusted registry, so it's a sensitive spot. The good news: it's well-built — it only *hashes* the files it fetches (no risky unpacking), uses a short-lived write-only credential, and never follows redirects.

The one thing we made explicit: the worker takes its instructions from a **queue**, and those queued instructions aren't signed. So whoever can put a message on that queue can tell the worker to fetch-and-publish something — meaning the queue is just as sensitive as the write credential itself. The fix is the normal cloud practice you'd use anyway: **lock the queue down with IAM** so only Écluse's front-end can put messages on it and only the worker can take them off. We deliberately *don't* cryptographically sign queue messages — for a simple one-sender/one-reader internal queue that isn't the industry norm, and it would add key-rotation overhead for little benefit over just controlling access. With that written into the operator guide, this threat is marked handled.

Docs and threat-model only — **no code changes**.

body:
> **Depends on [#2388](https://github.com/cloudflare/vinext/pull/2388)** — this extends the 5000-route scenario that PR adds, so merge it first (or merge this directly; its diff already includes that commit).

## What

Adds **Next.js (Turbopack)** as a second implementation of the **"Production build time (5000 routes)"** scenario from [#2388](https://github.com/cloudflare/vinext/pull/2388), via a new `benchmarks/nextjs-large` fixture — so the dashboard records how vinext and Turbopack compare *at scale*, not only at the default ~33 routes.

- `benchmarks/nextjs-large/` — a Turbopack fixture mirroring `benchmarks/nextjs` (same Next.js version/config), built at 5000 routes.
- `scenarios.json` — adds the `nextjs-large` setup (npm install + 5000-route generate) and a `Next.js` implementation on `production-build-large`.
- `build-time.mjs` — accepts `nextjs-large` (built with `next build --turbopack`, like `nextjs`).

## Why

The headline dashboard compares the two at ~33 routes, where vinext builds ~31.5% faster than Turbopack. That lead is **not constant — it widens with route count.** Local, same machine, median of 3 clean production builds (total wall-clock):

| Scale | vinext | Next.js (Turbopack) | vinext faster |
| --- | --: | --: | :-: |
| 33 routes | 2.6 s | 5.1 s | **1.95×** |
| 5,033 routes | 20.2 s | 106.0 s | **5.26×** |

Marginal cost per added route ≈ **3.5 ms (vinext)** vs **20 ms (Turbopack)**. The 33-route dashboard number understates vinext's advantage for realistic app sizes; recording the 5000-route comparison surfaces it.

## Cost — the tradeoff to weigh

**Main-runs only.** Like the default Next.js benchmark, the Turbopack side is skipped on pull requests (it runs on `main`, or when its inputs change), so **PR CI is unaffected.** The cost is ~**+100 s** on each `main` perf run for the 5000-route Turbopack build. vinext's own 5000-route build (~20 s) already runs via [#2388](https://github.com/cloudflare/vinext/pull/2388).

If the signal isn't worth the `main` minutes, feel free to close this — the vinext-only 5000-route scenario from [#2388](https://github.com/cloudflare/vinext/pull/2388) stands on its own.

## ⚠️ CI wiring needed (for a maintainer)

Same as [#2388](https://github.com/cloudflare/vinext/pull/2388): `perf.yml` doesn't know about the new fixture. To run green it needs the `benchmarks/nextjs` treatment applied to `benchmarks/nextjs-large`:

- **`grant_write_paths`** — add `benchmarks/nextjs-large` to `project_roots`, and `benchmarks/nextjs-large/{.next,node_modules}` to `paths`.
- **"Validate performance workspace paths"** — add `benchmarks/nextjs-large` (+ `app`/`.next`) to the checks.
- **PR skip** — the "Detect Next.js benchmark input changes" step sets `VINEXT_PERF_SKIP_IMPLEMENTATIONS=nextjs`; it should also skip `nextjs-large` (and add it to the `--implementation` allowlist) so PRs don't measure it without setup. Inputs share the same Next.js version as `nextjs`, so the same fingerprint / fork-PR guard applies.
