author: oofdere
body:
## Soundness issue

`Sequence::pop` computes the trailing position via `self.tokens.len() as i32`:

```rust
pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<i32> {
    let len = self.tokens.len() as i32;
    if len == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    if self.kv_remove((len - 1)..len) {
        ...
    }
}
```

Once `self.tokens.len()` exceeds `i32::MAX`, the `as` cast silently wraps to a negative `llama_pos`. llama.cpp's `llama_memory_seq_rm` treats `-1` as the "from start / to end" sentinel (see `llama.h`), so a wrapped position that lands on `-1` silently clears the **entire** sequence's KV cache instead of just the trailing token. Other wrapped values are interpreted as arbitrary signed positions, which the C side dereferences as cache indices — undefined behaviour reachable from purely safe Rust.

There's a parallel hole in the early-return check: if `tokens.len() == 2^32`, then `tokens.len() as i32 == 0` and `pop` silently returns `None` on a non-empty sequence (no KV mutation, but the user observes a phantom "empty" state and the on-disk `tokens` vec drifts from the KV cache).

## Fix

Replace the bare cast with `i32::try_from(...).unwrap_or_else(panic!(...))`, mirroring the shape adopted in #147 for `Sequence::push`. Safe Rust may panic on overflow, but it cannot pass an undefined value across the FFI boundary. The early-exit `len == 0` check is rewritten as `self.tokens.is_empty()` so the second wrap path (`len wraps to 0` on a non-empty vec) is also closed.

## Not a duplicate

I went through every open soundness PR. The closest neighbours target distinct surfaces:

- **#147** guards `Sequence::push` against the same `usize → i32` cast. Same shape of bug, different method — this PR is the matching fix on the `pop` side. Diffs are orthogonal and either merge order is fine.
- **#135** modifies `Sequence::decode` to clear the KV slot before re-decoding the trailing position. Different concern (logical post-pop refresh) and different method; does not touch `pop`.
- **#129** bounds-checks the `range` argument to `Sequence::remove` and `Sequence::copy_to` against `self.tokens.len()`. Different argument (caller-supplied range vs. trailing position) and different methods.
- **#126** bounds-checks `Sequence::kv_shift`. Different method.
- **#123**, **#138** validate `Sequence::kv_copy`. Different methods.
- Every other open soundness PR targets `Sampler` (NaN / double-apply), `Model` / `vocab` (bounds-check token), `Context::new` (`n_seq_max`), `Backend` (init/free race, constructor sealing), or doc/test-only changes.

No prior or in-flight PR validates the `usize → i32` conversion on `Sequence::pop`.

## Test plan

A new test target `tests/sequence_pop_pos_overflow.rs` pins the regression:

- `pop_on_empty_sequence_returns_none` — early-return path still returns `None`.
- `pop_returns_last_pushed_token_and_shrinks` — happy path: pops the last token, invalidates logits, decreases `len()`.
- `pop_to_empty_then_pop_again_returns_none` — drains a sequence and confirms `pop` keeps returning `None`.
- `i32_try_from_rejects_value_just_past_i32_max` — pure-logic check that pins the conversion shape the guard relies on, so a future refactor that re-introduces `as i32` will trip this test.

Driving the >2 GiB overflow path directly isn't realistic in CI, so the regression coverage follows the same split that #147 used: end-to-end happy-path tests plus a pinned `try_from` shape test. Tests are placed in their own target because the pre-existing `tests/sequence.rs` doesn't compile on this branch (it still references the removed `SamplerChain` API from the "native sampler wip" refactor).

## Retour utilisateur
> « si t'es malvoyant c'est quand même compliqué d'arriver jusqu'au bouton ? »

Vrai problème : il fallait **trouver** le bouton « 🔊 Écouter » pour démarrer, puis le **retrouver** pour arrêter.

## Causes & correctifs

### 1. La barre flottante d'arrêt ne s'affichait jamais (bug)
La barre fixe en bas `#tts-bar` (⏸ Pause / ⏹ Arrêter) avait un `style="display:none"` **inline** qui écrasait `.tts-bar.visible{display:flex}`. → Retiré (le CSS gère déjà caché/visible). Désormais, **pendant toute lecture, une barre fixe en bas** permet d'arrêter **sans scroller ni chercher**.

### 2. Lecture automatique à l'ouverture
Dans `renderActuDetail`, si la **lecture vocale est activée** (`_ttsEnabled`, même drapeau que MEL), l'actualité est **lue automatiquement** à l'ouverture → plus besoin de trouver le bouton pour démarrer.

### 3. Lecteurs d'écran
- `openOv` (`js/mat-core.js`) pose `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` sur les overlays.
- Le focus est porté sur le **titre `<h2>`** du détail à l'ouverture → l'article est annoncé/lu par le lecteur d'écran (les personnes aveugles utilisent leur propre synthèse).

## Versions
Bumps `?v=` (`mat-core` 4.2.21, `mat-actus` 4.4.8), cache SW **mat-v4.42.2**, changelog **v4.40.2**, doc `guide-utilisateur` §10.

## Validation
- Barre : `display` par défaut `none` → `flex` via `.visible` (vérifié) ;
- `openOv` applique `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"` (vérifié) ;
- `node --check` JS OK ; E2E existants (Échap, axe) inchangés.

author: tsyma
body:
Follow-up to #82, which was **squash-merged early** — only the first commit (the DSP tone-stack stage) landed in `main`, and it carries a **Windows build regression**. This PR fixes that and adds everything that came after.

## 🔴 Fix: MSVC 1 MB stack (main is currently broken on Windows)
`#82` merged `teq::EqEngine` as a **by-value** member of `cab::AmpEq` → `CabEngine` → the processor. `teq::EqEngine` is ~**200 KB** (a fixed 24-band bank), and `tools/dsp-test` stack-allocates the processor. On MSVC's **1 MB** main-thread stack (macOS = 8 MB) that overflows at construction → the *Integration DSP tests* CI step crashes before `main` (**exit 127**). Fix: hold the engine on the **heap** (`unique_ptr`, built in `prepare()`); the embedder keeps only a pointer. Still RT-safe (`process()` never allocates). Verified on Windows CI (workflow_dispatch, all green) and locally under `ulimit -s 1024`.

## Adds (all post-#82, never merged)
- **Editor UI** for the amp-EQ: a revealed row between the PREAMP and POWERAMP rows, toggled by an "AMP EQ" checkbox. Six knobs — Bass / Mid / Treble / Presence (double-click → 0 dB) + HPF / LPF (the enable toggle is the caption). Compact knobs on the left, the live curve fills the rest.
- **Live response curve** (`ui/EqCurve.h`) via `teq::EqEngine::magnitudeDbFor()` from a `cab::AmpEq::describe()` snapshot — the same mapping the audio path applies. Fills to the 0 dB shelf; roll-offs run off the graph; vertical dashed guides at each active band's frequency.
- **Perf badge** (`ui/PerfBadge.h`) next to the version: latency (samples + ms; PDC the plugin already reports) + a single-core DSP-load % (monotonic-clock wall-clock per stage, RT-safe, EMA-smoothed). Click → a CallOutBox with the per-stage breakdown (Preamp / EQ / Poweramp / Cab + Total).

## Verification
- Core unit tests: **484 checks, 0 failures** (incl. the 5 `AmpEq` tests).
- Integration `dsp_test` passes, incl. under a forced 1 MB stack.
- Plugin builds VST3 + AU + CLAP + Standalone (macOS); Windows CI green on the branch tip.

author: aldrin-isaac
body:
Refines #325 per the design follow-up.

## Changes

- **`request`/`release`** — renamed from `request`/`relinquish` (endpoint, handler, vocabulary).
- **Time-boxed, extendable window** (not an indefinite hold): `request` body is `{force, minutes}` — default **30m** when `minutes ≤ 0`; requesting again as the holder **extends** to `now + minutes` and keeps the original `since`. An **expired** reservation reads as free, so an abandoned hold auto-recovers — still no implicit heartbeat; the holder extends deliberately. Wire now carries `since` / `expires_at` / `last_active`; `WriteControlError` carries `expires_at`.
- **Per-network holder in the list** — `GET /networks` now includes each network's `write_control: {holder, since, expires_at}` (absent when free), so a UI shows who holds **every** network in one call.
- **Superuser force-takeover** — already works: `control.takeover` flows through `checkPermission`, whose superuser bypass (`checker.go:58`) fires before grant evaluation, so a superuser can always force a takeover. Now documented.

## Tests / validation

- Store lifecycle extended: default-30m window, explicit extend keeps `since` and grows the window; a dedicated **expiry** test (expired hold reads free, another caller acquires without `force`); the **network-list holder** assertion.
- `go build`/`vet`/full test green; **1node-vs-config 25/25** (enforcement off — no regression).

## Net model

A reservation with a **default 30-minute window** you can `request` (set), **extend** (re-request as holder), `release`, or have **taken over** (force; superuser-bypassable) — every transition an explicit, audited, permissioned API call. `GET /control` per network for detail; `GET /networks` for the cross-network holder view.

author: aalejandroaraujo
body:
Adds a doorway so Hermes can hand a job URL to career-ops, which evaluates it end to end with the existing batch machinery. Removes the manual print→WinSCP→notify bottleneck for normal pages.

## What's in it
- **`ingest-server.mjs`** (new): zero-dep Node HTTP server, runs as the container's main process. `POST /ingest {url,note}` → bearer-token auth → URL guard (reuses `rejectPrivateOrInvalid`) → dedup → append to `batch/batch-input.tsv` → single-flight `batch-runner.sh` drain → `202 {accepted,id}`. `GET /health`.
- **Dockerfile**: install Claude Code in the image so `claude -p` workers run in-container.
- **docker-compose.yml**: `careerops-bridge` external network; mount host `~/.claude` for auth; `command: npm run ingest`; add `CAREEROPS_INGEST_TOKEN`; drop `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` passthrough (subscription token must win); `HOME=/root`, `user: root`.
- **package.json**: `ingest` script. **.env.example**: token. **.gitignore**: retire `job-leads/` (use `jds/`). **docs/INGEST-BRIDGE.md**: setup + verify.

## Security
- No published host port; reachable only on `careerops-bridge` + bearer token.
- URL guard blocks loopback/private/invalid hosts.
- Never auto-submits — evaluate + render only.

## Verify
See `docs/INGEST-BRIDGE.md`. Smoke-tested locally: health 200, missing/bad token 401, private URL 400, missing url 400, unknown route 404.

author: viktormarinho
body:
Follow-up to #4180 (the `isApiKeyPrincipal` flag there raised: why is `boundAuth` optional / why are these args positional at all?).

Two related cleanups to `AccessControl`, both stemming from "`boundAuth` is always present at runtime":

## 1. `boundAuth` is now required + dead branch removed

`boundAuth` is built by the context factory for **every** request (even anonymous — no role/perms, then denied by the permission check). So it's never absent, yet it was typed optional, leaving dead guards and an unreachable branch.

- **Removed the dead `!userId && !boundAuth` branch in `check()`** — the `UnauthorizedError` 401 + public-tool fallback. It only ran when `boundAuth` was missing (impossible). Anonymous callers already get 403 via the permission path; public tools are gated by the MCP transport's own `isPublicTool` (`auth.ts`) and the `MESH_PUBLIC_` prefix. With it went the now-unused `isToolPublic`, the `getToolMeta` param, the `GetToolMetaFn` type, and the `MCP_MESH_KEY` import.
- Dropped the dead `if (!boundAuth) return false` guards in `checkResource` / `checkApiKeyAccess` / `checkMemberAccess`.

## 2. Single options-object constructor

The 6-positional constructor required three leading optionals and passing `undefined` to reach `boundAuth` — a footgun. Replaced with one `AccessControlOptions` object: `boundAuth` required, everything else named/optional, `connectionId` defaulting to `"self"`. TypeScript flagged every call site; all updated (`context-factory`, MCP transport, `automation-context`, unit tests).

**No behavior change** — the removed branch never executed in prod; the rest is a pure call-shape refactor. Tests that constructed `AccessControl` without a `boundAuth` now pass a mock (grant/granted), or were deleted (the "no BoundAuthClient" case, which can no longer happen).

## Heads-up / follow-up decision
Removing the dead branch removed the **last** `throw new UnauthorizedError` in the repo, so the type is now never thrown (its `instanceof` catches in `tools-rest.ts`/`org-fs.ts` are dead). Left as-is. Open question: drop `UnauthorizedError` + those catches, or restore 401 semantics for unauthenticated callers (anon → 401 vs today's 403)?

`tsc` + `oxlint` clean; auth+core unit tests green (except the pre-existing DB-gated `context-factory.integration.test.ts`).

author: bradflaugher
body:
Completes #175 (sub-agents — the invariant-sensitive half; phone-a-friend shipped in part a, b1f36bf).

A scheduled run can now delegate a scoped subtask to a **child** run via a new `spawn_subagent` native tool. The child is **not** a new or weaker loop — it is another `agentcore.Run`, governed exactly like the parent. **OFF by default** behind `FLEET_SUBAGENTS_ENABLED`; when off the tool is not even registered, so config/default behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## The four non-negotiable properties (review bar)

1. **Governance is one core.** The child runs through `(*Agent).Execute → agentcore.Run`, the entrypoint `TestEntrypointConformance` pins. The tool body (`internal/agent/subagent.go`) only adapts I/O around it — no second loop, no second policy path, no privileged executor.
2. **Monotonic privilege.** The child inherits the parent's sandbox (same network-seal posture — it has no namespace of its own to widen), the parent's brokered MCP client, and the parent's MCP/credential allowlists, and may only **subtract**: `allow_servers` is intersected with the parent's loaded set; the credential allowlist is the parent's, **copied**. A per-child model is resolved **host-side** like the phone-a-friend reviewer, so credentials never enter the sandbox or model context.
3. **Hard budget split.** The child's cost/token ceiling is **sliced from the parent's remaining budget**, and the child's actual spend is **charged back** into the parent. The parent's `MaxCostUSD`/`MaxTotalTokens` is the hard wall the collective spend of all descendants — across fan-out **and** depth — can never breach. New agentcore seam: `ScheduledPolicy.Budget()` + `.ChargeChildUsage()`.
4. **Recursion / fan-out caps.** `FLEET_SUBAGENTS_MAX_DEPTH` (default 2) and `FLEET_SUBAGENTS_MAX_CHILDREN` (default 4); a spawn exceeding either is **refused with a tool error**, never a panic or silent allow.

Credentials stay host-side: the child shares the parent's broker; MCP creds never enter any sandbox or model context.

## Where the invariants are enforced

- **Budget split:** `internal/agent/subagent.go` `spawn()` — `runtimePolicy.Budget()` read + `sliceCostBudget`/`sliceTokenBudget` hard-cap at the parent's remaining + `runtimePolicy.ChargeChildUsage()` charge-back. The child's own slice is enforced by the **same** `checkCeilings`/`budgetGuardedStep` the parent uses. `spawn_subagent` is a **sequential** tool, so spawns within a round serialize — each sees the prior sibling's spend already charged in (the split is exact).
- **Depth/fan-out:** `spawn()` `depth >= maxDepth` check + `reserveChildSlot()` under the parent lock.
- **Allowlist narrowing:** `narrowedCredentialAllowlist` (copy, never widen) + `childSelection` (intersection, never union).

## Tests (fake-LLM seam only, no real key)

`internal/agent/subagent_test.go` + `internal/agentcore/subagent_budget_test.go`: child runs through agentcore.Run with depth+1 / sliced budget / copied allowlist; combined child spend can never breach the parent ceiling; spawn at maxDepth refused; (maxChildren+1)-th spawn refused; allow_servers only narrows; tool registered iff enabled; charge-back folds into the parent's own ceiling check.

## Validation

- `make build`, `go vet -tags fleet_host_executor ./...`, `make lint`: clean.
- `go test -p 1 -tags fleet_host_executor ./internal/agentcore/... ./internal/agent/...`: pass (incl. `-race` on the concurrency-sensitive spawn tests).
- `gitleaks dir . --redact --exit-code 1`: no leaks.
- Pre-existing, environment-specific failure unrelated to this change: scheduledrun `TestPrepareWorktree_CustomPrefixAndBase` (assumes a `master` default branch) fails identically on `origin/main`.

## ADR

`docs/adr/0007-governed-sub-agents.md` documents that sub-agents **extend** (not weaken) ADR-0001: children spawn ONLY via `agentcore.Run` with monotonic privilege + budget/depth/fan-out caps. The charge-back vs. live-ledger trade-off and its precise bound are recorded under "Alternatives considered".

author: pedramamini
body:
## Summary

Triage of Sentry field crashes on the **rc** channel. Three issues were best-effort or fully-recovered conditions being reported to Sentry as if they were bugs (the same telemetry-noise-on-expected-condition family addressed in prior triages). Fixed in one branch:

### MAESTRO-M9 - `RangeError: Invalid string length` (regression)
`agentSessions.getGlobalStats` lost its `RangeError` carve-out when it was refactored onto `statsCache`. A session file too large to read into a single V8 string throws `RangeError: Invalid string length`, and both the Claude and Codex incremental read loops captured it unconditionally. Re-added the guard, mirroring the storage-layer pattern already present in `claude-session-storage.ts` / `codex-session-storage.ts`. Still live on `0.18.2-RC` (12 recent events).

### MAESTRO-FM - `EACCES`/`ENOENT` mkdir `.maestro/history` (553 occ)
`writeEntryLocal` is a best-effort cross-host history sync write. When the project lives in a permission-restricted or non-existent directory (read-only Dropbox / CloudStorage team folders, `/home/.maestro/history`), `mkdir` throws `EACCES`/`ENOENT`. The primary history store is unaffected, so we now skip Sentry for expected filesystem error codes and only report genuinely unexpected failures. Added regression tests.

### MAESTRO-JB - "Grooming error: Session not found" (65 occ)
`groupChat` `resetContext` already recovers from a grooming failure by falling back to a fresh session. When the failure is "Session not found" (the participant's session was deleted mid-summary), that's an expected, fully-recovered condition - skip the Sentry report; unexpected grooming failures still surface.

## Validation
- `tsc -p tsconfig.main.json` clean
- ESLint + Prettier clean on changed files
- `vitest` green: shared-history-manager (12, +2 new), agentSessions + groupChat (74)

## Deliberately not included
- **MAESTRO-Q2** (`maestro-p --status sample failed`, ~5.7k occ): a periodic best-effort sampler reporting every failure mode as a Sentry warning. Deferred in two prior triages pending a human call on `maestro-p` exit semantics; the `reason`/`stage` context isn't indexed as queryable tags, so there's no data-backed clean expected-boundary to carve out. Flagging for a decision rather than guessing.
- **MAESTRO-TP** (`No handler registered for 'pianola:get-rules'`): `pianola` has zero references in the codebase (unmerged dev-environment feature) - no handler or caller to fix here.
- Native/build issues (renderer/GPU crashes, spawn EINVAL/E2BIG, GLIBC_2.38) - genuine signal or build-infra, not app-fixable noise.

Note: merged into `rc`, so GitHub will reference but not auto-close the issues until `rc` reaches `main`. The M9/FM/JB code also exists on `main`; this PR is scoped to `rc` per request.

author: gigurra
body:
## What & why

JOH-316 slice **C1**. Flips the `conv == conv` actor-equality **self-checks** in `agentd` to compare the stable `agent_id`, so they survive conv rotation (reincarnate / `/clear`) and match the JOH-316 program ("agent_id by default, conv_id only at the harness edge").

These checks **work today** — every conv compared is a current generation resolved at the boundary (cron owner/target are re-resolved to the actor's *current* conv on read; selectors resolve any generation forward to head). So this is **robustness + intent-alignment, not a live-bug fix** — exactly the "works today" nature C1 calls out.

## The primitive

New `sameActor(a, b)` in `handlers.go` — the rotation-immune form of `a == b`:
- resolves each conv to its `agent_id` and compares; `a == b` short-circuit keeps the common self case cheap (no DB hit);
- **fail-closed on empty conv-ids** (an empty conv is "no actor", never equal to anything — incl. another empty);
- a plain conversation (no actor row) resolves to `""` and is matched by conv-id alone, so two distinct non-agent convs never collide and a non-agent never matches an agent — **preserving the old conv-literal allow/deny semantics exactly**.

Mirrors the JOH-317 inbox/ownership matcher (`callerIsRecipient`).

## Flipped (auth / visibility / security self-checks)

| File | Check | Kind |
|------|-------|------|
| `agent_dispatch.go` | `requireInboxAccess` `isOperator` | functional (read-marker) |
| `agent_dispatch.go` | `ownerOfGroupContaining` → agent-keyed `db.FindMemberInGroup` | visibility/auth |
| `cron_handlers.go` | `jobVisibleTo` owner + target | visibility |
| `cron_handlers.go` | `authCronWrite` self-vs-cross path | auth |
| `lifecycle.go` | bulk-retire self-skip | self-skip |
| `lifecycle.go` | delete self-prevention | security (strictly safer) |
| `dir.go` | terminal-spawn "only for itself" | security |

## Deliberately left conv-keyed (documented)

- `cron_handlers.go` create's `owner \!= targetConv` **group-routing heuristic** — not a self-check; flipping could alter delivery routing for the same-actor-different-conv edge.
- Display-only `caller_conv` echoes (`lifecycle.go` stop/resume/delete, `dir.go` dir responses) — not auth/visibility; identical output today; belong to the D1 display slice.
- `enrollment_handlers.go` — **no `conv==conv` self-check exists** (only a `callerConv == ""` human check); the brief's listing was stale.

No migration. No `agent_messages` touch.

## Authz symmetry (cold-reviewed)

Reviewed by a fresh **diff-only cold agent** instructed to audit authz symmetry. Verdict: **authz-safe, no blockers.** `sameActor` can only ever widen "self" to the SAME agent's other generations — distinct agents stay distinct (different `agent_id`s), so no check over-authorizes; deny-guards (delete self-block) only widen, and every grant-on-true path is fail-closed on DB error. One **NIT fixed**: `sameActor` is now fail-closed on empty conv-ids. Remaining NIT/QUESTIONs triaged as out-of-scope (a perf micro-opt; two pre-existing behaviors not introduced here).

## Tests

- `TestSameActor` — every branch: same conv, two generations of one agent (both orders), distinct agents, plain↔plain / plain↔agent, and empty conv-ids.
- `TestOwnerOfGroupContaining_RotationImmune` — a predecessor-generation conv still resolves to the member's agent (a genuine guard: **fails on the pre-flip code**).

Gates: `go build ./...`, `env -u CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_THRESHOLD_MINUTES go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `gofmt -l` (touched files) — all green.

author: ktursunov
body:
## What

A **code-coverage gate** for pull requests: it fails when coverage of the lines a PR changed (vs the base branch) is below **80%**. Global coverage stays a non-failing **warning**, so only changed code is gated — not legacy debt. The repo is a single component, so there's no per-component routing.

## How it works

Two CI jobs, both self-contained — no third-party coverage actions, no external services. **pnpm stays Python-free** (run `pnpm test:coverage` locally and open `coverage/index.html`); **Python runs only in CI**, processing the coverage artifact pnpm produced.

- **`test` job** (Node) — runs `pnpm test:coverage` (Vitest, Cobertura reporter) and uploads the report as the `coverage-report` artifact.
- **`coverage` job** (`needs: test`, Python) — downloads that artifact and:
  - **Coverage summary** — `scripts/ci/coverage-summary.py` renders overall + per-area coverage to the job summary (warning; runs on push and PR).
  - **Code-coverage gate** — `scripts/ci/diff-coverage.py` wraps [`diff-cover`](https://github.com/Bachmann1234/diff_cover), measures coverage of the changed lines, renders a per-file table, and **fails the PR** below 80% (pull requests only). Output goes to the job summary, so it works on fork PRs with a read-only token (no PR comment).

## What you'll see on a PR (job summary)

```
## Code coverage gate

**🔴 FAIL** — code coverage on changed lines (≥ 80%): 0/3 covered (0.0%).

| File | New lines | Coverage | Min | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |
| src/foo.ts | 0/3 | 0.0% | 80% | 🔴 |
```

When the changed lines are covered, the same check passes; a PR with no coverable changes passes with nothing to gate.

## Follow-up

- [ ] Make the `Coverage summary & gate` check required in branch protection for `main`.

author: pedramamini
body:
## Summary

Three field-crash fixes for the **stable (main) channel**, sourced from Sentry (`smash-labs/maestro`) and validated against the code + the affected releases (0.17.1 / 0.17.2, `channel:stable`). Fixes 2 and 3 are **byte-identical mirrors of rc PR #1141** so the rc->main merge converges with no conflict; fix 1 is unique to main.

## 1. Native bindings packaging (escalating on current main)

**Sentry:** MAESTRO-TE (`Cannot find module 'file-uri-to-path'`, escalating), MAESTRO-Q3 / MAESTRO-JV / MAESTRO-TC / MAESTRO-TD (`Could not locate the bindings file`). ~40+ events on 0.17.2.

`better-sqlite3` -> `bindings` -> `file-uri-to-path`, but `asarUnpack` only listed `better-sqlite3` and `node-pty`:

- The unpacked `bindings.js` does `require('file-uri-to-path')` at load. With `file-uri-to-path` still inside `app.asar`, resolution from `app.asar.unpacked` cannot cross back into the archive -> **"Cannot find module 'file-uri-to-path'"** (MAESTRO-TE). The require stack confirms it: `app.asar.unpacked/.../bindings/bindings.js` failing to load a module left in the asar.
- The mixed packed/unpacked layout also makes `bindings` compute an in-archive search root for the compiled `.node`, producing **"Could not locate the bindings file. Tried: .../app.asar/.../better_sqlite3.node"** (MAESTRO-Q3/JV, via `StatsDB.initialize` and `initCueDb`).

**Fix:** unpack the full native dependency closure so the whole chain resolves consistently from `app.asar.unpacked`:

```json
"asarUnpack": [
  "node_modules/node-pty/**/*",
  "node_modules/better-sqlite3/**/*",
  "node_modules/bindings/**/*",
  "node_modules/file-uri-to-path/**/*"
]
```

`node-pty` needs nothing extra (its only dep, `node-addon-api`, is build-time headers; it loads its `.node` directly).

## 2. Recoverable grooming session loss (MAESTRO-JB, 65 events, stable)

Group-chat context summary spawns a batch agent. If the participant's provider session was deleted mid-summary, the agent emits a **recoverable** `Session not found` error (`error-patterns.ts` `session_not_found`, `recoverable: true`) and the code already falls back to a fresh session. The explicit `captureException` in `groupChat.ts` reported it anyway. Skip it for that message; real summary failures still report. (Mirrors rc #1141.)

## 3. Oversized session files (MAESTRO-M9, regressed onto stable)

`getGlobalStats` reads each session file into a single string; a file too large throws `RangeError: Invalid string length`. The #1115 carve-out was lost when `getGlobalStats` was refactored onto `statsCache` (that refactor reached main, so M9 came back on `channel:stable`, release 0.17.1). Re-skip the expected `RangeError` in both the Claude and Codex parse loops in `agentSessions.ts`, mirroring the storage-layer pattern (`claude-/codex-session-storage.ts`). (Mirrors rc #1141.)

## Out of scope (intentionally not touched)

- **MAESTRO-FM** (shared-history write EACCES/EROFS): Sentry shows it is **100% `channel:rc`** (zero stable events). The code is latent on main but does not fire on stable; rc #1141 fixes it and it reaches main on the next merge. Not a main field issue.
- **MAESTRO-RA** (`agent-probe-failed`): `markFailed` already guards with `isExpectedConnectionFailure`; residual events are genuine signal.
- **MAESTRO-J0** (`Failed to load required prompt`), **MAESTRO-T8/T9** (`shellLogs is not iterable`): root cause not obvious enough to fix confidently.
- Native crashes, GLIBC/build-infra (MAESTRO-RS), `spawn E2BIG/EINVAL`, ENOSPC: already filtered or build/environment issues.

## Testing

- `vitest run` for `agentSessions.test.ts` (20) + `groupChat.test.ts` (54) -> all pass.
- `prettier --check` and `eslint` clean on changed files; type-check shows no errors in changed files.
- The packaging change is build-config; recommend a packaged smoke build before release to confirm the bindings chain loads.

The added lines in fixes 2 and 3 are verified byte-identical to rc PR #1141.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of oversized session data so affected sessions are skipped more gracefully instead of causing unnecessary errors.
  * Reduced noisy error reporting for expected recovery cases when resetting chat participant context, while still reporting unexpected failures.
  * Expanded app packaging coverage to include additional native dependencies, helping the desktop app start more reliably.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve local geometry fitting precision for rectangular and color-patch primitives so small bbox-edge adjustments (±0.01) can be discovered by the sequential optimizer.
- Provide a deterministic, low-risk change that can reduce pixel error for Plan-B BackBottom candidates (e.g., `GE9012_6M`) without introducing new runtime image-ID special-cases.

### Description
- Extend `_default_candidate_provider` in `src/iCCModules/imageCompositeConverterGeometryIrOptimizer.py` to emit finer per-edge bbox probes (±0.01) for `RectBorder` and `ColorPatch` elements while keeping existing coarse probes for other kinds.
- Add a regression test `test_default_optimizer_refines_rect_bbox_with_fine_edge_probe` in `tests/detailtests/test_geometry_ir_optimizer_helpers.py` that proves the fine edge probe can be chosen when it is the only improving candidate.
- Document Run TV in `docs/next_arbeitspaket_2026-06-28_runTV.md` and update `PLAN_B_KANDIDATEN.md` and `docs/README.md` to record the GE9012_6M work package and the new optimizer behavior.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/detailtests/test_geometry_ir_optimizer_helpers.py` and the test suite passed (`16 passed`).
- Ran the hardcoding check with `python tools/check_no_new_image_id_hardcoding.py` which reported no image-ID hardcoding (0 occurrences).

author: alexschrader
body:
**"Login so progress saves to username, not device"** (Alex, 2026-06-28). Stack decided with Alex: **Supabase** (auth + Postgres + sync), sign-in via **Google / Apple OAuth**.

This is the **design + verifiable core**. The Supabase client / auth UI / live wiring land in a follow-up PR built against the real project — because none of it can run or be tested until the Supabase project + Google OAuth exist, and **only Alex can create those.** So this PR unblocks that provisioning and locks the parts that must be *correct*.

## In this PR (all green, zero new deps, app untouched)
- **`src/store/sync.js`** — the pure push-vs-pull decision, the one piece that's dangerous to get wrong. Last-write-wins **with a fresh-device safety**: signing in on a new device PULLS the cloud instead of overwriting it with an empty store. 6 unit tests.
- **`supabase/schema.sql`** — one JSONB row per user (the existing `partialize` blob, opaque to Postgres so it never churns), `updated_at` trigger, and **row-level security** so the anon key can only ever touch the signed-in user's own row.
- **`BUILD-BRIEF-accounts-sync.md`** — full architecture + **your provisioning checklist**.
- **Graceful degrade by design:** no Supabase env → the feature stays dormant and the app behaves exactly as today. Ships dark, lights up on provisioning — no big-bang cutover, no risk to current local progress.

## 👉 Your move (unblocks the wiring PR) — from the brief
1. Create a Supabase project; grab the **Project URL** + **anon** key.
2. Run `supabase/schema.sql` in the SQL editor.
3. Enable **Google** provider (Google Cloud OAuth client → redirect URI Supabase gives you).
4. Set `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in Vercel (+ `.env.local`).
5. *(Later)* Apple sign-in — needs an Apple Developer account; worth it before App Store.

Once that's in, I build + verify the client, the **Sign in with Google** button in Settings, and the sync engine against your live project.

## Checks
45 unit tests (+6 new) · build clean. No content/contract changes.

## Flags
- Managed auth stores user emails → real PII; I'll add a short privacy note in Settings with the wiring.
- Last-write-wins: editing offline on two devices lets the later save win. Fine for solo use; a conflict UX is logged as a follow-up.

Draft — not for merge. Provision Supabase, then I wire it.

body:
## Summary

- **Deliverable A (tests):** `tests/integration/test_worker_wedge_pending.py` with two complementary tests:
  - **A1 `test_worker_loop_parks_on_zero_semaphore`** (mechanism, load-bearing): drives the real `_worker_loop` against `Semaphore(0)`, proves the loop parks at `await semaphore.acquire()` and recovers on `release()` 
  - **A2 `test_health_check_cannot_escalate_parked_worker`** (backstop-blindness): proves `_agent_session_health_check()` never escalates when `worker.done()==False`, documenting the 300s backstop's structural blindness
  - **B2 `TestAsyncioDebugHelper`**: 6 assertions against `_asyncio_debug_enabled()` helper
- **Deliverable B (`_asyncio_debug_enabled` + `set_debug` wiring):** pure helper in `worker/__main__.py` + env-gated `set_debug` startup wiring (default-off, fail-open, ships both branches). C1 limitation documented.
- **Deliverable D (forensic line):** always-on slot-exhaustion log in `session_health.py` pending branch — WARNING when `permits_free==0 AND running_count < max_sessions` (leaked-slot fingerprint), INFO for healthy backpressure, silent when permits free. Logging-only; recovery unchanged.
- **`.env.example`** placeholder for `WORKER_ASYNCIO_DEBUG`.
- **Findings doc** `docs/features/worker-wedge-investigation.md`: four hypotheses with verdicts, acquire/release audit table, detection surfaces, binary decision.

## Findings

- **H1 (semaphore exhaustion):** CONFIRMED as mechanism — A1 test reproduces it deterministically. No production slot-leak found in current code (all exit paths release via `finally` at line 1641); PTY-pool blocking (H3) is the live variant.
- **H2 (sync loop block):** Not confirmed — health-check log cadence normal.
- **H3 (PTY-pool holds slot):** CONFIRMED — sessions hold global slot while blocked at `await pty_pool.acquire_pair()`. With PTY pool size 3 and max sessions 8, this can deplete the semaphore.
- **H4 (set/clear race):** Mitigated — `_has_pending` guard closes the race window; worst case 300s delay.

body:
Closes #53

## Summary

Clicking a memory row now opens a **slide-over detail panel** showing everything TheBrain knows about it. Adds the missing owner-scoped `GET /memory/:id` so linked memories (which may be off the current page) can be opened too.

### Backend
- `GET /memory/:id` — owner-scoped: `findById` + ownership check; returns **404 (not 403)** when the id is unknown *or* owned by another user, so it never leaks another user's memory's existence. `:id` validated as a uuid (400 otherwise). Registered **last**, after `/capture`, `/capture-voice`, `/`, `/ask`, so it shadows nothing.
- Owner-scoping done at the service layer (`getById`) — left `repository.findById` untouched (the encoder relies on its broad signature).

### Frontend
- Rows are clickable → `MemoryDetail` slide-over (backdrop + ×/Escape close), rendered as a sibling **overlay** so the list stays mounted and **scroll position is preserved** on close.

- `links` render as clickable cards → fetch-by-id and swap the panel content (loading state, `ErrorBanner` on failure, inline "linked memory not found" on 404), with a "← Back" affordance.

> Note: the title says "heat timeline", but there's **no heat-history data** (heat is a single current value) — so per the acceptance criteria this shows numeric heat + the bar, not a fabricated chart.

`conversation_metrics.sender_id` persistia o **telefone cru** do cliente a cada turno (chat + WhatsApp) — PII desnecessária gravada na fonte, follow-up §39 LGPD da auditoria (achado da Ada).

author: etacassiopeia
body:
## Summary

The `lookup` response behavior (`_behaviors.lookup`, CSV-backed `${into}[column]` token replacement) was only applied on the **proxy** code path. A normal imposter `is` response with `_behaviors.lookup` silently did nothing — the tokens were left verbatim. (`copy` on an `is` response worked, which made the gap confusing.)

## Root cause (two parts)

1. `imposter/handler.rs` applied `copy` but **never** called `apply_lookup_behaviors` — only `proxy/handler.rs` did.
2. The `lookup` field lacked the single-or-array deserializer that `copy` has, so the Mountebank/docs single-object form (`"lookup": { ... }`) **failed to deserialize and silently dropped the entire `_behaviors` block** — the real reason the repro showed verbatim tokens.

## Fix

- Apply `apply_lookup_behaviors` on imposter `is` responses (after the copy block), using a process-global `CsvCache` (`OnceLock`, mirroring `get_http_client`).
- Add `deserialize_lookup_behaviors` so `lookup` accepts a single object **or** an array, mirroring `deserialize_copy_behaviors`.
- Surface CSV load failures with a `warn!` instead of discarding the error via `.ok()?`, so a misconfigured data source is diagnosable — benefits the proxy path too.

## Tests

- `test_lookup_behavior_applied_on_is_response` — real HTTP GET through an imposter with a single-object `lookup` + temp CSV; asserts body **and** response-header token replacement, status 200, and no residual `${row}` tokens.
- `test_lookup_behaviors_single_object_and_array` — unit test for the new deserializer (both forms).

## Verification
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --lib` → 616 pass (2 new).

Closes #213

author: acbecquet
body:
## Intent

Make the ceo-chat hands-free phone experience FAST and ROBUST, fixing two issues the captain hit on a real iPhone 14 test of the current build.

Bug A (latency): the broker latched until the agent's ENTIRE reply turn completed, then ran speakability+TTS — ~36s of silence on a 36s turn (proven in the captain's serve.log: repeated 'say seen but harness still streaming — holding (latch)'). Fix = speak INCREMENTALLY: streamReply emits complete speakable units (sentence/say-block boundaries via splitCompleteUnits) as the reply streams; runStreamingPipeline rewrites+synthesizes+emits each unit as a PipelineChunk progressively (serialized for ordered/gapless audio), so first audio lands ~1-2s in. Deliberate decision: the streaming speakability backend must be FAST — it uses the Anthropic API if a key is paired, else the deterministic rule-based rewriter (mock), and NEVER 'claude -p' per unit (>2s cold start each would defeat the fix). On hub the offline env's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is empty, so it intentionally uses the deterministic rewriter, which still honors the §7.3 contract (drops code/paths/URLs, keeps questions). runPipeline is kept intentionally for legacy/in-memory test drivers. Verified live against a real claude: first audio before turn-end.

Bug B (robustness): (1) Root cause of the wrong/dropped transcript was that an attached first mate shares ~/firstmate's project dir with OTHER concurrent claude sessions, so latestTranscriptIn (newest-by-mtime) flip-flopped between unrelated files and our injected prompt was in the older one. Fix = PROMPT-ANCHORED tap (latestTranscriptWithPrompt/findPromptAnchor/saysAfterAnchor): anchor each turn to the file that recorded our injected prompt and read only the says after it; re-resolved every poll so a mid-turn /clear or rotation is followed without loss/dup (streamReply dedups units). Deliberately NOT using /proc fd-pinning because claude opens→appends→closes the jsonl (verified, fd not held). (2) Auto-dismiss benign Claude modals before every inject (detectBenignModal/dismissBenignModals): ONLY the 'How is Claude doing this session?' rating prompt (Escape) and trust dialog (Enter) — conservatively, never auto-answering a real question to the captain; surfaced as a 'notice' frame to the diagnostics panel. (3) Reconnect/refresh robustness in app.ts: a refreshed client is replayed the last turn (replay flag, no auto-play) so it's never blank; a turn is NOT cancelled when the initiating socket drops (a refresh re-joins the broadcast for remaining chunks); cancel is explicit via a new 'stop' frame (hangup/barge-in), which aborts streamReply + the pipeline.

Constraints honored: offline piper voice + whisper STT stay the default with no key; code stays DOM-free + dependency-injected so npm run validate exercises the same logic against fakes. Added validate legs (prompt-anchored transcript, incremental speakable units, streaming pipeline + abort, benign-modal auto-dismiss, web progressive chunks + notice + reconnect replay); all existing legs plus the real piper→whisper e2e stay green (29 pass / 255 checks). Durable gotchas recorded in AGENTS.md. WS protocol additions: client 'stop'; server 'notice'; index on narration/audio; replay flag on reply/narration/audio/turn-done.

## What Changed

- Replaced whole-turn latching with **incremental speech**: `streamReply` emits complete speakable units as the reply streams (`splitCompleteUnits`) and `runStreamingPipeline` rewrites + synthesizes + emits each as a progressive, serialized `PipelineChunk`, so first audio lands ~1–2s in instead of after the full turn. Streaming speakability uses the Anthropic API when a key is paired, else the deterministic rule-based rewriter — never `claude -p` per unit. `runPipeline` is kept for legacy/in-memory drivers.
- Made the transcript tap **prompt-anchored** (`latestTranscriptWithPrompt`/`findPromptAnchor`/`saysAfterAnchor`, gated by an inject timestamp) instead of newest-by-mtime, so a first mate sharing a project dir with other concurrent sessions no longer flip-flops to the wrong file; re-resolved every poll to follow `/clear`/compaction rotations, with unit dedup and LRU-cached `parseTranscript` to bound per-poll cost.
- Hardened the web/session layer: auto-dismiss only benign Claude modals before inject (rating prompt → Escape, trust dialog → Enter, surfaced as a `notice` frame), replay the last turn to refreshed clients without auto-play, keep turns alive when the initiating socket drops, and add explicit `stop`-frame cancellation. WS protocol gains client `stop`, server `notice`, an `index` on narration/audio, and a `replay` flag; new validate legs cover anchoring, incremental units, streaming pipeline + abort, modal dismiss, and progressive web chunks/reconnect (29 pass / 0 fail).

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a well-bounded latency/robustness fix whose three prior review findings are correctly and verifiably addressed (timestamp-gated anchoring, per-turn Replay accumulation, cached parses with rescan-skip); remaining observations are info-level with no new error/warning issues found.

## Testing

Ran the project gate `npm run validate` to green (29 pass, 264/264 checks; the 2 live MiniMax/speakability legs skip without creds), confirming all new Phase-5 legs for the latency fix and robustness fixes pass alongside the existing piper→whisper real-audio round-trip. To show the end-user behavior rather than only unit assertions, I wrote and ran a latency demo against the actual streaming pipeline and real piper TTS, which proves first audio is spoken at 2.34s while the agent turn keeps streaming until 8.36s (~6s of former dead silence removed, 4 chunks spoken progressively). A real-device iPhone/browser hands-free screenshot was not attainable on this dev box (no mic, no MiniMax creds, no iOS device), which the change's own notes defer to the captain's device retest; the broker/transcript/server logic that comprises the change is fully exercised. Transient out/ artifacts were removed and the working tree is clean.

author: benmarte
body:
Closes #894

## Problem

Agent-role progress comments were silently failing to appear on GitHub issues. `_PR_COMMENT_HOWTO` in `scripts/daedalus_dispatch.py` instructed every spawned agent to POST its comment via `urllib.request`, reading `os.environ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]`. In the cron worker environment `GITHUB_TOKEN` is **not exported** (gh authenticates via keyring), so that line raised `KeyError`, the comment was dropped, and the agent completed having posted nothing.

PR #895 tried a `gh issue comment` rewrite and was reverted by #896. The PM's design clarification on #894 settled the correct approach: **remove agent-side GitHub auth entirely and have the dispatcher post via its already-authenticated `provider`.**

## Fix

- **Neutralized `_PR_COMMENT_HOWTO`** — it no longer contains the `urllib`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` snippet. It now tells agents NOT to post GitHub comments themselves and to write a clear kanban completion summary, which the dispatcher posts on their behalf. The prominent "🚨 MANDATORY … you MUST post" instructions in the role bodies were rewritten accordingly.
- **Added `_post_completion_comments()`** — runs every tick in `run()`. It scans DONE kanban cards, maps each card's assignee to its pipeline role, resolves the issue number from the title, and posts the card's summary to the issue via `provider.post_issue_comment(issue_number, formatted_summary)`. Posting is idempotent per `(issue, role)` via a `dispatch_state` flag, and **already-closed issues are skipped** so a backlog of historical DONE cards can't spam old issues on first run.
- **Added `_format_completion_comment()`** — renders the comment body, leading with `**Agent: <role>**` to mirror the prior convention.

This covers every role uniformly (validator, PM, developer, QA, reviewer, security, docs) without threading comment logic into seven separate completion flows.

## How to test

```
python -m pytest tests/ -q          # 1987 passed
python tests/test_daedalus.py       # dual-mode standalone runner: 247 passed
```

New tests assert: a comment is posted once per role on completion, posting is idempotent across ticks, closed issues are skipped, non-pipeline cards are ignored, a `None` provider is a no-op, and the comment body carries role/title/summary. Updated the tests that previously asserted the `GITHUB_TOKEN`/urllib body pattern (`tests/test_daedalus.py`, `tests/test_dispatch.py`).

## Manual testing

- Full suite green with no `GITHUB_TOKEN` exported, reproducing the cron condition that caused the silent drop.
- Verified `_resolve_howtos("github", ...)["comment"]` contains no `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`urllib` and points agents at the dispatcher.

## Note / follow-up

The docs agent's `**Agent: documentation**` PR comment (consumed by `_deliver_doc_reports` for Slack delivery) used the same token-based path, so it was already broken in cron. Routing that PR comment through the dispatcher's provider is out of scope for #894 and left as a follow-up.

author: sampennington
body:
## Problem

Dashboard tiles auto-save display-option changes back to the shared insight via `persistDisplayOptions`. The trigger (`insightVizDataLogic.setQuery` → `props.setQuery`) fires for *any* `InsightVizNode` query, including programmatic re-syncs — tile re-renders, results refreshes — that carry an unchanged query. Those produced spurious PATCHes to the insight and activity-log churn, surfacing as "insights saving too often" without anyone clicking Save.

## Changes

Guard the PATCH in `persistDisplayOptions` with an `objectsEqual` check against the saved insight query, so no-op saves are dropped before the request fires. Narrow fix at the single write choke point — it doesn't change the intended behavior where a real display-option edit on a tile still persists.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Slack app). Added a Jest test asserting the PATCH is skipped when the query matches the saved insight, and ran the suite locally — all 19 `insightDataLogic.test.ts` tests pass. The new test catches the no-op-save regression none of the existing tests covered (they only asserted that a *changed* query persists and debounces).

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

@sampennington traced a "saving too often" report to the dashboard display-options work and asked for a dirty-guard at the save path. Authored by the PostHog Slack app. The guard lives in `persistDisplayOptions` (the single PATCH choke point) rather than in the upstream `setQuery` listener, so it catches every spurious-save vector — per-toggle saves, `updateVizSpecificOptions`, and re-render/results-refresh loops — without touching the InsightViz query plumbing.

A larger follow-up is under discussion: storing tile display options as a per-tile override (extending the existing `filters_overrides` / `TileFilters` mechanism) so dashboard changes never mutate the shared insight at all. Not in this PR.

## What

Adds `check-skill-freshness.sh` as a CI gate in `tests.yml`, next to the existing skills-manifest check.

## Why

Skill staleness was only caught at **inject-time**: the SessionStart hook prepends a "(may be stale)" banner but still ships the full stale body underneath. A warning doesn't stop bad content from landing. This moves the catch to **author-time** — a skill whose `last_verified` is past its `freshness_days` window blocks the PR until someone re-verifies against `source_files` and bumps the date.

Part of the staleness+syncing hardening (companion to the plugin mirror-sync, gov-plugin #84). Verified green on current skills (all 7 fresh, 0–1 days).

## Note / follow-up

`last_verified` is still a manual promise — a future refinement is to tie it to the git-mtime of the cited `source_files` so a stale date can't pass while the described code has moved. And the **mirror-parity gate** (canonical↔plugin) still needs a decision: a true cross-repo check needs a PAT (the repo is `GITHUB_TOKEN`-only by policy), so the options are a plugin-side self-consistency check vs. a scheduled cross-repo diff — surfacing separately.

- **`extends`** — extend one or more parent domains, inheriting and overriding their configuration.
- **What gets inherited** — entities (and field selections), semantic + source filters, parameters, tags, labels (additive), and metadata sections.
- **Merge rules** — scalar fields (e.g. filter `sql`) are *replaced*; collection fields (e.g. entity `fields`) are *extended*; labels are *additive*; tags/metadata matched by key.
- **`merge: remove`** — drop an inherited entity, filter, source_filter, parameter, or tag.
- **Multiple inheritance** — compose base + mixins; parents evaluated left-to-right, rightmost wins, child overrides all.

Flagged as **Beta** throughout, matching the official docs.

## Files changed

- `skills/domain-creation/SKILL.md` — overview note, decision-flow entry, new **Domain Hierarchy** section, best practices, docs lookup, and `description` frontmatter (so hierarchy questions trigger the skill).
- `skills/domain-creation/reference.md` — `extends` in the YAML schema + full **Domain Hierarchy (Inheritance)** reference.
- `skills/domain-creation/examples.md` — worked examples: base + extending child, multiple-inheritance mixins, and `merge: remove`.
- Version bump to `1.1.1` across all manifest/marketplace files + `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

Grounded in the official `/domains#domain-hierarchy` docs and the `recipes/domain-hierarchy` recipe. `./scripts/validate-versions.sh` passes.

author: wowlegend
body: Fixes #6714. ## Problem With `noclobber` set in the interactive shell, every new tab prints an error as cmux rewrites its per-surface CLI shim on startup: - **zsh** (`setopt noclobber`): `_cmux_install_cli_command_shim:13: file exists: …/cmux-cli-shims//claude` - **bash** (`set -o noclobber`): `…/cmux-cli-shims//claude: cannot overwrite existing file` ## Root cause `_cmux_install_cli_command_shim` writes the generated shim with a plain `>` redirect. When the shim already exists (re-source, or a `$TMPDIR` shim persisted across sessions), `noclobber` refuses the overwrite. The function's `2>/dev/null` can't suppress it — the redirection itself fails, so the shell reports it to the terminal. ## Fix Use the explicit clobber operator `>|`, which this repo already uses for its own generated files (e.g. `cmux-zsh-integration.zsh` lines 689, 1205). One line in each integration: - `Resources/shell-integration/cmux-zsh-integration.zsh` - `Resources/shell-integration/cmux-bash-integration.bash` The open zsh-only PRs (#6715, #6769, #6815) fix the zsh line; this PR also fixes the **identical bug in the bash integration**, which none of them touch — resolving #6714 for both shells in one change. (fish is unaffected: `>` there doesn't honor a noclobber option.) ## Verification Under `setopt noclobber` / `set -o noclobber`, re-sourcing the integration with an existing shim prints the error before and is silent after; `>|` overwrites the cmux-owned shim cleanly. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes bash and zsh shim rewrite errors when `noclobber` is enabled by writing cmux CLI shims with the explicit clobber operator `>|`, resolving #6714. This prevents “file exists”/“cannot overwrite existing file” on new tabs and lets cmux reliably refresh its own shims. Written for commit fd02b252a491bc478273e2c47ea46a5fbf58dfcf. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved shell integration so generated CLI shim files are reliably overwritten even when `noclobber` is enabled. * This helps installation and update flows complete successfully in Bash and Zsh environments.

author: raimishah
body:
## What

Fixes a bug in `SynthefyNoriClient`'s remote retry loop (`_post_with_retries`): it could surface a **stale earlier-attempt exception** instead of the true final error.

### The bug
`last_exc` (and `response`) persisted across retry attempts. So if an earlier attempt raised a transient error (connection error or timeout) but the **final** attempt returned a *retryable* response (e.g. `503`), the terminal block raised the stale `APIConnectionError`/`APITimeoutError` rather than mapping the final `5xx` to `InternalServerError`. Callers got a misleading error type.

### The fix
Reset `last_exc`/`response` at the start of each attempt, so the terminal block reflects only the **final** attempt:
- final attempt raised → raise that exception;
- final attempt returned a retryable response → `_raise_for_status` maps it (`503` → `InternalServerError`).

## Tests
`test_final_error_wins_over_stale_earlier_attempt` — transient `ConnectError` on attempt 0, then `503`, asserting `InternalServerError`. **Verified it fails without the fix** (raises `APIConnectionError`) and passes with it. Full offline suite: `94 passed, 1 skipped`.

## Notes
- Independent of #23 (one-hot featurization), which is now merged; this branch is rebased onto the updated `main`.
- Version `4.2.1 → 4.2.2` (4.2.1 was taken by #23). Touches only `_post_with_retries` + its test (5-file diff).

# User description ## **User description** ## ** ** Upstream PR: https://github.com/awslabs/cli-agent-orchestrator/pull/336 Add Devin CLI provider implementation with unit tests and registration in all required locations. ## What Changed - Implemented `DevinCliProvider` with prompt/status parsing and `/exit` handling - MCP integration via temp `--config`, launching `cao-mcp-server` and passing `CAO_TERMINAL_ID` - Supports `agent_profile` system prompts and soft `allowed_tools` enforcement via a prepended security prompt - Registered `devin_cli` across the app: `ProviderType`, provider manager factory, `api/main.py` providers list, `launch` workspace-access list, settings agent dirs, agent profile listing, and `tool_mapping` (Bash/Read/Write) - Added comprehensive unit tests and fixtures; updated API test to include `devin_cli` - **NEW:** Added Playwright E2E tests for web UI integration - **NEW:** Added devcontainer for true end-to-end testing (bypasses WSL limitations) ## True End-to-End Testing with Devcontainer ### The Problem WSL has tmux limitations (`[Errno 95] Operation not supported`) that prevent real Devin CLI spawns. Unit and API tests pass, but actual agent spawning cannot be tested in WSL. ### The Solution: Devcontainer on Host Machine A `.devcontainer/` configuration that: - Runs on **host machine Docker** (not WSL) - bypasses tmux limitations - Installs Devin CLI and mounts your credentials from `~/.config/devin/` - Installs Playwright browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) - Pre-installs agent profiles for Devin CLI - Forwards port 9889 for CAO server ### How to Use for True E2E Testing **Prerequisites:** 1. Docker installed on your **host machine** (not WSL) 2. VS Code with Dev Containers extension 3. Devin CLI credentials on host at `~/.config/devin/` **Steps:** ```bash # 1. Open project in VS Code Dev Container code . # Press F1 → "Dev Containers: Reopen in Container" # 2. Start CAO server (inside devcontainer) cao-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9889 # 3. Run E2E tests (from host machine or devcontainer) cd web npm run test:e2e # 4. Access web UI open http://localhost:9889 ``` **Why This Works:** - ✅ Real tmux sessions (no WSL limitations) - ✅ Actual Devin CLI spawns with your credentials - ✅ Full stack testing: frontend → API → backend → tmux → Devin CLI - ✅ Playwright can test real user interactions ### Alternative: CI Testing If you don't have Docker on your host machine, the CI pipeline (which runs on real Linux) will perform the true end-to-end testing of Devin CLI spawns. ## Web UI E2E Tests - Why They Matter ### What They Test These E2E tests verify the complete user journey through the CAO web interface: - Web interface loads and renders correctly - Devin CLI appears in the providers list (both API and UI) - Spawn Agent modal opens and shows Devin CLI as an option - Agent profiles are available for Devin CLI selection - Provider registration works end-to-end ### How They Help vs Existing Tests **Existing Unit Tests:** - ✅ Test individual functions in isolation - ✅ Fast and focused - ❌ Don't test integration between components - ❌ Don't catch UI rendering issues - ❌ Don't verify user interaction flows **Existing API Tests:** - ✅ Test HTTP endpoints - ✅ Verify backend logic - ❌ Don't test frontend rendering - ❌ Don't catch JavaScript errors - ❌ Don't verify UI state management **NEW E2E Tests:** - ✅ Test the full stack: frontend → API → backend - ✅ Verify UI rendering and user interactions - ✅ Catch integration issues between React components and backend - ✅ Provide confidence that web features work for real users - ✅ Prevent regressions in web UI functionality ### Example Issues E2E Tests Catch - Frontend shows wrong provider list (API works, UI broken) - Modal doesn't open due to JavaScript error - Provider dropdown missing options (CSS/React state issue) - Button clicks don't trigger API calls (event handler bug) ### Trade-offs - **Pros:** Catches integration bugs, validates user experience, prevents UI regressions - **Cons:** Slower than unit tests, can be flaky in CI, requires browser setup Overall, E2E tests complement unit and API tests by providing confidence that the **complete user experience** works correctly, not just individual components in isolation. ## Bug Fixes - Fixed Markdown heading collision in prompt detection: do not treat response headings (`#`) as input prompts; terminate on horizontal rules/status bar only ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added Devin CLI (`devin_cli`) provider support end-to-end, including orchestration, agent profiles, tool restrictions, and workspace confirmation. * Enabled an alternative input delivery mode for CLIs that don’t support paste-buffer. * Expanded web provider fallback options to include Devin CLI. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved terminal status fallback behavior when live output isn’t available. * Hardened tmux piping by safely quoting paths; updated FIFO storage to use per-user temp with secure permissions. * Fixed provider installed/uninstalled reporting for Devin CLI. * **Documentation** * Added Devin CLI documentation and updated README/provider examples. --- --- # Generated description Below is a concise technical summary of the changes proposed in this PR: Add DevinCliProvider and wire it into provider selection, launch/session handling, terminal input delivery, status parsing, and tool restrictions through ProviderManager, TerminalService, and McpApp. Extend the web UI and test harness with Devin provider listings, graph/session updates, and end-to-end coverage for the new CLI flow.

author: laazyj
body:
## Summary

Stands up a new subsite at **clara.jasonduffett.net** as a self-contained sibling to the apex site — distinct palette, same privacy/cookie mechanism, separate analytics — and populates it with its first piece of content: the **"Amy and the Rain Forest"** story.

The architecture is **delegated DNS now, repo split deferred**: Clara gets its own hosted zone (delegated from the parent), cert, bucket, and CloudFront distribution, but stays in this monorepo. It can be lifted into its own repo later with a call-site edit.

## Content — `packages/clara/`
- Trimmed Eleventy package: the **"Amy and the Rain Forest"** story homepage + `privacy` + `404`.
- The homepage is a full-bleed forest scene the reader scrolls a story sheet up over, with scroll-triggered reveals (`layouts/story.njk`).
- Shared document chrome (`<head>` + footer) is extracted into `partials/head.njk` and `partials/site-footer.njk`, reused by both `base.njk` (cream prose pages) and `story.njk` so the shell isn't duplicated.
- Story styling is scoped under `.story`, so `privacy`/`404` and the cookie banner keep the distinct light/playful palette, separate from the apex's dark zine theme.
- Fonts load via `<link>` + `preconnect` (not a render-blocking CSS `@import`), trimmed to the weights actually used.
- The hero illustration is re-encoded from a 1.2 MB PNG to **AVIF (201 KB, ~46 dB PSNR)** with a WebP fallback via `image-set()` — an ~83% reduction with no visible quality loss. The source PNG and the intermediate composition assets live in `assets-src/`, which is **not** deployed.
- **Same** consent mechanism as the main site (Consent Mode v2, opt-in, `jd-consent-v1`), wired to a **separate** GA4 property via `CLARA_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`.
- Root `package.json` gains `clara:build`/`clara:start`/`clara:clean` aliases, mirroring the `site:*` scripts.

## Infrastructure — `packages/cdk/`
- `clara-system.ts` is its own composureCDK `compose()` graph: delegated hosted zone, dedicated `ClaraCertStack` (us-east-1), own bucket + distribution with a trimmed pretty-URL function.
- The subdomain is delegated from the parent zone by a single `ZoneDelegationRecord` at the composition root (`app.ts`). The child zone's name servers resolve as a CloudFormation token, so **there is no manual nameserver handoff**.
- **The apex is untouched**: the only change to existing infrastructure is the additive delegation record in the DNS stack (see the `DnsStack` snapshot diff — purely additive; every other apex snapshot is unchanged).

## Wiring
- `about.md`: Clara's name in the copyright copy now links to the subsite (the single inbound link).
- `deploy.yml`: passes `CLARA_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`; CDK nx targets depend on `clara:build`.

## Verification
`npm run verify` passes: format ✓, build (3 projects) ✓, lint ✓, tests 21/21 ✓ (includes new assertions for the Clara cert and the delegation record).

## Required before this goes live
1. Create a GA4 property for Clara and add its measurement ID as a GitHub repo variable `CLARA_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`.
2. On merge, `deploy.yml` provisions the zone, delegation, cert (auto-validated in the existing zone), and distribution — no registrar/DNS action needed.

## Follow-up (noted, not in this PR)
The NS delegation is expressed as a composureCDK `createNsRecordBuilder()` component — no raw-CDK escape hatch. composureCDK 0.8.6 makes `NsRecordBuilderProps.values` `Resolvable<string[]>` natively (upstream issue #244), so the earlier local patch-package hack has been removed.

The one remaining composureCDK gap is id-pinning when nesting lifecycles under `compose()` (the `withFixedId` adapter in `app.ts`, which keeps the apex's logical ids byte-identical) — filed upstream as issue #245.

## Summary

Initial scaffold for the **SGML Sales** project — a Python backend that powers the end-to-end sales infrastructure for the company (~$10M annual sales), as the operational counterpart to the **SGML Marketing Pipeline**.

It models the B2B commercial pipeline and the accounting hooks needed to keep revenue/AR in sync with the sales motion:

```
Lead → Opportunity → Quote → Order → Invoice → AR/Revenue
```

## What's included

- **FastAPI app** (`src/sgml_sales/`) with a SQLModel domain model: `Customer`, `Product`, `Lead`, `Opportunity`, `Order`, `Invoice`.
- **Reusable CRUD route factory** plus bespoke endpoints (opportunity stage transitions, invoice payment).
- **Reporting endpoints/services**: `/reports/pipeline` (open/weighted/closed-won value) and `/reports/accounting` (accounts receivable, recognized revenue) — the hook point for syncing to the SGL accounting ledger.
- **Tests** (`pytest`): health check + an end-to-end sales flow (customer → opportunity → win → invoice → payment) asserting the reports update correctly. ✅ 2 passed.
- **Tooling**: Ruff config (lint clean), GitHub Actions CI, a `SessionStart` hook + `scripts/setup.sh` for Claude Code web sessions.
- **Docs**: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/BRANDING.md`.

## ⚠️ Branding placeholders — action needed

body:
A separate **"Flash / update adapter"** section on the CAN-adapter node, answering "add a section to update/flash it with a guided mode for when to press the button".

The adapter is **not a Klipper MCU**, so it's flashed over **USB-DFU**. Entering DFU needs the **physical BOOT button** (gs_usb exposes no software bootloader-entry) - so the flow *guides* that step rather than faking one-click; the flash itself is host-automated:

1. Pick adapter model (auto-set from the confirmed board; wrong firmware can brick it).
2. **Unplug, HOLD BOOT while plugging USB back in, release** (the button timing, highlighted).
3. **Check for DFU** - confirms the device actually entered the bootloader before Flash is enabled.
4. Risk checkbox + **Flash** -> downloads the **official BTT firmware** for the revision and runs `dfu-util` (already in the passwordless-sudo grant); shows the log.

- Backend `canbus_flash` service + `GET /topology/canbus/{firmware,dfu-status}` + `POST /topology/canbus/flash` (refused while printing; refused unless actually in DFU; downloads the official .bin per chip).
- Frontend `CanFlashPanel.vue`; 12 `canbus.flash.*` strings ×19 locales.

Verified: `dfu-util` present + `sudo -n dfu-util` granted on CB2; the official V1/V2 firmware URLs resolve. Backend ruff/format/mypy + 45 tests; frontend type-check + eslint + prettier + 362 vitest pass.

author: asgeirf
body:
A single default flow can now vary by target language without forking it. `defaults.locales.<lang>.tools` overrides a tool's config for that locale only — the lever for "German redacts PII, others don't" and similar per-locale needs.

## Changes
- **Project model**: `Defaults.Locales map[string]LocaleDefaults`, each carrying per-locale tool presets (`tools`).
- **Merge precedence** (same shape, now locale-aware): a flow step's own config **>** the per-locale preset **>** the project-wide `defaults.tools` preset. The per-locale overlay is keyed by the run's target locale, so it applies to convergence (`kapi run`) and any targeted run alike; locales with no entry use the project defaults.

```yaml
defaults:
  flow: translate-and-check
  locales:
    de:
      tools:
        redact: { enabled: true }   # German redacts PII; other locales don't
```

The field round-trips through the recipe like the other un-modeled defaults (`flow`, gates, `tools`): the convergence surface reads the recipe fresh, so the CLI and desktop honor it without a TS-type change.

## Tests
A per-locale pseudo-translate prefix applies to `de` only; `fr` falls back to the project-wide preset and the `de` override does not leak. Docs: the convergence page documents per-locale toggles.

## Summary

GitHub's scheduled crons are best-effort and routinely drop top-of-hour slots under load. With the previous **hourly** poll, a single missed slot added up to ~2h of extra lag before a finished race appeared on the site — exactly what happened with the 2026 Austrian GP (the ~16:17 slot was skipped, so the result didn't land until the next successful run).

This bumps the guard poll cadence to **every 15 minutes** to shrink worst-case post-race lag and ride through dropped slots.

- **`update.yml`** — schedule cron `17 * * * *` → `2,17,32,47 * * * *` (every 15 min, still offset off the hour to dodge GitHub's top-of-hour load spike). The weekly `--full` reconciliation and the `update` job are unchanged.
- Updated "hourly" wording in `update.yml` comments, `check_update_due.py`/test docstrings, and `CLAUDE.md`.

The `check` job stays a no-network ~15s no-op when nothing is due, so the extra runs are cheap; the (network) `update` job only runs when the guard says a new race result is due.

author: mkmk749278
body:
## The finding (from the diagnostic we just shipped)

With the per-pair reason column now showing **pre-evaluation** skips, the live Pairs page reported **every promoted mover** as `spread_too_wide · scan skip · 0s ago` — FET (17.6M vol), PUNDIX (17.4M), GWEI (15.5M), OPN (19.3M) included. Those are liquid pairs with ~0.02–0.08% real spreads. Liquid pairs *all* flunking a "0.5%" spread gate = the value fed to the gate is wrong.

## Root cause — an off-by-100 unit bug

`ScanContext.spread_pct` is a **percent of mid** (`0.5` == 0.5%):
- stored as `(ask-bid)/mid * 100.0` (scanner `_fetch_global_book_tickers`);
- the regular gate uses `spread_threshold = 0.02` (== 0.02%);
- `check_spread_adaptive` documents the arg as "spread as a percentage of mid-price".

The mover gate compared it against the literal **`0.005`** — i.e. **0.005%**, ~100× too tight. Its own log string already said `"> 0.5% — skip"`, so **0.5% was always the intent** — the author wrote `0.005` thinking the value was a fraction (where 0.005 == 0.5%). Result: **100% of promoted movers were skipped before any evaluator ran.** VSB / BREAKDOWN_SHORT / MOVER_TREND_PULLBACK / MOVER_AVWAP_SCALP never got a single mover — the whole mover-scalp path was dead on arrival.

## Fix

- **`config/__init__.py`** — new env-tunable `MOVER_MAX_SPREAD_PCT` (default **0.5**, percent units), documented with the unit and the bug it replaces.
- **`src/scanner/__init__.py`** — gate on the config value instead of the hard-coded `0.005`; correct the log's double-`×100` so it prints the real spread.

After this, movers reach the evaluators. The per-pair column will then show the **next** layer — actual eval outcomes (`no_reclaim`, `mover_run_too_small`, `✓ fired`) or `basic_filters_failed` for any genuinely wide book — instead of a blanket pre-eval skip. That's the real test of the mover-scalp paths, finally unblocked.

## Owner sign-off requested ⚠️

This is a **money-path gate** (it decides which movers the scalp paths may trade), so per the change-management protocol I'm **not auto-merging** — holding for your approval. It's a bug fix restoring the documented 0.5% intent, and `MOVER_MAX_SPREAD_PCT` is env-tunable so you can tighten/loosen live without a code change. Recommend merge.

## Tests / checks

- `tests/test_mover_spread_gate.py` — regression guard pinning the threshold to percent units (asserts it's not the `0.005` bug value, and that 0.02–0.08% spreads pass).
- Broad sweep (scanner/config/scalp/mover): 570 passed. `ruff` clean; config loads (`MOVER_MAX_SPREAD_PCT = 0.5`).

author: go-to-k
body:
## Problem

`AWS::ECS::Service` `ServiceConnectConfiguration` drift **detection** shipped in #406, but revert was **detect-only**: Cloud Control cannot sub-path patch a writeOnly prop (it rejects an `add` at a nested path — *"can only be updated using 'add' operation"*), so the finding was reported not-revertable.

## Fix

Make it revertable with a `SDK_NESTED_WRITERS` writer that re-supplies the **whole** declared config via `ecs:UpdateService` — the only API that sets it.

- The whole config comes from `ctx.declared` (the resolved template intent), **not** the nested op value, so any drift under `ServiceConnectConfiguration` (a client alias, the namespace, enabled) converges to the declared whole.
- CamelCased back from the declared PascalCase. `UpdateService` re-defaults `DiscoveryName` to `PortName`, which the reader folds, so the stack converges clean.
- A service with **no** declared config sends `enabled: false` to turn Service Connect off.

`ServiceConnectConfiguration` graduates out of `WRITEONLY_NESTED_NO_CC_REVERT` (now empty, kept for a future `VolumeConfigurations` once that prop is projected).

## Tests

- Unit: the `UpdateService` writer (camelCase + cluster/service resolution + the no-declared-config disable); the plan now routes the nested finding to an `sdk` item (not not-revertable).
- **Live integ** (the existing `ecs-serviceconnect-readgap`, updated): an out-of-band client-alias `DnsName` change is **DETECTED** and **revert restores it**, converging CLEAN. **INTEG PASS.**

Completes the ECS ServiceConnect feature (detect + revert).

author: chewji9875
body:
## Problem

When Antigravity quota is exhausted, the upstream Gemini API returns HTTP 200 with an SSE streaming response containing **empty candidates** (`candidates[].content.parts:[]`) and `finishReason:"STOP"`. Previously, this was treated as a successful response — the client received zero bytes of output, the combo router marked the request as succeeded, and the exhausted account remained in rotation for future requests.

Reproducer: `agy --print "say hi"` → 0 bytes output (HTTP 200, no error).

## Root Cause

`validateResponseQuality()` had no detection for the Gemini-specific empty-parts pattern. The Claude empty-content detection (PR #5104) already handled `content_filter` 502s, but Gemini's quota-exhaustion response arrives as HTTP 200 with `parts:[]` — a shape the existing validators didn't cover.

## Fix

### 1. Detection in `validateQuality.ts` (+45 lines)

Added Gemini empty-parts tracking in the SSE bounded-peek loop:

- Tracks `geminiEmptyCandidatesCount`, `geminiHasContent`, `geminiLastFinishReason` across all parsed SSE chunks.
- Only runs when `isKnownNonClaudeStreamPayload()` returns false (i.e., no content-bearing candidates detected — the narrow case where all candidates have empty parts).
- After peek loop ends: if all candidates had empty parts AND finishReason is STOP (or null), returns `{valid: false, reason: "streaming empty content (gemini parts:[])"}`.

This is safe because `isKnownNonClaudeStreamPayload()` at line 124 already early-returns `true` for Gemini streams with actual content (text, functionCall, executableCode). The new code never runs for valid streams.

### 2. Cooldown in `runtimeUnits.ts` (+19 lines)

After `validateResponseQuality` returns invalid with the Gemini empty-content reason on an Antigravity unit:

- Calls `lockModel(provider, connectionId, modelStr, "quota_exhausted", 3_600_000)` — 1 hour cooldown.
- Logs warning with locked provider/model/connection info.

This prevents the combo from immediately reselecting the same exhausted Antigravity provider on subsequent requests. Follows the existing `quota_exhausted` pattern from `chatCore.ts:2988` and `accountFallback.ts:818`.

### 3. Tests (7 new, 204 lines)

| # | Test | Expected |
|---|------|----------|
| 1 | Single empty `parts:[]` + STOP event | `valid: false` |
| 2 | Multi-chunk empty `parts:[]` stream | `valid: false` |
| 3 | Valid Gemini text content | `valid: true` (no false positive) |
| 4 | Mixed: empty then content | `valid: true` (no false positive) |
| 5 | Non-Gemini SSE (OpenAI `choices` format) | `valid: true` (non-regression) |
| 6 | Non-streaming JSON Gemini payload | `valid: true` |
| 7 | Integration: `executeRuntimeUnitCombo` + `isModelLocked` | Lock applied after empty stream |

## Verification

- **7/7 new tests**: PASS
- **96/96 broader suite**: PASS (antigravity + validate-response-quality + combo-streaming + plan3-p0 + fixes-p1 + security-fase01)
- **Typecheck**: `tsc --pretty false -p tsconfig.typecheck-core.json` → exit 0
- **ESLint**: clean on all 3 changed files
- **Pre-existing failure**: `webdav-server-3485.test.ts` → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND scripts/dev/webdav-handler.mjs` (last existed v3.8.22, unrelated to this change)

## Files Changed

| File | Lines | Change |
|------|-------|--------|
| `open-sse/services/combo/runtimeUnits.ts` | +19 | lockModel cooldown on Antigravity empty-parts detection |
| `open-sse/services/combo/validateQuality.ts` | +45 | Gemini empty `parts:[]` detection in SSE peek |
| `tests/unit/antigravity-empty-content-detection.test.ts` | +204 | 7 tests: detection, false-positive guards, lockModel integration |

author: samflowsai-coder
body:
## Problema (perda silenciosa de decisão)

`poll_decisoes_once` (`app/integrations/flowpcp/poll_decisoes.py`) avançava o cursor para `proximo_cursor` ao fim de **todo** lote, **independente** de cada decisão ter sido confirmada.

O `/decisoes` do Flow (`pcp-app`) usa cursor watermark `atualizado_em >=` com dedup real `reconciliado_em IS NULL`, e **assume** que o Importador reprocessa a borda. Mas o Importador já passava o cursor pra frente. Consequência:

- Lote `[d1@14:00, d2@14:01, d3@14:02]`, UPDATE no Fire de `d2` dá timeout (não confirma) → cursor avança pra `14:02` → próximo poll pede `>= 14:02` → **d2 (14:01) nunca mais volta** e fica `reconciliado_em IS NULL` pra sempre. A data renegociada de d2 **some**.
- Efeito colateral: a lógica de "5 tentativas" do `pedido_nao_encontrado_no_fire` ficava **inalcançável** para qualquer decisão que não fosse a última do lote.

Mascarado em produção porque lotes de 1 decisão (comuns) auto-curam via `>=`. Morde com ≥2 decisões e uma não-última falhando. **Severidade alta, probabilidade média.**

## Correção

- `processar_decisao` retorna `bool` (True = confirmada/sai do feed; False = re-tentar no próximo poll).
- `poll_decisoes_once` só salva `proximo_cursor` se **todas** as decisões do lote confirmaram; senão mantém o cursor.
- Manter o cursor é seguro: re-buscar é idempotente e o dedup do Flow (`reconciliado_em IS NULL`) filtra as já confirmadas. Decisões novas continuam fluindo (sem head-of-line block); o `pedido_nao_encontrado` agora alcança as 5 tentativas.

## Testes

- `test_poll_nao_avanca_cursor_se_decisao_do_meio_falha` — reproduz o skip (RED→GREEN).
- `test_poll_avanca_cursor_quando_todas_confirmadas` — guarda contra over-correction.
- Suíte completa: **563/563** · ruff limpo.

## Contexto

Achado numa auditoria do fluxo de integração Importador↔FlowPCP (validação dos dois lados + revisão de design). Itens de hardening restantes (token per-tenant, outbox transacional, alerta em DEAD, cancelamento ERP→PCP) ficam fora deste PR — diff de uma intenção só.
